# Adventure

> Text adventures for walkers — a step-gated interactive fiction engine and
> authoring tool for Android.

**Status:** pre-alpha. Features, data formats, UI and public APIs may change
without notice. The repository is under active development.

Сейчас работа над приложением ведется по плану в файле docs/checklist-tracker.md

## What is this?

Adventure is an Android app for people who enjoy text adventures (such as
*Fighting Fantasy* and similar gamebooks) and walking — and for authors who
want to write text quests. Chapters are unlocked by real-world steps counted
by the phone's step sensor (or Health Connect), so reading progress is tied
to physical activity.

Two primary audiences:

- **Authors** — write, edit and preview interactive adventures inside the app.
- **Developers** — extend the app, add features, integrate new step sources.

End users of the app find everything they need in the in-app UI; this README
and `docs/` are for authors and developers.

## Features (current)

- Adventure editor: scenes, choices, conditional branching, tags
  (health / items / journal), chapter ends with step gates, death scenes,
  initial player state.
- Reader with HUD (health, inventory, journal), save/resume progress, death
  handling (step back / restart chapter / restart adventure).
- Step counter: foreground service using `TYPE_STEP_COUNTER` plus optional
  Health Connect source; 30-day history; monotonic all-time counter.
- Utilities: validator, search, story statistics, map view, JSON
  import/export via the Storage Access Framework.
- Adjustable font size and custom fonts, in-app debug log viewer.

See [ROADMAP.md](./ROADMAP.md) for what is planned.

## Quick start (developers)

Requirements:

- Android Studio (latest stable)
- JDK 21 (the project's Gradle toolchain)
- Android device or emulator with `minSdk 26`

Build and run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/andrey-ufo/Adventure.git
cd Adventure
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug
```

On first launch the app asks you to choose a folder (via the Storage Access
Framework). Adventure creates two sub-folders inside it:

- `Adventures/` — library of finished works
- `NewAdventures/` — drafts

and a few service files (`progress.json`, `step_history.json`,
`debug_log.txt`) at the root of the chosen folder.

## Documentation

Full documentation lives in [`docs/`](./docs/index.md). Start there.

- **For authors** — [Authoring guide](./docs/authoring-guide.md)
- **For developers** — [Getting started](./docs/getting-started.md),
  [Architecture overview](./docs/architecture.md)
- **Documentation rules** — [docs/documentation-rules.md](./docs/documentation-rules.md)

## Project structure (high level)

- `app/src/main/java/com/myapp/adventure/` — application code
  - `data/` — domain models (Adventure, Scene, Choice, Tag, …) and editor models
  - `service/` — `StepCounterService` (foreground sensor service)
  - `step/` — step source abstraction, Health Connect integration
  - `ui/` — fragments, adapters, editor, reader
  - `utils/` — persistence (`ProgressManager`, `StepHistoryManager`,
    `Logger`), helpers
- `app/src/main/res/` — layouts, drawables, strings, themes
- `app/src/main/res/raw/test_adventure.json` — sample adventure used for testing
- `docs/` — documentation

## Architecture invariants

The step pipeline has three layers, from lowest to highest:

1. **Source** — `StepCounterService` (sensor) or optional
   `HealthConnectStepSource`. Emits step *deltas*; never touches game state
   or `progress.json`.
2. **History** — `StepHistoryManager`, the single owner of step history
   (30 daily buckets + monotonic `totalStepsAllTime`; in-memory cache,
   batched disk writes, `Mutex`-protected).
3. **Game** — `AdventureReaderFragment` reads only aggregates from
   `StepHistoryManager` and owns chapter-gate state (`remainingSteps`,
   `isGateActive`).

Future features (achievements, step-gated choices, adventure unlocks, ranks)
build on `StepHistoryManager`'s read APIs and must not open `progress.json`
or `step_history.json` directly. Full details will be documented in
[docs/architecture.md](./docs/architecture.md).

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a Pull Request.

Project conventions:

- **Source-code comments are in English.** All Russian comments in the code
  must be translated to English.
- `test_adventure.json` is the reference sample adventure. It must be
  updated whenever the app gains new features, so it always exercises the
  current feature set.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

# Contributing to Adventure

Thanks for your interest in Adventure. The project is **pre-alpha**: features,
data formats, UI and public APIs may change without notice. Contributions are
welcome — see below for how to build the app, report issues, and open pull
requests.

By contributing you agree that your changes are licensed under the project's
[MIT License](./LICENSE).

## Ways to contribute

- **Report a bug** — open an issue using the bug report template.
- **Suggest a feature** — open an issue using the feature request template.
- **Improve the docs** — fixes and additions to `docs/` are welcome; follow
  [`docs/documentation-rules.md`](./docs/documentation-rules.md).
- **Send a pull request** — code, tests, or docs.

Please search existing issues and pull requests before opening a new one.

## Build and run

Requirements:

- Android Studio (latest stable)
- JDK 21 (the project's Gradle toolchain)
- Android device or emulator with `minSdk 26`

From a terminal:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/andrey-ufo/Adventure.git
cd Adventure
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug
```

On first launch the app asks you to choose a folder (via the Storage Access
Framework). The app creates `Adventures/` and `NewAdventures/` inside it, plus
`progress.json`, `step_history.json` and `debug_log.txt`.

## Report a bug

Use the **Bug report** issue template. Include:

- App version (`versionName`) and commit hash, if known.
- Android version and device/emulator model.
- Exact steps to reproduce, in numbered order.
- Expected behaviour vs. actual behaviour.
- Relevant lines from `debug_log.txt` (see below) and, if the bug is visible,
  a screenshot.

### Collecting the debug log

Enable logging in the app (Settings → «Включить запись лога в файл» / "Enable
file logging"), reproduce the bug, then use the in-app log viewer (Menu →
«Логи игры» / "Game logs") to copy the log or open `debug_log.txt` from the
chosen folder. Trim long logs — keep only the relevant window.

## Suggest a feature

Use the **Feature request** issue template. Focus on the user or author
problem you want to solve, not on the implementation. Link to related issues
or roadmap items if relevant.

## Pull requests

Before opening a pull request:

1. Read [`docs/documentation-rules.md`](./docs/documentation-rules.md) if you
   change anything under `docs/`.
2. Make sure the project builds: `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`.
3. Keep changes focused. One logical change per pull request is easier to
   review and revert than a mixed batch.
4. Describe *what* changed and *why* in the PR description. Use the pull
   request template as a checklist.
5. Update documentation when the behaviour you changed is described in
   `docs/` or in `README.md`.

### Project conventions

- **Source-code comments are in English.** All Russian comments in the code
  must be translated to English.
- **Docs are in English.** See
  [`docs/documentation-rules.md`](./docs/documentation-rules.md) for file
  structure, status markers and link rules.
- **`test_adventure.json` is the reference sample adventure.** It must be
  updated whenever the app gains new features, so it always exercises the
  current feature set.
- **Domain terminology** — use the spellings in
  [`docs/glossary.md`](./docs/glossary.md). When adding a new term, add it to
  the glossary in the same change.
- **Progress log entries are in English.** From Ф2.8 onward. Rationale:
    (a) the project is MIT and its contributors are English-speaking;
    (b) `documentation-rules.md §1` already requires English docs;
    (c) dense Cyrillic content breaks automated digest tools (`gitingest`)
    and GitHub search. See `docs/progress/progress-log.md` for the format.

### Commit messages

Short imperative subject line (e.g. "Fix reader crash on empty chapter"), then
a blank line, then an optional body explaining *why*. No strict format — this
project is too early for conventional commits.

## Code of conduct

Be kind. Assume good faith. This is a small pre-alpha project; the focus is on
making the app better, not on winning arguments.

## Questions

If something is unclear, open a discussion or an issue. There is no private
channel for contributor questions.

# Roadmap

**Status:** evolving. This is a one-page planning document, not a promise.
Priorities may change as the project evolves.

Known issues live in the repository's [issue tracker](https://github.com/andrey-ufo/Adventure/issues).
This file only describes direction; it does not track every task.

## Current focus

The project is **pre-alpha**. The current focus is:

- Stabilising the editor and reader UX so that authors can build and play
  adventures end-to-end without surprises.
- Stabilising the step pipeline (sensor and Health Connect) so that step
  gates behave predictably across reboots and app restarts.
- Keeping the documentation foundation honest and up to date
  (see [`docs/documentation-rules.md`](./docs/documentation-rules.md)).

## Next

Planned next, once the current focus is stable enough:

- **Step-gated choices** — per-choice `remainingSteps`, the same mechanism as
  chapter gates.
- **Achievements** — a `StepAchievementEngine` that reads from
  `StepHistoryManager` (e.g. "≥50 000 steps in the last 7 days → +10 stamina").
- **Adventure unlocks** — compare `StepHistoryManager.getTotalSteps()` against
  per-adventure thresholds.
- **Ranks** — a pure function of `getTotalSteps()`; the statistics screen
  already shows a rank progress bar as a template.

These build on the read APIs of `StepHistoryManager` and must not open
`progress.json` or `step_history.json` directly.

## Later

Desirable, but dependent on earlier work:

- **JSON adventure format specification** — a formal spec for the adventure
  file format, written only once the format stabilises.
- **Deep architecture docs** — sequence diagrams and per-class notes, written
  once the feature set stabilises.
- **English UI locale** — the Russian → English mapping is being prepared in
  [`docs/glossary.md`](./docs/glossary.md); the actual Android resources
  (`values-en/`) will follow.
- **Screenshots and tutorials** for the authoring guide — deliberately
  deferred until the UI stabilises.

## Post-Ф10

Everything after the checklist 2.1 is accepted lives in
[`docs/roadmap.md`](./docs/roadmap.md). It covers three groups:

- **Gamebook mechanics** (Ф12–Ф18) — support for more formats and
  mechanics from gamebooks beyond the current feature set: RNG, combat,
  character initialization, external outcomes (physical dexterity,
  puzzles), cross-adventure state, meta-mechanics, authoring UI for all
  of the above. Each mechanic's current status is in
  [`docs/gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md`](./docs/gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md).
- **Nice-to-have** — the 17 explicit Nice items + 10 `.advanced`
  extensions from the checklist, each with an entry trigger.
- **Distribution / community** — Play Store, F-Droid, Steam (conditional
  on a JS runtime), community docs.

No dates. No promises. Every item there is triggered by a concrete
question, not by a calendar. This one-page `ROADMAP.md` stays the
high-level summary; `docs/roadmap.md` is the full plan.

## Not planned (for now)

Explicitly out of scope at this stage:

- Public release to app stores.
- Backend services or cloud sync of adventures or progress.
- Migration of the docs to MkDocs / Docusaurus / any static-site generator.
- A `CHANGELOG.md` — there are no releases yet.
- A `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — the project is too small for a formal policy;
  common-sense kindness is expected (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

If you think something belongs on this list, open an issue.

            }
        }
    }
    compileOptions {
        sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_11
        targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_11
    }
    buildFeatures {
        viewBinding = true
        compose = true
    }

    lint {
        baseline = file("lint-baseline.xml")
        abortOnError = true
        checkReleaseBuilds = false
        // Явно указываем конфиг, чтобы AGP не искал его эвристически.
        lintConfig = file("lint.xml")
        // Именно disable исключает детектор из запуска;
        // severity="ignore" в lint.xml только подавляет отчёт после выполнения.
        // 2026-11-10: TEMPORARY WORKAROUND — remove when fixed upstream.
        //
        // UnsafeFragmentLifecycleObserverDetector (androidx.fragment:fragment-ktx
        // 1.9.1) infinite-recurses through viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope
        // .launch { ... } lambdas: RecursiveMethodVisitor.visitCallExpression
        // :183 <-> :187 loops with no depth limit, pinning one WorkerExecutor
        // thread at 98% CPU and making lintAnalyzeDebug hang for 10+ minutes.
        //
        // The upstream fix exists in AndroidX main but is not in any stable
        // release yet. Relevant commits:
        //   - caa8296 "Avoid duplicate reports in UnsafeFragmentLifecycleObserverDetector"
        //   - 1ff2f34 "Limit the call depth to search"
        //   - (unnamed) "Short-circuit Compose boundaries"
        //
        // ACTION WHEN UPDATING fragment-ktx: once fragment 1.10.0+ (or a
        // 1.9.x point release that mentions these commits in its release
        // notes) is available, bump the version and DELETE the four
        // `disable +=` lines below and the matching entries in
        // app/lint.xml. Verify by running `./gradlew :app:lintDebug
        // --rerun-tasks` — it should finish in well under a minute.
        disable += "FragmentAddMenuProvider"
        disable += "FragmentBackPressedCallback"
        disable += "FragmentLiveDataObserve"
        disable += "UnsafeRepeatOnLifecycleDetector"
        htmlReport = true
        xmlReport = true
        textReport = true
    }
}

FILE: app/src/main/java/com/myapp/adventure/MainActivity.kt

package com.myapp.adventure

import android.os.Bundle
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import com.myapp.adventure.ui.setup.SetupFragment
import com.myapp.adventure.utils.Logger
import com.myapp.adventure.utils.ThemeManager
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking

class MainActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        // Theme bootstrap must happen BEFORE super.onCreate(): AppCompat reads
        // the night mode and theme during its own onCreate, and changing them
        // afterwards causes a flash or a spurious recreate().
        ThemeManager.initialize(this)
        runBlocking { ThemeManager.awaitInitialized() }
        ThemeManager.apply(this)

        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_main)

        val prefs = getSharedPreferences("adventure_prefs", MODE_PRIVATE)
        val savedUri = prefs.getString("adventure_folder_uri", null)
        if (savedUri != null) {
            Logger.init(this, savedUri)
        }

        com.myapp.adventure.step.StepSourceManager.start(this)

        if (savedInstanceState == null) {
            supportFragmentManager.beginTransaction()
                .replace(R.id.fragment_container, SetupFragment())
                .commit()
        }
    }
}

FILE: app/src/main/java/com/myapp/adventure/data/Adventure.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.data

import com.google.gson.annotations.SerializedName

data class Adventure(
    /**
     * b2: adventure-format schema version, written as `"version": 5`.
     * `null` on files that predate v3 (no `version` field) — Gson
     * omits it, and `JsonToIr.parse` treats it as v1 (identity
     * migration). The editor writes `5` from `buildAdventure()`
     * because it emits v5-shaped JSON (`scene.gate`,
     * `gate_repeatable`, `is_ending`, `start_scene`).
     */
    @SerializedName("version")
    val version: Int? = null,
    val title: String,
    /**
     * Ф4-infra (3b-6h): empty default. The old RU default
     * `"Неизвестен"` propagated into the JSON file on save for
     * legacy adventures without `author`, and then into the library
     * list. An empty string is honest (no author set); the library
     * shows a blank author line, same as an adventure with
     * `"author": ""`.
     */
    val author: String = "",
    val description: String = "",
    @SerializedName("initial_state")
    val initialState: PlayerState? = null,
    /**
     * Ф2.7: объявления переменных (`{"health": {"type": "int_range",
     * "min": 0, "max": 100}}`). Nullable, чтобы Gson **опускал** поле
     * в JSON, если автор не объявил ни одной переменной — не мусорить
     * `"variables": {}` в каждом файле.
     *
     * **Формат (A1 из Ф2.7):** map `name → {type, min?, max?}`.
     * `type` — строка (`"bool"`, `"int"`, `"int_min"`, `"int_range"`,
     * `"item_count"`, `"item_list"`), совпадает с `@SerialName` в
     * `:engine/ir/types/VarType`. `min`/`max` — только для `int_min`
     * (только `min`) и `int_range` (оба), `null` для остальных.
     *
     * **Парсинг на :engine-стороне** — Ф2.8 (`JsonToIr` → `AdventureDto`
     * → `VarDecl`). Сейчас `:engine` видит `variables: emptyMap()` и
     * работает в fallback-режиме `TypeChecker` (см. Ф2.2/C4).
     */
    @SerializedName("variables")
    val variables: Map<String, VariableDto>? = null,
    /**
     * Ф4.3.1: reusable choice templates. `null` (field absent) means
     * Gson does not write `"choice_templates": []` into files that have
     * no templates — same "empty → omit" policy as `variables` / `tags`.
     */
    @SerializedName("choice_templates")
    val choiceTemplates: List<ChoiceTemplateDto>? = null,
    val tags: List<TagDefinition>? = null,
    @SerializedName("death_scene")
    val deathScene: DeathScene? = null,
    /**
     * b2: explicit start scene id (`"start_scene"`). Required from
     * v3; `JsonToIr.parse` rejects v5 files without it. The editor
     * writes it from `buildAdventure()` (first scene of the first
     * chapter, or the first scene overall — the editor has no
     * explicit "start" affordance yet).
     */
    @SerializedName("start_scene")
    val startScene: String? = null,
    val chapters: List<Chapter>? = null
)

data class DeathScene(
    val id: String = "death_scene",
    /**
     * Ф4-infra (3b-6h): empty default. Reader falls back to
     * `R.string.reader_default_death_text`; see
     * `:engine/ir/DeathScene.text` KDoc.
     */
    val text: String = "",
    @SerializedName("allow_step_back")
    val allowStepBack: Boolean = true,
    @SerializedName("allow_chapter_restart")
    val allowChapterRestart: Boolean = true,
    @SerializedName("allow_adventure_restart")
    val allowAdventureRestart: Boolean = true
)

data class Chapter(
    val id: String,
    val title: String = "",
    /**
     * **Legacy (v1) chapter-level gate.** In v1 files this field was
     * `"required_steps": N` and meant "walk N steps to enter this
     * chapter"; `JsonToIr.parse` migrates it to `Gate(N)` on the last
     * scene of the previous chapter. Since b2 the editor emits
     * per-scene `gate` instead and never writes `required_steps`.
     *
     * **Nullable**, not `Int = 0`: Gson omits `null` fields on
     * serialization, so a freshly-written v5 file does not carry
     * `"required_steps": 0` on every chapter. Old v1 files still
     * load correctly — `loadFromUri` reads `requiredSteps ?: 0` for
     * the v1 → v5 migration.
     */
    @SerializedName("required_steps")
    val requiredSteps: Int? = null,
    val scenes: List<Scene>? = null
)

data class Scene(
    val id: String,
    val text: String,
    @SerializedName("set_flags")
    val setFlags: List<String>? = null,
    @SerializedName("remove_flags")
    val removeFlags: List<String>? = null,
    @SerializedName("modify_stats")
    val modifyStats: Map<String, Int>? = null,
    val choices: List<Choice>? = null,
    /**
     * Ф1.7.5: `"is_ending"` from the adventure JSON. `null` on files
     * that predate v4 (or on `:app/data/Adventure` produced by code
     * that does not yet write the field — sections 2–3 add that).
     *
     * **Nullable, not `Boolean = false`.** Gson does not honour
     * Kotlin defaults; a non-nullable `Boolean` would silently be
     * `false` for old files, indistinguishable from "explicitly not
     * an ending". `null` keeps the "field absent" semantics clear.
     * Existing call sites read it as `scene.isEnding ?: false`.
     */
    @SerializedName("is_ending")
    val isEnding: Boolean? = null,
    /**
     * b2: per-scene step gate (`"gate": N`). `null` = no gate. The
     * editor writes it from `EditorScene.gateRequiredSteps > 0`;
     * `JsonToIr.parse` reads it as `Gate(requiredSteps = N,
     * repeatable = …)` in the IR.
     *
     * **Distinct from `Chapter.required_steps`** (legacy v1): a
     * chapter-level gate is migrated to `Gate(N)` on the *last scene
     * of the previous chapter* by `JsonToIr.parse`. The editor no
     * longer emits chapter-level gates — only per-scene ones.
     */
    @SerializedName("gate")
    val gate: Int? = null,
    /**
     * b2: whether the gate re-engages on every visit
     * (`"gate_repeatable": true`). Only meaningful when [gate] is
     * non-null. `null` = "absent" → `JsonToIr` defaults to `false`
     * ("once passed, stays passed in this playthrough"). Emitted by
     * the editor only when the author ticks "повторять" AND a gate
     * is set — omitting the field when `false` keeps the JSON clean
     * (matches the `is_ending` pattern).
     */
    @SerializedName("gate_repeatable")
    val gateRepeatable: Boolean? = null,
    /**
     * Ф4.5 (N5): `"merge": true` — this scene is a merge point. Nullable,
     * `null` means "field absent" (identity migration — merge = false).
     * Written by `buildAdventure` from `EditorScene.isMerge` (currently
     * only reachable via hand-edited JSON; the editor UI for merge
     * lands in Ф4.10).
     */
    @SerializedName("merge")
    val merge: Boolean? = null,
    /**
     * Ф4.5 (N5): `"merge_sources": ["s1", "s2"]` — declared incoming
     * branches. `null`/empty = no sources declared (the analyzer in Ф4.6
     * will collect them from the `nextScene` graph). Written by
     * `buildAdventure` from `EditorScene.mergeSources` (empty → `null`,
     * Gson omits the field).
     */
    @SerializedName("merge_sources")
    val mergeSources: List<String>? = null,
)

data class Choice(
    val text: String,
    @SerializedName("next_scene")
    val nextScene: String,
    val condition: String? = null,
    /**
     * Ф4.3.2b: "show this choice?" condition (distinct from
     * [condition] which is "enable this choice?"). Populated from a
     * template's `visibilityCondition` when the choice is expanded via
     * `applyTemplate`. Persisted to JSON as `"visibility_condition"`.
     *
     * **`:engine` ignores this field today.** `JsonToIr`'s
     * `ChoiceDto` has no `visibility_condition`, and
     * `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }` silently drops it. The
     * runtime gates only on [condition]. When Ф4.4 / N4 adds the
     * visibility behaviour to the reader, a matching
     * `visibility_condition` field lands in `engine/format/dto/ChoiceDto`
     * and `:engine/ir/Choice.visibilityCondition` (already exists —
     * added in Ф4.2.1) is populated by the parser.
     */
    @SerializedName("visibility_condition")
    val visibilityCondition: String? = null,
    @SerializedName("set_flags")
    val setFlags: List<String>? = null,
    @SerializedName("remove_flags")
    val removeFlags: List<String>? = null,
    @SerializedName("modify_stats")
    val modifyStats: Map<String, Int>? = null,
    /**
     * Ф4.3.2b: if this choice was expanded from a template, the source
     * reference (template id + args). `null` for hand-written choices.
     *
     * **JSON shape:** `"template_ref": { "template_id": "...", "args": {
     * ... } }`. Written by the editor's `buildAdventure()`; read back by
     * `loadFromUri` so the reference survives a save / load round-trip.
     *
     * **Runtime sees only the expanded fields** (`text`, `condition`,
     * `setFlags`, `removeFlags`, `modifyStats`, `nextScene`). `:engine`'s
     * `JsonToIr` does not parse `template_ref` (its `ChoiceDto` has no
     * field for it, and `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }` silently
     * drops it) — this is intentional: the runtime does not need the
     * reference, only the expanded content. When / if `:engine` needs
     * the reference (e.g. for a future "un-expand" tool), a matching
     * `template_ref` field lands in `engine/format/dto/ChoiceDto` and
     * `Choice.templateRef` (IR) is populated by the parser.
     */
    @SerializedName("template_ref")
    val templateRef: TemplateRefDto? = null,
)

/**
 * Ф4.3.2b: JSON shape of a `template_ref` on a `Choice`.
 *
 * **Same wire shape as `:engine/ir/TemplateRef`:** `template_id` (the
 * id of the source `ChoiceTemplate`) + `args` (parameter name → actual
 * variable name). The two classes are deliberately separate — `:app` uses
 * Gson, `:engine` uses kotlinx.serialization — and live in different
 * modules (see `docs/architecture.md` invariant I1). Keeping the **wire**
 * shape identical (hand-maintained) is what makes the editor ↔ reader
 * round-trip lossless: `:app` writes `template_id` / `args`, `:engine`
 * (in future) reads the same keys.
 *
 * **Why `template_id`, not `id` or `templateId`.** Matches the IR
 * `TemplateRef` `@SerialName` and the choice-template adventure-file
 * convention (`choice_templates[].id` is the referenced id; the reference
 * itself uses `template_id` for unambiguity, mirroring
 * `"death_scene": { "id": ... }`).
 */
data class TemplateRefDto(
    @SerializedName("template_id")
    val templateId: String,
    val args: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
)

data class PlayerState(
    val flags: List<String>? = null,
    val stats: Map<String, Int>? = null
)

/**
 * Ф2.7 — DTO переменной для Gson-save.
 *
 * `type` — одна из строк `@SerialName` в
 * `com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType`:
 * `"bool"`, `"int"`, `"int_min"`, `"int_range"`, `"item_count"`,
 * `"item_list"`. `min`/`max` — только для `int_min` / `int_range`,
 * `null` для остальных (Gson опускает `null`-поля при
 * `setPrettyPrinting()` только если настроено `serializeNulls = false`,
 * что по умолчанию true — то есть `null` **пишутся** как `"min": null`.
 * Для чистоты JSON в `saveAdventure()` лучше собирать `VariableDto`
 * через `when` с явным отбрасыванием `min`/`max` для Bool/ItemCount/…
 * — либо настроить `GsonBuilder().serializeNulls(false)`, но это
 * затронет все поля `Adventure`. Оставлено как есть: `"min": null`
 * в JSON валидно и не мешает парсингу Ф2.8).
 */
data class VariableDto(
    val type: String,
    val min: Int? = null,
    val max: Int? = null,
)


/**
 * Ф4.3.1 — choice-template DTO for Gson-save.
 *
 * Mirrors `engine/.../format/dto/ChoiceTemplateDto`, but lives in
 * `:app/data` — the editor's write-side model. Conditions are strings
 * (as in JSON); effects are three parallel fields (as in `Scene` /
 * `Choice`).
 *
 * Parameters are `List<VarDeclDto>`, not `Map`: the parameter name is
 * a value (not a key), and order matters for the UI.
 */
data class ChoiceTemplateDto(
    val id: String,
    val parameters: List<VarDeclDto>? = null,
    val text: String,
    @SerializedName("visibility_condition")
    val visibilityCondition: String? = null,
    @SerializedName("availability_condition")
    val availabilityCondition: String? = null,
    @SerializedName("set_flags")
    val setFlags: List<String>? = null,
    @SerializedName("remove_flags")
    val removeFlags: List<String>? = null,
    @SerializedName("modify_stats")
    val modifyStats: Map<String, Int>? = null,
    @SerializedName("next_scene")
    val nextScene: String,
)

/**
 * Ф4.3.1 — DTO for one typed template parameter.
 *
 * Differs from `VariableDto` (`type`, `min`, `max`) by carrying `name`:
 * in `Adventure.variables` the name is a map key; in
 * `ChoiceTemplate.parameters` it is an object field.
 */
data class VarDeclDto(
    val name: String,
    val type: String,
    val min: Int? = null,
    val max: Int? = null,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.data

import androidx.annotation.StringRes
import com.myapp.adventure.R
import java.util.UUID

data class EditorScene(
    val uid: String = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
    var id: String = "",
    var idIsAuto: Boolean = true,
    var title: String = "",
    var text: String = "",
    /**
     * Narrative chapter boundary. The reader does not use this field
     * for gates (Ф1.5.4 — chapters are pure narrative grouping); it
     * is used by the editor's map / stats / validator to group scenes
     * into chapters and to show the "🏁 Конец главы" badge.
     *
     * **Replaces the old "конец главы + requiredSteps" pair.** Before
     * b2, `isChapterEnd` also wrote `chapter.required_steps = N` on
     * the *next* chapter — that was the legacy v1 gate, migrated by
     * `JsonToIr` to `Gate(N)` on this scene. From b2, the gate is a
     * **separate** per-scene concept ([gateRequiredSteps] /
     * [gateRepeatable]), so an author can express four combinations:
     * chapter end without a gate, gate without a chapter end, both,
     * neither. The old behaviour (chapter end implicitly means a
     * gate) is preserved on load via `loadFromUri`'s v1 migration,
     * but is no longer how the UI models things.
     */
    var isChapterEnd: Boolean = false,
    /**
     * b2: per-scene step gate, `0` = no gate. Written as
     * `"gate": N` on the scene. Distinct from [isChapterEnd]
     * (narrative boundary) and [isEnding] (adventure ending).
     * Mutually compatible with both: a scene can be the last of a
     * chapter, an ending, and have a gate, independently.
     */
    var gateRequiredSteps: Int = 0,
    /**
     * b2: whether the gate re-engages on every visit
     * (`"gate_repeatable": true`). Only meaningful when
     * [gateRequiredSteps] > 0. Default `false` ("once passed, stays
     * passed in this playthrough") matches `Gate.repeatable`
     * default in `:engine/ir/Gate.kt` and the "least surprising"
     * policy confirmed 2026-11-07.
     */
    var gateRepeatable: Boolean = false,
    var isDeathScene: Boolean = false,
    var deathAllowStepBack: Boolean = true,
    var deathAllowChapterRestart: Boolean = true,
    var deathAllowAdventureRestart: Boolean = true,
    var isEnding: Boolean = false,
    /**
     * Ф4.5 (N5): the author marked this scene as a merge point. Round-
     * trips with `:app/data/Scene.merge` (save/load). **No editor UI in
     * 4.5** — the checkbox is Ф4.10; the field exists so that a scene
     * with `"merge": true` in JSON survives open→save.
     */
    var isMerge: Boolean = false,
    /**
     * Ф4.5 (N5): declared incoming branches. Round-trips with
     * `:app/data/Scene.mergeSources`. Empty → `null` in JSON (Gson
     * omits). Same UI deferral as [isMerge].
     */
    var mergeSources: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val tags: MutableList<EditorTag> = mutableListOf(),
    val choices: MutableList<EditorChoice> = mutableListOf()
)

data class EditorChoice(
    val uid: String = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
    var text: String = "",
    var nextSceneId: String = "",
    var conditionTag: String = "",
    /**
     * Ф4.3.2b: "show this choice?" condition — distinct from
     * [conditionTag], which is "enable this choice?". Populated by
     * `AdventureEditorViewModel.applyTemplateToChoice()` from a
     * template's `visibilityCondition`; persisted to JSON as
     * `choices[].visibility_condition`. The reader (Ф4.4 / N4) will use
     * it to distinguish hidden vs disabled; today it is stored but
     * dormant (reader gates only on [conditionTag] via IR `condition`).
     */
    var visibilityConditionTag: String = "",
    val tags: MutableList<EditorTag> = mutableListOf(),
    /**
     * Ф4.3.2b: if this choice was expanded from a `ChoiceTemplate`, the
     * template's id. `null` for hand-written choices. Editor-only
     * metadata — the runtime sees only the expanded [text] /
     * [conditionTag] / [visibilityConditionTag] / [tags] /
     * [nextSceneId]. Used by the "update all uses" flow (Ф4.3.3).
     */
    var templateUid: String? = null,
    /**
     * Ф4.3.2b: arguments used when this choice was expanded. Empty map
     * for hand-written choices. Persisted to JSON as
     * `template_ref.args` so Ф4.3.3 can re-apply with the same args.
     */
    var templateArgs: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
)

data class EditorTag(
    var name: String = "",
    var value: Int = 0,
    var isStatModifier: Boolean = false,
    var category: TagCategory = TagCategory.JOURNAL,
    var displayName: String = "",
    var visible: Boolean = false
)

fun EditorScene.deepCopy(): EditorScene = copy(
    // Ф4.5: freeze `mergeSources` so undo/redo snapshots cannot alias
    // the live editor state (same principle as `templateArgs`).
    mergeSources = mergeSources.toList(),
    tags = tags.map { it.copy() }.toMutableList(),
    choices = choices.map { choice ->
        choice.copy(
            tags = choice.tags.map { it.copy() }.toMutableList(),
            // Ф4.3.2b: `templateArgs` is `Map` (immutable interface), but
            // the caller could have passed a `MutableMap`. `toMap()`
            // freezes it so that undo/redo snapshots cannot alias the
            // live editor state.
            templateArgs = choice.templateArgs.toMap(),
        )
    }.toMutableList()
)

data class RebuildResult(
    val oldId: String,
    val newId: String,
    val updatedReferences: Int
)

/**
 * Ф2.7 — UI-форма объявления переменной.
 *
 * Не переиспользует `:engine/ir/types/VarType` напрямую, потому что
 * UI нужна «промежуточная» форма: автор печатает `0` в `min` и ещё
 * не ввёл `max`. `VarType.IntRange(min, max)` требует оба значения
 * сразу — промежуточного состояния нет. Поэтому `kind + min? + max?`
 * (см. [toVarType] для конверсии в IR, permissive-fallback при
 * недозаполненных полях).
 *
 * @property name имя переменной (совпадает с ключом в `variables`).
 * @property kind тип из ограниченного набора (см. [VarKind]).
 * @property min нижняя граница, `null` если не применимо / не введена.
 * @property max верхняя граница, `null` если не применимо / не введена.
 */
data class EditorVarDecl(
    var name: String = "",
    var kind: VarKind = VarKind.BOOL,
    var min: Int? = null,
    var max: Int? = null,
)

/**
 * Ф2.7 — тип переменной в UI-редакторе.
 *
 * 1:1 с `VarType` из `:engine` (Bool / Integer / IntMin / IntRange /
 * ItemCount / ItemList). Отдельный enum нужен, чтобы `Spinner` показывал
 * человекочитаемые лейблы и чтобы UI не тянул IR-классы.
 */
enum class VarKind(@StringRes val displayNameRes: Int) {
    BOOL(R.string.var_kind_bool),
    INTEGER(R.string.var_kind_integer),
    INT_MIN(R.string.var_kind_int_min),
    INT_RANGE(R.string.var_kind_int_range),
    ITEM_COUNT(R.string.var_kind_item_count),
    ITEM_LIST(R.string.var_kind_item_list);

    /** Whether `min`/`max` are shown in the UI for this type. */
    val needsMin: Boolean
        get() = this == INT_MIN || this == INT_RANGE
    val needsMax: Boolean
        get() = this == INT_RANGE
}

/**
 * Конверсия UI-модели в IR-тип.
 *
 * **Permissive default.** Если `IntMin`/`IntRange` выбраны, но
 * `min`/`max` не заполнены — возвращает `Integer` (самый широкий
 * числовой тип). Смысл: одна недозаполненная декларация не должна
 * каскадить `UnknownVariable` на все ссылки на переменную через
 * fallback-таблицу. Вместо этого автор получит **Warning** от
 * `StoryValidator` («min/max не заполнены — тип понижен до Integer»)
 * и сможет исправить.
 *
 * @return `VarType` или `null`, если имя пустое (объявление не
 *   используется, не попадает в IR).
 */
fun EditorVarDecl.toVarType(): com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType? {
    if (name.isBlank()) return null

    /**
     * Ф4.3.1 — choice template in the editor.
     *
     * Mirrors `:engine/ir/ChoiceTemplate`, but uses the editor's vocabulary:
     * conditions are raw strings (like `EditorChoice.conditionTag`), effects
     * are `EditorTag` (like `EditorScene.tags` / `EditorChoice.tags`).
     * Parameters are `EditorVarDecl` (reused from `VariablesAdapter`;
     * supports the intermediate state "min entered, max not yet").
     *
     * `uid` is the editor's stable id (survives rename), same role as
     * `EditorScene.uid` / `EditorChoice.uid`. `id` is the `ChoiceTemplate.id`
     * from the IR (used as `templateRef.templateId` when `applyTemplate`
     * runs). May be empty on creation — the author fills it in;
     * `buildAdventure` skips templates with empty `id` on save (validation
     * warns separately).
     */
    data class EditorTemplate(
        val uid: String = java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
        var id: String = "",
        var text: String = "",
        var visibilityCondition: String = "",
        var availabilityCondition: String = "",
        val parameters: MutableList<EditorVarDecl> = mutableListOf(),
        val effects: MutableList<EditorTag> = mutableListOf(),
        var nextSceneId: String = "",
    )

    fun EditorTemplate.deepCopy(): EditorTemplate = copy(
        parameters = parameters.map { it.copy() }.toMutableList(),
        effects = effects.map { it.copy() }.toMutableList(),
    )

    val minLocal = min
    val maxLocal = max
    return when (kind) {
        VarKind.BOOL -> com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType.Bool
        VarKind.INTEGER -> com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType.Integer
        VarKind.INT_MIN -> minLocal?.let {
            com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType.IntMin(it)
        } ?: com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType.Integer
        VarKind.INT_RANGE -> if (minLocal != null && maxLocal != null) {
            com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType.IntRange(minLocal, maxLocal)
        } else {
            com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType.Integer
        }
        VarKind.ITEM_COUNT -> com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType.ItemCount
        VarKind.ITEM_LIST -> com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType.ItemList
    }
}

/**
 * Ф4.3.1 — choice template in the editor.
 *
 * Mirrors `:engine/ir/ChoiceTemplate`, but uses the editor's vocabulary:
 * conditions are raw strings (like `EditorChoice.conditionTag`), effects
 * are `EditorTag` (like `EditorScene.tags` / `EditorChoice.tags`).
 * Parameters are `EditorVarDecl` (reused from `VariablesAdapter`;
 * supports the intermediate state "min entered, max not yet").
 *
 * `uid` is the editor's stable id (survives rename), same role as
 * `EditorScene.uid` / `EditorChoice.uid`. `id` is the `ChoiceTemplate.id`
 * from the IR (used as `templateRef.templateId` when `applyTemplate`
 * runs). May be empty on creation — the author fills it in;
 * `buildAdventure` skips templates with empty `id` on save (validation
 * warns separately).
 */
data class EditorTemplate(
    val uid: String = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
    var id: String = "",
    var text: String = "",
    var visibilityCondition: String = "",
    var availabilityCondition: String = "",
    val parameters: MutableList<EditorVarDecl> = mutableListOf(),
    val effects: MutableList<EditorTag> = mutableListOf(),
    var nextSceneId: String = "",
)

fun EditorTemplate.deepCopy(): EditorTemplate = copy(
    parameters = parameters.map { it.copy() }.toMutableList(),
    effects = effects.map { it.copy() }.toMutableList(),
)

package com.myapp.adventure.data

/** Visual state of the "💾 Save" indicator in the editor toolbar. */
enum class SaveStatus {
    /** Nothing pending to save — the adventure was just opened / loaded. */
    SAVED,
    /** Editing: debounce timer is running, changes not yet persisted. */
    EDITING,
    /** Snapshot taken, file write in progress. */
    SAVING,
    /** Loaded from a file just now. */
    LOADED,
    /** Saved to disk just now. */
    SAVED_TO_FILE,
}

/**
 * Immutable snapshot of the editor state, exposed as `StateFlow` from
 * [com.myapp.adventure.ui.editor.AdventureEditorViewModel].
 *
 * **Why this exists.** `AdventureEditorViewModel` still exposes mutable
 * `MutableList`s (`scenes`, `variables`, `templates`, …) because the
 * existing View consumers (`EditorSceneAdapter`, `InitialStateAdapter`,
 * `VariablesAdapter`, `TemplateListAdapter`) mutate them in place and then
 * call `notifyDataSetChanged()`. Compose uses `equals()` to skip
 * recomposition; a mutation like `scene.title = "x"` keeps the same object
 * identity and never triggers an emit.
 *
 * [EditorUiState] fixes this for Compose consumers: each `commitState()`
 * takes a deep copy of every list, so each emit carries structurally
 * different objects and Compose recomposes. The View consumers are
 * unaffected — `uiState` runs in parallel with the mutable lists.
 *
 * **Migration path (Phase 3.1).** This is step 3.1b (after 3.1a). Later
 * steps move View consumers to Compose one by one (3.1c–3.1e). When the
 * last consumer is Compose-native (3.1f), the mutable lists can be
 * removed from the ViewModel; `commitState()` then becomes the only
 * entry point for state changes and the deep copies disappear.
 */
data class EditorUiState(
    val title: String = "",
    val author: String = "",
    val description: String = "",
    val variables: List<EditorVarDecl> = emptyList(),
    val templates: List<EditorTemplate> = emptyList(),
    val initialStateTags: List<EditorTag> = emptyList(),
    val scenes: List<EditorScene> = emptyList(),
    val expandedScenes: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    val expandedSceneSettings: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    val expandedChoices: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    val expandedMapChapters: Set<Int> = emptySet(),
    val isHistoryInitialized: Boolean = false,
    val pendingJumpToSceneUid: String? = null,
    val variablesExpanded: Boolean = false,
    val initialStateExpanded: Boolean = false,

    // ----- Toolbar state (3.1b) -----
    val saveStatus: SaveStatus = SaveStatus.SAVED,
    val hasUnsavedChanges: Boolean = false,
    val menuExpanded: Boolean = false,
    val undoEnabled: Boolean = false,
    val redoEnabled: Boolean = false,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.data

data class ProgressData(
    val adventureFileName: String,
    val currentChapterIndex: Int = 0,
    val currentSceneId: String = "",
    val flags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    val appliedSceneEffects: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    val itemOrder: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val previousStepSnapshot: PlayerStateSnapshot? = null,
    val chapterStartSnapshot: PlayerStateSnapshot? = null,

    // ----- Steps gate (delta-based, survives reboot) -----

    /** Steps remaining until the next chapter opens. */
    val remainingSteps: Int = 0,

    /** Whether a steps gate is currently active. */
    val isGateActive: Boolean = false,

    /**
     * Raw TYPE_STEP_COUNTER reading at the moment this ProgressData was saved.
     * On load, the delta (currentAbsolute - lastAbsoluteAtSave) is subtracted from
     * [remainingSteps] to catch up with steps taken while the app was closed.
     * -1 means "unknown" (sensor has not produced any event yet).
     */
    val lastAbsoluteAtSave: Int = -1,

    /**
     * Fingerprint of the player-visible analyzer warnings at the moment
     * the player acknowledged them ("Продолжить игру" in the warning
     * dialog). Empty string = no acknowledgment yet, or the file has
     * changed since the last acknowledgment.
     *
     * **Why a fingerprint, not a Boolean.** If the author fixes one
     * warning and introduces another, a Boolean would stay `true` and
     * the player would never see the new warning. The fingerprint
     * changes whenever the set of warnings changes (a warning removed
     * or added, or a message changed), so the dialog re-appears — which
     * is correct: the player has not acknowledged *this* set yet.
     *
     * The fingerprint format is opaque; only the reader computes and
     * compares it. Old `progress.json` files without this field default
     * to `""`, which means "show the warning dialog on next open" —
     * the safe default.
     */
    val warningsFingerprint: String = "",

    /**
     * Scene ids whose **non-repeatable** gates (`gate_repeatable =
     * false`, the default) have been passed in this playthrough.
     *
     * Persisting this is essential: without it, a player who passed a
     * one-shot gate, closed the app, and reopened it would have to walk
     * the same steps again — the entire chapter-unlocking mechanic
     * would be broken across sessions. `repeatable = true` gates are
     * never listed here: they re-engage on every visit, so "passed" is
     * not a persistent state for them.
     *
     * Cleared by "restart adventure" (a new playthrough starts from
     * scratch). Old `progress.json` files without this field default to
     * `emptyList()`, which means "no gates passed" — the safe default.
     *
     * **In-progress gate state** (a gate the player is currently
     * walking through) is stored in [isGateActive] + [remainingSteps],
     * which already exist. This field is only about *completed*
     * non-repeatable gates.
     */
    val passedGates: List<String> = emptyList()
)

package com.myapp.adventure.data

import androidx.annotation.StringRes

enum class SearchFieldType(val icon: String) {
    SCENE_TITLE("📄"),
    SCENE_TEXT("📝"),
    CHOICE_TEXT("💬"),
    TAG_NAME("🏷")
}

/**
 * One search hit.
 *
 * **Ф4-infra (3b-6e-1):** [detail] was a plain `String` built inside
 * `SearchService` in Russian. That made `SearchService` (an `object`
 * without `Context`) a hidden source of user-facing strings and a hidden
 * blocker for `values-en/`. Now [detailRes] is a `@StringRes Int` and
 * the caller (`AdventureEditorFragment.showSearchDialog`) resolves it
 * with `getString(...)`.
 *
 * **Parametrized details.** One detail line is parametrized:
 * "Выбор #%d" (choice index). [detailArg] carries the `Int` argument;
 * for non-parametrized details it is `null`. The caller does:
 * ```
 * val text = if (result.detailArg != null)
 *     context.getString(result.detailRes, result.detailArg)
 * else
 *     context.getString(result.detailRes)
 * ```
 * If a future detail needs two or more args, upgrade [detailArg] to
 * `Array<Any>` — one call site, one field.
 */
data class SearchResult(
    val sceneUid: String,
    val sceneTitle: String,
    val fieldType: SearchFieldType,
    @StringRes val detailRes: Int,
    val detailArg: Int? = null,
    val contextBefore: String,
    val match: String,
    val contextAfter: String,
    val totalMatchesInField: Int,
    val charOffset: Int
)

package com.myapp.adventure.data

import androidx.annotation.StringRes

enum class IssueSeverity { ERROR, WARNING }

/**
 * One issue in the editor's "Проверить" (Validate) dialog.
 *
 * **Ф4-infra (3b-6e-1):** [title] was a plain `String` — Russian titles
 * were produced by `StoryValidator.titleFor(...)` (in `:utils`, no
 * `Context`) and by `AdventureEditorFragment.showValidationDialog`
 * inline. Now [titleRes] is a `@StringRes Int`; both producers return
 * / assign resource IDs, and the dialog resolves them with
 * `getString(...)`. Same separation as `SearchResult.detailRes`.
 *
 * **`description` stays `String`.** It carries engine-level messages
 * (`typeError.message`, `compileError.message`, `lintIssue.message`)
 * which are **English** by contract — they come from `:engine` and are
 * diagnostic, not localization surface. The caller adds no prefix; the
 * message already names the scene / flag / error.
 */
data class ValidationIssue(
    val severity: IssueSeverity,
    val sceneUid: String,
    @StringRes val titleRes: Int,
    val description: String
)

package com.myapp.adventure.ui.theme

import android.content.res.Configuration

import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.material3.Typography
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.CompositionLocalProvider
import androidx.compose.runtime.Immutable
import androidx.compose.runtime.ReadOnlyComposable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.staticCompositionLocalOf
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalDensity
import androidx.compose.ui.text.font.FontFamily
import androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.Density
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.myapp.adventure.data.theme.AppThemeConfig
import com.myapp.adventure.data.theme.BuiltInThemes
import com.myapp.adventure.utils.FontManager
import com.myapp.adventure.utils.ThemeManager

/**
 * Root theme for all Compose screens. Reads the current [AppThemeConfig]
 * from [ThemeManager] and the selected font from [FontManager], then
 * applies them via [MaterialTheme].
 *
 * Font scaling: the user's chosen scale (`FontManager.getFontScale`,
 * 0.85–1.3) is multiplied into `LocalDensity.fontScale`, mirroring what
 * Android does with SP values in the View world. DP values (padding,
 * corner radii) are not affected — same as on View screens.
 *
 * When [ThemeManager] is not initialized (previews, early composition),
 * `currentThemeSync()` returns [BuiltInThemes.DEFAULT].
 */
@Composable
fun AdventureTheme(
    isDark: Boolean = isSystemInDarkTheme(),
    config: AppThemeConfig = ThemeManager.currentThemeSync(),
    content: @Composable () -> Unit,
) {
    val context = LocalContext.current

    val colorScheme = remember(config, isDark) { config.toColorScheme(isDark) }
    val extendedColors = remember(config, isDark) { config.toExtendedColors(isDark) }
    val shapes = remember(config) { config.shapes.toShapes() }

    val fontFamily = remember { FontManager.getFontFamily(context) }
    val typography = remember(fontFamily) { Typography().withFontFamily(fontFamily) }

    // Scale SP values by the user's chosen font scale, like the View world does.
    // DP values remain unaffected because LocalDensity.density is unchanged.
    val baseDensity = LocalDensity.current
    val userFontScale = remember(config.typography.baseScale) {
        FontManager.getFontScale(context) * config.typography.baseScale
    }
    val scaledDensity = remember(baseDensity, userFontScale) {
        Density(baseDensity.density, baseDensity.fontScale * userFontScale)
    }

    CompositionLocalProvider(
        LocalDensity provides scaledDensity,
        LocalAdventureThemeConfig provides config,
        LocalAdventureExtendedColors provides extendedColors,
    ) {
        MaterialTheme(
            colorScheme = colorScheme,
            shapes = shapes,
            typography = typography,
            content = content,
        )
    }
}

/** Replaces [FontFamily] on every Typography style, keeping sizes/weights intact. */
private fun Typography.withFontFamily(family: FontFamily): Typography = Typography(
    displayLarge = displayLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
    displayMedium = displayMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
    displaySmall = displaySmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
    headlineLarge = headlineLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
    headlineMedium = headlineMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
    headlineSmall = headlineSmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
    titleLarge = titleLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
    titleMedium = titleMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
    titleSmall = titleSmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
    bodyLarge = bodyLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
    bodyMedium = bodyMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
    bodySmall = bodySmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
    labelLarge = labelLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
    labelMedium = labelMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
    labelSmall = labelSmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Extended colors (statuses not covered by Material 3's ColorScheme)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Status colours available on top of [MaterialTheme.colorScheme]. */
@Immutable
data class AdventureExtendedColors(
    val statusSuccess: Color,
    val statusWarning: Color,
    val statusDanger: Color,
    val statusInfo: Color,
    val statusNeutral: Color,
)

val LocalAdventureThemeConfig = staticCompositionLocalOf<AppThemeConfig> {
    BuiltInThemes.DEFAULT
}

val LocalAdventureExtendedColors = staticCompositionLocalOf<AdventureExtendedColors> {
    BuiltInThemes.DEFAULT.toExtendedColors(isDark = false)
}

/**
 * Accessor companion for [AdventureTheme]. Use:
 * ```
 * Text(color = AdventureTheme.extendedColors.statusSuccess)
 * ```
 */
object AdventureTheme {

    val config: AppThemeConfig
        @Composable @ReadOnlyComposable
        get() = LocalAdventureThemeConfig.current

    val extendedColors: AdventureExtendedColors
        @Composable @ReadOnlyComposable
        get() = LocalAdventureExtendedColors.current
}

@Preview(name = "Light", showBackground = true)

            }
        }
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.data.theme

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Complete description of a theme: colour palette (light + dark), plus
 * typography, shapes and spacing. This is the single source of truth for
 * the app's look, both for View screens (via the XML mirror) and for
 * Compose (via `ThemeManager.getColorScheme`).
 *
 * @property id Stable, URL-safe, lowercase identifier. Built-in themes
 *   use `"default"`; user themes will use `"custom_<uuid>"`. Never
 *   displayed to the user.
 * @property displayName Human-readable name shown in the theme picker.
 * @property isBuiltIn `true` for shipped presets (read-only), `false` for
 *   user themes (editable, deletable).
 * @property light Colour palette used in light mode.
 * @property dark Colour palette used in dark mode.
 * @property typography Font family id + scale factor.
 * @property shapes Corner radii.
 * @property spacing Spacing scale.
 *
 * The `@Serializable` with `explicitNulls = false` and default values on
 * every field makes this forward-compatible: adding new fields in a future
 * app version will still parse old JSON, as long as the new field has a
 * default value.
 */
@Serializable
data class AppThemeConfig(
    val id: String,
    val displayName: String,
    val isBuiltIn: Boolean = false,
    val light: ThemeColors,
    val dark: ThemeColors,
    val typography: ThemeTypography = ThemeTypography.Default,
    val shapes: ThemeShapes = ThemeShapes.Default,
    val spacing: ThemeSpacing = ThemeSpacing.Default,
) {
    init {
        require(id.matches(Regex("[a-z0-9_]+"))) {
            "Theme id must match [a-z0-9_]+, was: $id"
        }
        require(displayName.isNotBlank()) { "displayName must not be blank" }
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.ui.theme

import androidx.compose.material3.ColorScheme
import androidx.compose.material3.darkColorScheme
import androidx.compose.material3.lightColorScheme
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import com.myapp.adventure.data.theme.AppThemeConfig
import com.myapp.adventure.data.theme.ThemeColors

/**
 * Bridges the data-layer [AppThemeConfig] (Compose-free, colors as Long)
 * to Compose's [ColorScheme] / [AdventureExtendedColors].
 *
 * Kept in the UI layer on purpose: `data.theme` must not depend on Compose,
 * so the conversion lives here.
 */

/** Converts the light or dark palette of [this] to a Compose [ColorScheme]. */
fun AppThemeConfig.toColorScheme(isDark: Boolean): ColorScheme {
    val c = if (isDark) dark else light
    return if (isDark) {
        darkColorScheme().copyWithPalette(c)
    } else {
        lightColorScheme().copyWithPalette(c)
    }
}

/**
 * Copies every role from [c] onto the receiver. Roles that [ThemeColors]
 * does not define (surfaceContainer*, surfaceTint, …) keep their Material
 * default — extend [ThemeColors] later if a theme needs them.
 */
private fun ColorScheme.copyWithPalette(c: ThemeColors): ColorScheme = copy(
    primary = c.primary.toComposeColor(),
    onPrimary = c.onPrimary.toComposeColor(),
    primaryContainer = c.primaryContainer.toComposeColor(),
    onPrimaryContainer = c.onPrimaryContainer.toComposeColor(),
    inversePrimary = c.inversePrimary.toComposeColor(),

    secondary = c.secondary.toComposeColor(),
    onSecondary = c.onSecondary.toComposeColor(),
    secondaryContainer = c.secondaryContainer.toComposeColor(),
    onSecondaryContainer = c.onSecondaryContainer.toComposeColor(),

    tertiary = c.tertiary.toComposeColor(),
    onTertiary = c.onTertiary.toComposeColor(),
    tertiaryContainer = c.tertiaryContainer.toComposeColor(),
    onTertiaryContainer = c.onTertiaryContainer.toComposeColor(),

    background = c.background.toComposeColor(),
    onBackground = c.onBackground.toComposeColor(),
    surface = c.surface.toComposeColor(),
    onSurface = c.onSurface.toComposeColor(),
    surfaceVariant = c.surfaceVariant.toComposeColor(),
    onSurfaceVariant = c.onSurfaceVariant.toComposeColor(),
    inverseSurface = c.inverseSurface.toComposeColor(),
    inverseOnSurface = c.inverseOnSurface.toComposeColor(),

    error = c.error.toComposeColor(),
    onError = c.onError.toComposeColor(),
    errorContainer = c.errorContainer.toComposeColor(),
    onErrorContainer = c.onErrorContainer.toComposeColor(),

    outline = c.outline.toComposeColor(),
    outlineVariant = c.outlineVariant.toComposeColor(),
    scrim = c.scrim.toComposeColor(),
)

/** Converts the project-specific status colors (not part of M3) to Compose. */
fun AppThemeConfig.toExtendedColors(isDark: Boolean): AdventureExtendedColors {
    val c = if (isDark) dark else light
    return AdventureExtendedColors(
        statusSuccess = c.statusSuccess.toComposeColor(),
        statusWarning = c.statusWarning.toComposeColor(),
        statusDanger = c.statusDanger.toComposeColor(),
        statusInfo = c.statusInfo.toComposeColor(),
        statusNeutral = c.statusNeutral.toComposeColor(),
    )
}

/**
 * ARGB Long (`0xAARRGGBB`) → Compose [Color]. `toInt()` truncates the
 * high zero bytes; the result is a 32-bit ARGB int, which is exactly
 * what [Color] expects.
 */
internal fun Long.toComposeColor(): Color = Color(this.toInt())

FILE: app/src/main/java/com/myapp/adventure/data/theme/HexColorSerializer.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.data.theme

import kotlinx.serialization.KSerializer
import kotlinx.serialization.descriptors.PrimitiveKind
import kotlinx.serialization.descriptors.PrimitiveSerialDescriptor
import kotlinx.serialization.encoding.Decoder
import kotlinx.serialization.encoding.Encoder

/**
 * Serializes an ARGB colour (stored as [Long] in `0xAARRGGBB` form) to a
 * human-readable hex string and back.
 *
 * Format:
 *  - Opaque colours (alpha = 0xFF) serialize as `"#RRGGBB"`.
 *  - Translucent colours serialize as `"#AARRGGBB"`.
 *  - Both `#RRGGBB` and `#AARRGGBB` are accepted when decoding.
 *
 * Rationale: theme JSON is user-editable and should be diff-friendly.
 * Storing the raw `Long` would produce `0xFF5D4037L`, which is unreadable
 * in a hand-edited file.
 */
object HexColorSerializer : KSerializer<Long> {

    override val descriptor =
        PrimitiveSerialDescriptor("HexColor", PrimitiveKind.STRING)

    override fun serialize(encoder: Encoder, value: Long) {
        val alpha = ((value shr 24) and 0xFF).toInt()
        val rgb = value and 0xFFFFFF
        val hex = if (alpha == 0xFF) {
            "#%06X".format(rgb)
        } else {
            "#%02X%06X".format(alpha, rgb)
        }
        encoder.encodeString(hex)
    }

    override fun deserialize(decoder: Decoder): Long {
        val raw = decoder.decodeString().trim()
        require(raw.startsWith("#")) { "Hex colour must start with '#': $raw" }
        val hex = raw.substring(1)
        return when (hex.length) {
            6 -> 0xFF000000L or hex.toLong(16)              // #RRGGBB → opaque
            8 -> hex.toLong(16)                              // #AARRGGBB
            else -> error("Hex colour must be #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB: $raw")
        }
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.ui.theme

import androidx.compose.foundation.shape.RoundedCornerShape
import androidx.compose.material3.Shapes
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.myapp.adventure.data.theme.ThemeShapes

/**
 * Maps the data-layer [ThemeShapes] (dp values) to Compose [Shapes].
 * Material 3 has five named slots; we map small→extraSmall/small,
 * medium→medium, large→large/extraLarge so a single theme knob
 * (cornerSmall/Medium/Large) covers them.
 */
fun ThemeShapes.toShapes(): Shapes = Shapes(
    extraSmall = RoundedCornerShape(cornerSmall.dp),
    small = RoundedCornerShape(cornerSmall.dp),
    medium = RoundedCornerShape(cornerMedium.dp),
    large = RoundedCornerShape(cornerLarge.dp),
    extraLarge = RoundedCornerShape(cornerLarge.dp),
)

package com.myapp.adventure.data.theme

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Full Material 3 colour role set, plus project-specific status colours.
 *
 * Every value is an ARGB colour encoded as [Long] `0xAARRGGBB`. Use
 * [HexColorSerializer] for JSON round-tripping. Convert to Compose
 * `Color` in the UI layer (`Color(argb)`), never in this layer — the
 * data module must not depend on Compose.
 */
@Serializable
data class ThemeColors(
    // Primary
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val primary: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onPrimary: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val primaryContainer: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onPrimaryContainer: Long,

    // Secondary
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val secondary: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onSecondary: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val secondaryContainer: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onSecondaryContainer: Long,

    // Tertiary
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val tertiary: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onTertiary: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val tertiaryContainer: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onTertiaryContainer: Long,

    // Background / Surface
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val background: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onBackground: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val surface: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onSurface: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val surfaceVariant: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onSurfaceVariant: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val inverseSurface: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val inverseOnSurface: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val inversePrimary: Long,

    // Error
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val error: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onError: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val errorContainer: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val onErrorContainer: Long,

    // Outline
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val outline: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val outlineVariant: Long,

    // Scrim
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val scrim: Long,

    // Project-specific statuses (not part of M3, used in editor / stats)
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val statusSuccess: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val statusWarning: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val statusDanger: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val statusInfo: Long,
    @Serializable(with = HexColorSerializer::class) val statusNeutral: Long,
)

FILE: app/src/main/java/com/myapp/adventure/data/theme/ThemeDataStore.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.data.theme

import android.content.Context
import androidx.datastore.core.DataStore
import androidx.datastore.preferences.SharedPreferencesMigration
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.PreferenceDataStoreFactory
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.Preferences
import androidx.datastore.preferences.preferencesDataStoreFile
import okio.Path.Companion.toOkioPath

/**
 * Creates the app's theme [DataStore].
 *
 * Uses [PreferenceDataStoreFactory.createWithPath] with an Okio path. This
 * factory internally creates an [androidx.datastore.core.okio.OkioStorage],
 * which delegates file moves to Okio's `FileSystem.atomicMove`. On Windows
 * Okio uses `Files.move(..., ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING)`, so it can
 * replace an existing `*.preferences_pb` file — unlike the default
 * `FileStorage`, which relies on `File.renameTo` and fails on Windows
 * (issue b/203087070). This makes production and JVM unit tests behave
 * consistently across platforms.
 *
 * The file `theme_prefs.preferences_pb` lives in the app's private storage.
 * On first creation, keys `theme_id` and `night_mode` are migrated out of
 * the legacy `adventure_prefs` SharedPreferences file; after migration these
 * keys are removed from SharedPreferences, while unrelated keys
 * (`adventure_folder_uri`, `logging_enabled`) stay put.
 *
 * Custom themes are stored under the `custom_themes_json` key as a JSON
 * array — the same file, so all theme state lives in one place.
 */
object ThemeDataStore {

    private const val DATASTORE_FILE = "theme_prefs"

    /** Legacy SharedPreferences file used before the DataStore migration. */
    private const val LEGACY_PREFS_FILE = "adventure_prefs"

    /** SharedPreferences keys migrated into the DataStore exactly once. */
    private val MIGRATED_KEYS = setOf("theme_id", "night_mode")

    fun create(context: Context): DataStore<Preferences> {
        val file = context.applicationContext.preferencesDataStoreFile(DATASTORE_FILE)
        return PreferenceDataStoreFactory.createWithPath(
            migrations = listOf(
                SharedPreferencesMigration(
                    context = context.applicationContext,
                    sharedPreferencesName = LEGACY_PREFS_FILE,
                    keysToMigrate = MIGRATED_KEYS,
                )
            ),
            produceFile = { file.toOkioPath() },
        )
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.data.theme

import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.intPreferencesKey
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.stringPreferencesKey

/**
 * Keys stored inside the theme DataStore.
 *
 * - [KEY_THEME_ID] — id of the active theme (`"default"`, `"custom_<uuid>"`, …).
 * - [KEY_NIGHT_MODE] — an `AppCompatDelegate.MODE_NIGHT_*` constant, stored
 *   as an `Int` (matching what AppCompat uses internally).
 * - [KEY_CUSTOM_THEMES] — a JSON array of user-created `AppThemeConfig` objects.
 */
internal object ThemePreferences {
    val KEY_THEME_ID = stringPreferencesKey("theme_id")
    val KEY_NIGHT_MODE = intPreferencesKey("night_mode")
    val KEY_CUSTOM_THEMES = stringPreferencesKey("custom_themes_json")
}

FILE: app/src/main/java/com/myapp/adventure/data/theme/ThemeRepository.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.data.theme

import androidx.datastore.core.DataStore
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.Preferences
import androidx.datastore.preferences.core.edit
import kotlinx.coroutines.CompletableDeferred
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.SharingStarted
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.collect
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.combine
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.onEach
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.stateIn
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.serialization.builtins.ListSerializer
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json

/**
 * Single source of truth for theme state: which theme is active, its
 * night-mode override, and the list of user-created themes.
 *
 * Backed by a [DataStore] (see [ThemeDataStore]). The class caches the
 * latest state in memory as volatile fields so synchronous UI code
 * (View-based screens during the transition period) can read it without
 * blocking. All writes go through DataStore; the cache is updated
 * optimistically so reads immediately reflect the change.
 *
 * Threading: the constructor starts a coroutine in [scope] that keeps the
 * cache in sync with DataStore. Call [awaitInitialized] before relying on
 * the cache; it suspends only until the first DataStore emission has been
 * processed, not until the DataStore closes.
 */
class ThemeRepository(
    private val dataStore: DataStore<Preferences>,
    private val scope: CoroutineScope,
) {

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // In-memory cache (volatile: written from IO, read from main)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @Volatile private var cachedThemeId: String = ThemeSelection.DEFAULT_THEME_ID
    @Volatile private var cachedNightMode: Int = ThemeSelection.DEFAULT_NIGHT_MODE
    @Volatile private var cachedCustomThemes: List<AppThemeConfig> = emptyList()

    private val initialized = CompletableDeferred<Unit>()

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Flows
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    private val _selection = MutableStateFlow(ThemeSelection.Default)
    val selection: StateFlow<ThemeSelection> = _selection.asStateFlow()

    private val _customThemes = MutableStateFlow<List<AppThemeConfig>>(emptyList())
    val customThemes: StateFlow<List<AppThemeConfig>> = _customThemes.asStateFlow()

    /** All available themes: built-in presets plus user-created ones. */
    val allThemes: StateFlow<List<AppThemeConfig>> =
        combine(selection, customThemes) { _, customs ->
            BuiltInThemes.all + customs
        }.stateIn(scope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, BuiltInThemes.all)

    /** The currently active theme, resolved from [selection]. */
    val currentTheme: StateFlow<AppThemeConfig> =
        combine(selection, customThemes) { sel, customs ->
            BuiltInThemes.byId(sel.themeId)
                ?: customs.firstOrNull { it.id == sel.themeId }
                ?: BuiltInThemes.DEFAULT
        }.stateIn(scope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, BuiltInThemes.DEFAULT)

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Init
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    init {
        scope.launch {
            // onEach fires on every emission, including the first one, so
            // `initialized` completes as soon as the cache is warm.
            // `collect()` then keeps us subscribed for subsequent updates
            // (writes from setX() methods, DataStore edits from elsewhere).
            dataStore.data
                .onEach { prefs ->
                    applyPrefs(prefs)
                    initialized.complete(Unit)   // idempotent
                }
                .collect()
        }
    }

    private fun applyPrefs(prefs: Preferences) {
        val themeId = prefs[ThemePreferences.KEY_THEME_ID]
            ?: ThemeSelection.DEFAULT_THEME_ID
        val nightMode = prefs[ThemePreferences.KEY_NIGHT_MODE]
            ?: ThemeSelection.DEFAULT_NIGHT_MODE
        val customs = decodeCustomThemes(prefs[ThemePreferences.KEY_CUSTOM_THEMES])

        cachedThemeId = themeId
        cachedNightMode = nightMode
        cachedCustomThemes = customs

        _selection.value = ThemeSelection(themeId, nightMode)
        _customThemes.value = customs
    }

    /** Suspends until the initial DataStore read has populated the cache. */
    suspend fun awaitInitialized() = initialized.await()

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Synchronous reads (safe after awaitInitialized)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    fun getThemeIdSync(): String = cachedThemeId
    fun getNightModeSync(): Int = cachedNightMode
    fun getCustomThemesSync(): List<AppThemeConfig> = cachedCustomThemes

    fun getThemeByIdSync(id: String): AppThemeConfig =
        BuiltInThemes.byId(id)
            ?: cachedCustomThemes.firstOrNull { it.id == id }
            ?: BuiltInThemes.DEFAULT

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Writes
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    suspend fun setThemeId(themeId: String) {
        awaitInitialized()
        val safeId = if (isKnownTheme(themeId)) themeId
        else ThemeSelection.DEFAULT_THEME_ID
        cachedThemeId = safeId                         // optimistic update
        dataStore.edit { it[ThemePreferences.KEY_THEME_ID] = safeId }
    }

    suspend fun setNightMode(nightMode: Int) {
        awaitInitialized()
        cachedNightMode = nightMode                    // optimistic update
        dataStore.edit { it[ThemePreferences.KEY_NIGHT_MODE] = nightMode }
    }

    suspend fun setTheme(themeId: String, nightMode: Int) {
        awaitInitialized()
        val safeId = if (isKnownTheme(themeId)) themeId
        else ThemeSelection.DEFAULT_THEME_ID
        cachedThemeId = safeId
        cachedNightMode = nightMode
        dataStore.edit {
            it[ThemePreferences.KEY_THEME_ID] = safeId
            it[ThemePreferences.KEY_NIGHT_MODE] = nightMode
        }
    }

    suspend fun addOrReplaceCustomTheme(config: AppThemeConfig) {
        awaitInitialized()
        require(!config.isBuiltIn) {
            "Cannot store a built-in theme as custom: ${config.id}"
        }
        val updated = cachedCustomThemes
            .filterNot { it.id == config.id } + config
        persistCustomThemes(updated)
    }

    suspend fun removeCustomTheme(id: String) {
        awaitInitialized()
        val updated = cachedCustomThemes.filterNot { it.id == id }
        val removeActive = cachedThemeId == id

        cachedCustomThemes = updated
        if (removeActive) cachedThemeId = ThemeSelection.DEFAULT_THEME_ID

        val encoded = json.encodeToString(
            ListSerializer(AppThemeConfig.serializer()),
            updated,
        )
        dataStore.edit { prefs ->
            prefs[ThemePreferences.KEY_CUSTOM_THEMES] = encoded
            if (removeActive) {
                prefs[ThemePreferences.KEY_THEME_ID] = ThemeSelection.DEFAULT_THEME_ID
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Internals
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    private fun isKnownTheme(id: String): Boolean =
        BuiltInThemes.byId(id) != null || cachedCustomThemes.any { it.id == id }

    private suspend fun persistCustomThemes(themes: List<AppThemeConfig>) {
        val encoded = json.encodeToString(
            ListSerializer(AppThemeConfig.serializer()),
            themes,
        )
        cachedCustomThemes = themes                    // optimistic update
        dataStore.edit { it[ThemePreferences.KEY_CUSTOM_THEMES] = encoded }
    }

    private fun decodeCustomThemes(encoded: String?): List<AppThemeConfig> {
        if (encoded.isNullOrBlank()) return emptyList()
        return try {
            json.decodeFromString(
                ListSerializer(AppThemeConfig.serializer()),
                encoded,
            )
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            // Corrupted JSON — drop custom themes silently rather than crash.
            // Logging via Logger requires a folder URI that may not be ready
            // at this point in the startup sequence.
            emptyList()
        }
    }

    companion object {
        private val json = Json {
            ignoreUnknownKeys = true   // forward-compat: old readers don't break on new fields
            encodeDefaults = true
        }
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.data.theme

import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatDelegate

/**
 * The user's active theme selection: which palette to show + which night
 * mode. Together with [customThemes] this fully determines the app's look.
 *
 * [nightMode] is an `AppCompatDelegate.MODE_NIGHT_*` constant (an `Int`).
 * Using the raw constant instead of a higher-level enum keeps this class
 * free of UI concerns and makes DataStore round-tripping trivial.
 */
data class ThemeSelection(
    val themeId: String = DEFAULT_THEME_ID,
    val nightMode: Int = DEFAULT_NIGHT_MODE,
) {
    companion object {
        const val DEFAULT_THEME_ID = "default"
        val DEFAULT_NIGHT_MODE = AppCompatDelegate.MODE_NIGHT_FOLLOW_SYSTEM
        val Default = ThemeSelection()
    }
}

object StepCounterConstants {
    const val ACTION_START = "com.myapp.adventure.START_STEP_COUNTER"
    const val ACTION_STOP = "com.myapp.adventure.STOP_STEP_COUNTER"
    const val ACTION_UPDATE = "com.myapp.adventure.UPDATE_STEPS"

    /** Absolute (raw) reading from the step counter sensor since boot. */
    const val EXTRA_ABSOLUTE_STEPS = "absolute_steps"

    /** Delta since the previous sensor event (diff of absolute readings). */
    const val EXTRA_DELTA = "delta_steps"

    /**
     * Boolean: whether a step counter sensor is present on this device.
     * Broadcast together with [ACTION_UPDATE] so consumers can react to it.
     */
    const val EXTRA_SENSOR_AVAILABLE = "sensor_available"

    const val NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_ID = "step_counter_channel"
    const val NOTIFICATION_ID = 1
