# Engine types

**Status:** stable. Describes the type system introduced in Ф2 (2.1–2.8) of
[`checklist-tracker.md`](./checklist-tracker.md). Changes here are breaking
for every adventure file — extend with care.

This document is the reference for the **variable type system**: how
variables are declared, how the parser and type checker use them, what the
author must know when writing conditions and effects, and what is
enforced at runtime versus checked only at parse time.

It is the companion to [`engine-architecture.md`](./engine-architecture.md)
(which describes the module at a structural level) and to
[`gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md`](./gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md) (which
maps mechanics to phases, not types).

## Why a type system

Before Ф2, the author wrote:

```json
"choices": [{"text": "Enter", "condition": "has_sword", "next_scene": "b"}]
```

The parser accepted `has_sword`. At runtime, `has_sword` looked at the
player's flags. But `sword` was declared as an **item** — it lived in
`stats`, never in `flags`. So `has_sword` was always `false`, the button
was always disabled, and the author saw no error — just a "grey button
that should be active".

Ф2 closes this gap in two layers:

1. **Type checker** (parse time) — every reference is checked against
   the declared type: `has_sword` on `ItemCount` is a **blocking error**
   with a fix hint (`use 'sword > 0' instead`).
2. **Declarations** — the author states every variable's type in
   `"variables"`; there is no more "inferred from usage". Fallback mode
   exists for backward compatibility (see [Fallback](#fallback)).

## Where variables live

Variables are declared once in `"variables"` at the top of the adventure
file, and referenced by name from conditions (`"condition": "sword > 0"`)
and effects (`"modify_stats": {"sword": -1}`).

```json
{
  "title": "Example",
  "variables": {
    "health":    { "type": "int_range", "min": 0, "max": 100 },
    "sword":     { "type": "item_count" },
    "has_key":   { "type": "bool" },
    "gold":      { "type": "int_min", "min": 0 },
    "score":     { "type": "int" },
    "documents": { "type": "item_list" }
  },
  "initial_state": {
    "flags": ["has_key"],
    "stats": { "health": 100, "sword": 1, "gold": 10, "score": 0 }
  },
  "chapters": [  ]
}
```

In the IR, `"variables"` becomes `Adventure.variables: Map<String, VarDecl>`,
where each entry is `VarDecl(name, type)` with `type: VarType`.

`VarDecl.name` and the map key are identical by construction; the IR keeps
both so that `inferTypes` (see [Migration](#migration)) can return a
`Map<String, VarDecl>` directly comparable to the file's `variables`.

## The six types

| Type | JSON | IR | Default | Bounds (semantic) | When to use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bool** | `{"type": "bool"}` | `VarType.Bool` | `false` | n/a | Flags: "has sword", "met wizard". Referenced from `has_X` / `!has_X`, set with `set_flags` / `remove_flags`. |
| **Integer** | `{"type": "int"}` | `VarType.Integer` | `0` | none | Unbounded numbers: score, computed totals. Use when the variable genuinely has no min/max (rare). |
| **IntMin** | `{"type": "int_min", "min": N}` | `VarType.IntMin(N)` | `min` | `>= N` | Resources that cannot go negative but have no upper bound: gold, stamina, ammo, health (if the story never caps it). **Most common numeric type.** |
| **IntRange** | `{"type": "int_range", "min": A, "max": B}` | `VarType.IntRange(A, B)` | `min` | `[A, B]` | Bounded stats: health 0..100, skill 1..12, endurance 20..30, day 0..30. |
| **ItemCount** | `{"type": "item_count"}` | `VarType.ItemCount` | `0` | `>= 0` | Inventory items, stackable potions, arrows. Same runtime as `IntMin(0)`, kept distinct so the type checker can tell "how many" from "any number". |
| **ItemList** | `{"type": "item_list"}` | `VarType.ItemList` | `emptyList()` | n/a | Unordered collection of item identifiers. Reserved for Ф4 (N3, choice templates); today the type checker only knows "non-numeric". |

### Choosing between the numeric types

Ask two questions about the variable:

1. **Can it go below zero?** If no → `IntMin(0)` or `IntRange(0, N)`.
2. **Can it ever exceed some N?** If no → `IntMin(min)` (or `Integer` if
   the lower bound also doesn't apply). If yes → `IntRange(min, max)`.

For example:

| Variable | Question 1 | Question 2 | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `health` (0..100) | yes | yes (100) | `IntRange(0, 100)` |
| `gold` | yes | no | `IntMin(0)` |
| `score` | no | no | `Integer` |
| `skill` (1..12) | yes (1) | yes (12) | `IntRange(1, 12)` |
| `potion` (count) | yes | no | `ItemCount` |

**Rule of thumb: prefer `IntMin(0)` over `Integer`.** Most game variables
are resources that cannot go negative. `Integer` (no lower bound) should be
rare — it is useful for scores that may become negative after penalties,
and for variables whose bounds the author genuinely does not want to commit
to.

### Why three numeric variants, not one

- **Clarity at the JSON level.** `{"type": "int_range", "min": 0, "max": 100}`
  reads immediately as "health-like stat"; `{"type": "int"}` reads as
  "any integer". Six explicit variants make the intent visible.
- **Type-checker hints.** A `Compare` on `IntRange` can be validated
  against the range in a future phase (Ф3.6, `Analyzer.deadConditions`);
  this is impossible if all numerics collapse to one type.
- **Clamp policy.** Once type-aware clamping lands (see
  [Runtime clamp](#runtime-clamp)), the applier needs to know the bound.
  Today it clamps everything to `>= 0` regardless; the type is what will
  drive the policy.

## Type checking (parse time)

After the JSON parses cleanly, `JsonToIr.parse` runs
`TypeChecker.check(adventure)` (Ф2.3). The checker produces
`TypeError`s, not `ParseError`s: parse errors mean "the file cannot be
turned into IR"; type errors mean "the file is structurally sound, but its
variable references are wrong". Both are blocking — the reader refuses to
open the file, the editor shows the errors in the validation dialog.

### What is rejected

| Variant | Trigger | Example | Fix hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UnknownVariable` | A name in a condition or effect is not in `variables` | `condition: "has_swrod"` | Rename to `has_sword` |
| `HasOnNonBool` | `has_X` / `!has_X` where `X` is not `Bool` | `condition: "has_sword"` on `ItemCount` | Use `sword > 0` |
| `SetFlagOnNonBool` | `set_flags` on a non-`Bool` variable | `set_flags: ["gold"]` | Use `modify_stats: {"gold": 1}` |
| `RemoveFlagOnNonBool` | `remove_flags` on a non-`Bool` variable | `remove_flags: ["health"]` | Use `modify_stats: {"health": -health}` |
| `ModifyStatOnNonNumeric` | `modify_stats` on `Bool` or `ItemList` | `modify_stats: {"has_key": 1}` | Use `set_flags` / `remove_flags` |
| `CompareOnNonNumeric` | `X op N` where `X` is not numeric | `condition: "has_key > 0"` | Use `has_has_key` |
| `InRangeOnNonNumeric` | `X in a..b` where `X` is not numeric | (reserved for Ф3.2) | Use `has_X` or a `Compare` |
| `InitialFlagOnNonBool` | A non-`Bool` name in `initial_state.flags` | `"flags": ["health"]` | Move to `initial_state.stats` |
| `InitialStatOnNonNumeric` | A `Bool` / `ItemList` name in `initial_state.stats` | `"stats": {"has_key": 1}` | Move to `initial_state.flags` |

Every error is scoped to a scene (`sceneId`) except `InitialState` ones
which have `sceneId == null` and appear first in the sorted output.

### Error ordering

`TypeChecker.check` returns errors sorted by
`(sceneId == null, sceneId.value, message)`. This is stable across runs,
which matters for snapshot tests of the editor's validation dialog and
for `git diff` of golden outputs.

## Fallback

**What it is.** If `variables` is empty (or absent from the JSON — pre-Ф2.8
files), `TypeChecker` runs in **fallback mode**: it infers a provisional
type table from `tags` and `initialState`, and checks references against
that.

**Why keep it.** Two reasons:

1. **Backward compatibility.** Files written before Ф2.8 carry no
   `variables`. Without fallback, those files would fail parse with
   `UnknownVariable` on every reference. Fallback lets the reader open
   them; the editor shows a warning "types are not declared" and offers
   to declare them (Ф2.7).
2. **Incremental migration.** An author opening an old file in the editor
   sees the warning, clicks "Suggest types" (Ф9.2, future), gets a
   `variables` block pre-filled by `inferTypes`, reviews and saves.
   Fallback makes the file playable **while** the author migrates it.

**How the inferred table is built.** See `TypeChecker.buildTypeTable` KDoc;
summary:

- **`tags[].category`** — `HEALTH` → `IntMin(0)`, `ITEM` → `ItemCount`,
  `JOURNAL` → `Bool` (or `IntMin(0)` if the name appears in
  `initialState.stats`).
- **`initialState.flags`** → `Bool`.
- **`initialState.stats`** → `IntMin(0)`.

If the inferred table is **empty** (no tags, no initial state), the checker
returns no errors — there is nothing to check against, and pretending
otherwise would produce false positives. The "you have not declared
variables" signal is a **UI concern** (Ф2.7 warning, Ф9.2 realtime-linter),
not a `TypeError`.

**Fallback is not weaker.** Typo `has_swrod` still produces
`UnknownVariable` if `sword` is a tag. `has_sword` on `sword: ItemCount`
still produces `HasOnNonBool`. Fallback only loses the ability to check
**cross-field** consistency (e.g. "author declared `HEALTH` but used
`Bool`"), which strict mode sees.

## Migration

**Tool:** `inferTypes(adventure): Map<String, VarDecl>` — public in
`:engine/ir/types/TypeInference.kt` (Ф2.8.2).

Given a parsed `Adventure` with an empty or incomplete `variables`, it
proposes a `Map<String, VarDecl>` that the author can review and copy into
the JSON.

**Priority resolution** when signals conflict:
`HEALTH tag > ITEM tag > numeric usage > Bool usage`.

Rationale in `inferTypes` KDoc, summary:

- **`tags[].category`** is deliberate — the author wrote it. It beats
  incidental usage.
- **Numeric usage > Bool usage** — a Bool cannot appear in `modify_stats`
  (it is a type error), while a numeric can appear in `set_flags` only
  by mistake. When both signals are present, the type checker's
  subsequent error ("`SetFlagOnNonBool`") is a clearer fix-target than
  "`ModifyStatOnNonNumeric`".

**`inferTypes` never guesses bounds.** It emits only `Bool`,
`ItemCount`, or `IntMin(0)` — never `Integer` or `IntRange`. The author
who wants a bounded variable declares it explicitly.

**Idempotence.** On `test_adventure.json` (which now has both declarations
and usage), `inferTypes(adv) == adv.variables` — this is the tripwire test
`TypeInferenceTest > real test_adventure_json - inference matches declared variables`.
If it fails, either the file was edited inconsistently or the logic
drifted.

**What it is not.** `inferTypes` does not validate. It does not check
against an existing `variables` block; it does not resolve contradictions
in contradictory usage. It is a **suggestion engine**, not a validator.
Validation is `TypeChecker`.

## Runtime clamp

**Current state (as of Ф2).** `EffectsApplier.apply` clamps every
`Effect.ModifyStat` to `>= 0`, regardless of the variable's declared
type. This is the same policy as Ф1.5 (`EffectsApplier.kt` KDoc,
"Clamp policy (temporary, until Ф2.8)"). Ф2 did not change it — the DoD
for Ф2.8 was "inferTypes + test_adventure migration + type-clean
reference sample", not "type-aware clamp".

Consequence: a `IntRange(0, 100)` variable (`health`) can exceed its
`max` if the player walks through enough `+50` effects, because the
applier does not enforce the upper bound. The **type checker** sees the
range and will be able to flag out-of-range literals in a future phase
(Ф3.6, `Analyzer.deadConditions`), but the **runtime** today only knows
"not below zero".

**What is not enforced yet:**

| Type | Declared bound | Enforced at runtime | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Bool` | n/a | n/a | Flags are set/removed, not clamped |
| `Integer` | none | `>= 0` (over-eager) | No lower bound in type; applier clamps anyway |
| `IntMin(N)` | `>= N` | `>= 0` (**not `>= N`**) | `N > 0` (e.g. `skill: 1..12` but declared `IntMin(1)`) is not enforced |
| `IntRange(A, B)` | `[A, B]` | `>= 0` (**not `[A, B]`**) | Upper bound not enforced; lower bound only `>= 0` |
| `ItemCount` | `>= 0` | `>= 0` | Correct by coincidence (policy matches type) |
| `ItemList` | n/a | n/a | Applier does not touch lists |

**Why this is deferred.** Type-aware clamp needs a `VarType` lookup at
every `ModifyStat`, which means `EffectsApplier.apply` must take the
`Adventure` (or at least `variables`). That changes its signature and
every call site (`Engine.step`, the reader preview, the debug panel).
Worth doing — but tied to save/restore (Ф5.2, S5, delta model), because a
restored state must be clamped identically to a freshly-applied one.
Doing it now would double the work in Ф5.

**What the author should know today:**

- **Do not rely on `IntRange.max` being enforced.** If the story needs a
  hard cap, add an explicit `Compare` condition on the choice that
  raises the stat, or a scene effect that resets it.
- **Do not rely on `IntMin(N > 0)` being enforced.** A negative delta can
  bring a `skill: 1..12` variable down to `0`. Add an explicit guard if
  the range matters.
- **`ItemCount` is safe** — the applier's `>= 0` policy matches the type.
- **`Integer` will not go below 0** even though the type permits it.
  This is an over-eager policy, not a bug — it has the same explanation
  as above.

The clamp will be type-aware in a future phase; when it lands, this
section will change to "enforced" and the type declarations will become
fully authoritative.

## Common authoring mistakes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Choice is visible but always disabled; no error in editor | `condition: "has_sword"` on an `ItemCount` variable, but file still in fallback mode (no `variables`) | Add `variables` block; the checker will now reject it as `HasOnNonBool` |
| Choice is visible but always disabled; error in editor: "Variable 'swrod' is used but not declared" | Typo in condition | Rename to `sword` |
| Health rises indefinitely, upper bound ignored | `IntRange(0, 100)` declared, but applier does not enforce `max` (see [Runtime clamp](#runtime-clamp)) | Add explicit `Compare` guard, or wait for type-aware clamp |
| Stat goes to 0 but the story expected it to stay at `min: 1` | `IntMin(1)` declared, but applier clamps only `>= 0` | Same — explicit guard, or wait |
| `initial_state.flags` contains a numeric name; editor reports `InitialFlagOnNonBool` | Author put `health` in `flags` by mistake | Move to `initial_state.stats` |

  `Stat`, `Health`, …).

# Gamebook mechanics — coverage

**Status:** evolving. Reference, not a contract. Update when a mechanic moves
between statuses.

This file records **which gamebook mechanics from
[`research/gamebook-mechanics.md`](./research/gamebook-mechanics.md)
Adventure supports today, which are partial, and which are planned** — and
for the unsupported ones, what architectural piece is missing. It is the
answer to "does the checklist need new items for this?" — the short answer
is **no** (see §"Why the checklist does not change"), but the long answer
is the table below.

**Not to be confused with:**
- [`progress/progress-log.md`](./progress/progress-log.md) — chronological
  log of "what was done". This file is a static status map, updated only
  when a mechanic changes status.
- [`roadmap.md`](./roadmap.md) — the full post-Ф10 plan (Ф12+). This file
  points to it; the roadmap defines the order and content of those phases.

## How to read

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Supported** | The mechanic is fully expressible with today's IR (`Condition`, `Effect`, `Scene`, `Choice`, `Gate`) and `Engine.step`. No future phase needed. |
| **Partial** | Expressible, but with caveats — e.g. no atomicity, no dedicated counter, semantics pushed onto author or reader. Usable today; a dedicated mechanic may follow in a later phase. |
| **Not supported** | Requires an architectural piece that does not exist yet. "Blocked by" names the piece; "Planned" points to the roadmap phase. |

**Blocked-by codes:**

| Code | What is missing | Where it would live |
|---|---|---|
| **RNG** | A `RandomSource` abstraction injected into `Engine.step` (deterministic in tests, real RNG in production) | `:engine` — Ф12 |
| **PROC** | A first-class `Procedure` node in IR for multi-step computations (combat rounds, complex crafting) | `:engine` — Ф13. Partially addressed by N6 (subroutines, Ф4.7–Ф4.8); not enough for combat |
| **EXT** | An "external outcome" hook on `Engine.step` (physical dexterity, visual puzzle) — engine receives a pre-decided boolean from `:app` | `:engine` + `:app` — Ф15 |
| **CROSS** | Cross-adventure / cross-run state: `LibraryState`, separate from `ProgressData` | `:engine` + `:app` — Ф16 |
| **MULTI** | Multiplayer mechanics (two-player simultaneous choices, shared state) | `:engine` + network — Ф17 |
| **UI** | Authoring UI for the mechanic (the engine may already support it, but authors cannot express it) | `:app` editor — Ф18 |
| **APP** | Concern that lives entirely in `:app` (wall-clock timing, notifications), not in `:engine` | `:app` — Ф15 or later |

**37 entries** (source doc calls them "34 mechanics"; its tables enumerate
37 — 34 base mechanics + 3 sub-variants of `M-RES-RNG`:
`HIGH`/`LOW`/`DVD`).

|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Navigation | 7 | 3 | 1 | 3 |
| M2 Resolution | 10 | 2 | 0 | 8 |
| M3 State | 7 | 6 | 0 | 1 |
| M4 Combat | 4 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| M5 Meta | 9 | 2 | 2 | 5 |
| **Total** | **37** | **13** | **3** | **21** |

## Architectural gaps (why "not supported")

Every "not supported" mechanic traces back to one of the six gaps below.
Closing a gap unlocks all mechanics that list it in "Blocked by".

| Gap | Mechanics it unblocks | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| **RNG** | `M-NAV-RANDOM`, `M-NAV-EVENT`, `M-RES-RNG*`, `M-RES-HYBRID`, `M-RES-BOOST`, `M-STATE-BUILD` | Ф12 |
| **PROC** | `M-COMBAT-ROUND`, `M-COMBAT-CMP`, `M-COMBAT-DRAIN`, `M-META-CRAFT` (atomicity) | Ф13 |
| **EXT** | `M-RES-PHYS`, `M-RES-PUZZLE` | Ф15.1 |
| **CROSS** | `M-META-XFER`, `M-META-PERSIST`, `M-META-LEGACY` | Ф16 |
| **MULTI** | `M-COMBAT-MULTI` | Ф17 |
| **APP** | `M-META-REALTIME` | Ф15.2 |

## What the foundation already supports (why no new Must)

Four pieces already in the plan make the roadmap feasible without
re-architecting:

1. **N6 (subroutines, Ф4.7–Ф4.8)** — a multi-step call/return mechanism
   from IR. Not enough for combat on its own (combat is a loop with state,
   not a single call), but it is the scaffolding for `Procedure` (Ф13).
2. **Sealed `Condition` / `Effect`** (Ф1.2) — a new variant (e.g.
   `Effect.Roll`) can be added without breaking existing code, and the
   parser rejects unknown variants via `@SerialName` rules. This is what
   makes "add a mechanic without rewriting the engine" possible.
3. **Versioned IR + migrations** (Ф5.3) — every new mechanic bumps
   `Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION` (v2 → v3 → …) and adds a migration for
   old files. `test_adventure.json` exercises each new mechanic (Rule 1
   of [`test-adventure-policy.md`](./test-adventure-policy.md)).
4. **`CompiledAdventure` with O(1) lookup** (Ф1.5.5.1) — the runtime
   indexes are the same shape regardless of how many mechanics exist.
   Combat, RNG, cross-adventure state do not change the "find scene by
   id" lookup — they change what happens **inside** a step, not how a
   scene is found.

**What would change the checklist:** if a future Must-hard requirement
("the app must support combat at release") appeared, Ф12–Ф13 would have
to be pulled before Ф10. There is no such requirement today. See
`docs/roadmap.md` for the full post-Ф10 plan.

## Update procedure

**When you implement a mechanic** (i.e. a gap closes or a new `Effect`/
`Condition`/`Procedure` variant lands):

1. Change its row's status: `Not supported` → `Supported` (or `Partial`).
2. Clear or adjust "Blocked by" (it may still be partial).
3. Move "Planned" to `—` (done).
4. **Add** a new entry to
   [`progress/progress-log.md`](./progress/progress-log.md) — this file
   is a snapshot, the progress log is the history.
5. If the mechanic has an authoring UI, update
   [`authoring-guide.md`](./authoring-guide.md) (Ф10.7) in the same PR.

**When you add a new mechanic to `research/gamebook-mechanics.md`:**

1. Add a row to the corresponding M-class table here with the initial
   status (`Not supported` unless it maps to existing IR).
2. Add it to the appropriate "Architectural gaps" bucket, or add a new
   bucket if no existing gap covers it.
3. Add a phase to [`roadmap.md`](./roadmap.md) if it is not covered by
   an existing one.

# Glossary

**Status:** evolving. Terms are added and refined as the app evolves.

This file is the single source of truth for:

- **Domain terminology** — how core concepts are named in code and docs.
- **UI strings** — Russian UI text mapped to English, so that adding an
  English locale later is a lookup, not a redesign.
- **Naming conventions** — spellings we commit to across the project.

When a new term is introduced anywhere in the project, add it here in the same
change. When in doubt about a spelling, follow this file — not your intuition.

## How to use

- **In docs**: use the English term from the "English" column. Do not invent
  synonyms.
- **In the app (Russian)**: the current UI uses Russian. When a string in the
  app matches a row here, treat the row as the canonical mapping.
- **For future i18n**: the Russian string is the source key. Keep the mapping
  up to date as the UI evolves.
- **In code**: keep the identifiers exactly as they appear in the
  "Identifier" columns. Renaming a data model or JSON field is a **breaking
  change** and requires a doc-update PR.

## 1. Domain terms

Concepts that appear across code, JSON and documentation.

| English            | Russian                   | Notes                                                                 |
|--------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Adventure          | Приключение               | Also the project's name. Never translate "Adventure" when it refers to the app or the project. |
| Chapter            | Глава                     | A group of scenes. **Pure narrative grouping** — no gate of its own. Gates live on scenes (see Gate, Ф1.5.4). |
| Gate               | Шлюз                      | A step requirement on a single scene (`scenes[].gate`). The player must walk N steps after entering the scene before any exit is allowed. Can sit anywhere in a chapter (first, middle, last), or be absent. |
| Scene              | Сцена                     | One screen of text and (optionally) choices.                          |
| Choice             | Выбор / вариант действия  | A single selectable action in a scene.                                |
| Next scene         | Следующая сцена           | The scene a choice leads to (`next_scene`).                           |
| Condition          | Условие                   | A rule that must hold for a choice to be visible.                     |
| Tag                | Метка                     | An effect or flag used by a scene or choice.                          |
| Flag               | Флаг                      | A boolean-ish marker (`set_flags` / `remove_flags`).                  |
| Stat               | Стат                      | A numeric value (`modify_stats`).                                     |
| Item               | Предмет                   | A tag with `category=ITEM`. Shown in the inventory.                   |
| Journal entry      | Запись журнала            | A tag with `category=JOURNAL` and `visible=true`.                     |
| Health             | Здоровье                  | A tag with `category=HEALTH` (or the literal name `health`).          |
| Initial state      | Начальное состояние       | The player's starting flags and stats (`initial_state`).              |
| Player state       | Состояние игрока          | Current flags + stats + inventory of the player.                      |
| Death scene        | Сцена смерти              | Special scene shown when the player dies (`death_scene`).             |
| Chapter end        | Конец главы               | A scene that closes a chapter (`isChapterEnd`).                       |
| Step gate / Gate   | Шаговый шлюз / Гейт       | A step requirement on a **scene** (`scenes[].gate`), not on a chapter. The player must walk N steps after entering the scene before any exit is allowed. Can sit anywhere in a chapter. See also `Gate`. |
| Required steps     | Требуемые шаги            | The numeric threshold of a `Gate` (`gate.requiredSteps`). In v1 files this lived on `chapters[].required_steps`; the v1→v2 migration moves it to the last scene of the previous chapter. |
| Remaining steps    | Осталось шагов            | Steps left until the gate opens.                                      |
| Death (state)      | Смерть                    | The player's health has reached zero.                                 |
| Draft (editor)     | Черновик                  | Unsaved editor state, saved in `editor_draft_prefs`.                  |
| Validation issue   | Проблема валидации        | A warning or error reported by `StoryValidator`.                      |
| Story stats        | Статистика истории        | Scene/word/choice counts shown in the editor.                         |
| RandomSource       | Источник случайности      | **Planned (Ф12+).** Abstraction over randomness in `Engine.step`; injected so tests are deterministic. See `docs/roadmap.md`. |
| Procedure          | Процедура                 | **Planned (Ф13+).** A multi-step computation invoked from a scene or choice (e.g. combat rounds), modelled as a dedicated IR node. See `docs/roadmap.md`. |
| Combat             | Бой                       | **Planned (Ф13+).** A procedure that resolves a fight between player and enemy over several rounds. Requires RNG (Ф12) and procedures (Ф13). See `docs/roadmap.md`. |

## 2. JSON field names

These are the canonical field names of the adventure JSON. They are part of
the file format and must not be renamed without a migration plan.

| Field                                 | Meaning                                                     |
|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `title`                               | Adventure title.                                            |
| `author`                              | Adventure author.                                           |
| `description`                         | Short description.                                          |
| `initial_state`                       | Player's starting flags and stats.                          |
| `initial_state.flags`                 | Starting flags (list of strings).                           |
| `initial_state.stats`                 | Starting stats (map name → int).                            |
| `tags`                                | Registry of tag definitions for this adventure.             |
| `tags[].name`                         | Stable, machine-readable tag name.                          |
| `tags[].display_name`                 | Human-readable name shown in the UI.                        |
| `tags[].category`                     | `HEALTH` / `ITEM` / `JOURNAL`.                              |
| `tags[].visible`                      | Whether the tag is shown in the HUD.                        |
| `death_scene`                         | Optional. Death scene definition.                           |
| `death_scene.id`                      | Scene ID used for the death screen.                         |
| `death_scene.text`                    | Text shown when the player dies.                            |
| `death_scene.allow_step_back`         | Whether the "step back" button is shown.                    |
| `death_scene.allow_chapter_restart`   | Whether the "restart chapter" button is shown.              |
| `death_scene.allow_adventure_restart` | Whether the "restart adventure" button is shown.            |
| `chapters`                            | Ordered list of chapters.                                   |
| `chapters[].id`                       | Chapter ID.                                                 |
| `chapters[].title`                    | Chapter title.                                              |
| `chapters[].required_steps`           | **Legacy (v1 only).** Steps needed to enter this chapter. Migrated on load to `scenes[].gate` on the last scene of the previous chapter. Ignored in v2 files. |
| `scenes[].gate`                       | **v2+.** Positive integer: steps the player must walk after entering this scene before any exit is allowed. Absent = no gate. See `Gate`. |
| `chapters[].scenes`                   | Scenes in this chapter.                                     |
| `scenes[].id`                         | Scene ID (unique per adventure).                            |
| `scenes[].text`                       | Scene body text.                                            |
| `scenes[].set_flags`                  | Flags to add when the scene is entered.                     |
| `scenes[].remove_flags`               | Flags to remove when the scene is entered.                  |
| `scenes[].modify_stats`               | Stat changes when the scene is entered.                     |
| `scenes[].choices`                    | Available choices in this scene.                            |
| `choices[].text`                      | Choice label shown to the player.                           |
| `choices[].next_scene`                | ID of the scene this choice leads to.                       |
| `choices[].condition`                 | Optional condition gating this choice.                      |
| `choices[].set_flags`                 | Flags to add when this choice is taken.                     |
| `choices[].remove_flags`              | Flags to remove when this choice is taken.                  |
| `choices[].modify_stats`              | Stat changes when this choice is taken.                     |

## 3. Tag categories

| Value      | Russian  | Meaning                                                    |
|------------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `HEALTH`   | Здоровье | Numeric health-like value; shown in the HUD heart icon.    |
| `ITEM`     | Предмет  | Inventory item; shown in the HUD backpack.                 |
| `JOURNAL`  | Журнал   | Boolean-like flag or visible journal entry.                |

The literal tag name `health` is always treated as `HEALTH`, regardless of the
declared category.

## 4. Conditions (as strings in JSON)

| Syntax    | Meaning                                        |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------|
| `has_X`   | True if flag `X` is set or stat `X` > 0.       |
| `!has_X`  | True if flag `X` is not set and stat `X` ≤ 0.  |
| `X >= N`  | True if stat `X` is at least `N`.              |
| `X < N`   | True if stat `X` is less than `N`.             |
| *(empty)* | Always true.                                   |

## 6. Naming conventions

- **"Adventure" as the project and the app** — never translated. The word is
  the brand.
- **Domain terms in code** — use the spellings in section 1 (e.g.
  `Adventure`, `Chapter`, `Scene`, `Choice`, `DeathScene`, `PlayerState`).
- **JSON fields** — always `snake_case`, exactly as listed in section 2.
- **Kotlin identifiers** — as in the codebase (`EditorScene`, `EditorChoice`,
  `EditorTag`, `StepHistoryManager`, `ProgressManager`, `StepCounterService`,
  `HealthConnectStepSource`, `SensorStepSource`).
- **Paths and folder names** — `Adventures/` and `NewAdventures/` are the
  only user-visible folders created by the app; their names are fixed.
- **Russian UI text** — use «guillemets» for quoted user-facing text inside
  English docs, e.g. «Меню».

## 7. Not covered (yet)

Deliberately excluded, to be added as the relevant feature stabilizes:

- Locale codes and Android resource qualifiers (`values-ru`, `values-en`,
  etc.) — to be documented when the English locale is added.
- Format specifications for `progress.json`, `step_history.json`,
  `debug_log.txt` — internal persistence formats that may still change.
- Debug-only strings beyond the debug panel (internal simulations) — these
  are for developers and live only in code.

Add new sections as the app gains new user-facing surfaces.


================================================
FILE: docs/i18n-policy.md
================================================
# i18n policy

**Status:** evolving. Governs where user-facing strings live and how they
are written. This file is the single source of truth until full
localization lands in Ф7; the language rules for documentation itself are
in [`documentation-rules.md §1`](./documentation-rules.md#1-language).

## Where strings live

| Kind of string | Where | Language |
|---|---|---|
| User-facing UI (labels, buttons, toasts, dialog titles, error messages) | `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` | RU (source key). EN added in Ф7.3. |
| Log/debug strings (`Logger.log(...)`) | inline in `.kt` | RU (temporary; Ф7.3 may move them). |
| Debug panel labels (`dialog_debug_*.xml`, `showDebugPanel`) | inline in `.xml` / `.kt` | RU (temporary; debug-only, not user-facing). |
| Adventure content (scene text, choice text, tag display names) | `test_adventure.json` / user files | Per-author; **not** translated by the app. |
| Developer-facing strings (exception messages, code comments, KDoc) | `.kt` inline | EN (per `CONTRIBUTING.md`). |

**Why user-facing strings go into `strings.xml`.** Two reasons that matter
today: (a) **digest / source-control readability** — a `.kt` or `.xml`
file with Russian `setText("Меню")` / `android:text="Сохранить"`
some tools (gitingest, some diff viewers) have trouble with; moving the
Cyrillic into one small `strings.xml` keeps the source files largely
ASCII; (b) **ready for Ф7.3** — `values-en/` translation is a lookup
step, not a rewrite.

**Why log / debug / content strings stay outside.** Log strings are
diagnostic, not user-facing (the reader rarely sees them); translating
them to `strings.xml` adds ~80 keys with no reader benefit. Debug panel
labels are for developers only. Adventure content belongs to the author,
not the app's UI.

## Naming convention

- **`snake_case`, prefix by area:**

  | Prefix | Area |
    |---|---|
  | `app_*` | Application-wide (`app_name`). |
  | `menu_*` | Main menu (`MenuFragment`). |
  | `library_*` | Adventure list (`AdventureListFragment`). |
  | `editor_*` | Editor: toolbar, scene card, choice card, map. |
  | `template_*` | Template list screen and edit dialog (since Ф4.3.2a). |
  | `reader_*` | Reader (`AdventureReaderFragment`). |
  | `stats_*` | Statistics (`StatisticsFragment`). |
  | `settings_*` | Settings (`SettingsFragment`). |
  | `setup_*` | First-run setup (`SetupFragment`). |
  | `logs_*` | Log viewer (`LogViewerFragment`). |
  | `search_*` | Search dialog (`AdventureEditorFragment.showSearchDialog`). |
  | `validation_*` | Validation dialog (`AdventureEditorFragment.showValidationDialog`). |
  | `action_*` | Shared action buttons outside dialogs (`action_menu`, `action_back`, `action_undo`, `action_redo`, `action_debug`). |
  | `dialog_*` | Shared dialog buttons (`dialog_save`, `dialog_cancel`, …). |

- **Plurals** use `<plurals name="<area>_<noun>_plural">` — same pattern
  as the existing `steps` (one / few / many / other).

- **Placeholders** use positional format: `%1$d`, `%2$s` — same pattern
  as the existing `stats_rank_progress`.

- **Shared buttons** (`save`, `cancel`, `delete`, `ok`, …) live under the
  `dialog_*` prefix and are reused across screens — do not duplicate
  `dialog_cancel` as `editor_cancel` + `template_cancel`.

## What NOT to do

- **Do not inline user-facing Russian in `.kt` or `.xml`** — use
  `@string/…` in layouts and `getString(R.string.…)` in Kotlin. The
  only exceptions are the two rows in the table above marked
  "RU (temporary)".
- **Do not add `values-en/` yet.** The translation phase is Ф7.3. An
  empty `values-en/` with copies of Russian would make an English
  system show Russian UI with the false appearance that translations
  exist; an empty `values-en/` with no copies would show Russian UI
  anyway (Android falls back to `values/`). Either way, the directory
  buys nothing until real EN strings are ready.
- **Do not translate progress-log entries, KDoc, comments, or
  developer-facing strings** — those follow
  [`documentation-rules.md §1`](./documentation-rules.md#1-language).

## Migration status

- **Ф4-infra (batch 1, this batch):** policy file, `strings.xml` header
  comment + shared dialog buttons.
- **Ф4-infra (batch 2a):** `fragment_*.xml` layouts (editor, list,
  map, reader, log viewer, menu, settings, setup, template list) →
  `@string/…`. Also `action_*` shared button prefix introduced.
- **Ф4-infra (batch 2b):** `dialog_*.xml` and `item_*.xml` layouts →
  `@string/…`, except debug-panel layouts (`dialog_debug_*`,
  `item_debug_*`) which are deliberately left inline.
- **Ф4-infra (batch 3):** all user-facing `setText(...)` /
  `Toast.makeText(...)` / `AlertDialog` titles and buttons in Kotlin →
  `getString(R.string.…)`, except `Logger.log` and debug-panel labels.
- **Ф4-infra (batch 3b-5-fix):** `ruQuantityString` workaround
  (`app/.../utils/PluralHelper.kt`). `<plurals>` rules come from the
  **device** locale, not from the source `values/` directory — on a
  non-`ru` device, Russian plurals get wrong forms
  (`4882 шагов` instead of `4882 шага`). Forcing the Russian locale at
  the call site fixes it for every device until English defaults land.
  **Remove this workaround in Ф7.3**, when `values/` becomes English
  and `values-ru/` carries the Russian forms.
- **Ф7.3:** `values-en/` translation, generated from `strings.xml`.
  After this phase, `ruQuantityString` is deleted and call sites use
  `context.resources.getQuantityString(...)` — the device locale then
  picks the right rules automatically.

## See also

- [`documentation-rules.md §1`](./documentation-rules.md#1-language) —
  language rules for documentation itself.
- [`glossary.md`](./glossary.md) — Russian ↔ English term reference.
- [`checklist-tracker.md`](./checklist-tracker.md) §Ф7.3 — full
  localization phase.

> Interactive text adventures for Android, gated by real-world steps.

**Status:** pre-alpha. These docs are a living tree; some sections are still
`draft` and will grow as the project stabilizes. See
[`documentation-rules.md`](./documentation-rules.md) for how docs are written
and maintained.

  scenes, choices, tags, chapters, step gates, death scenes.

# Roadmap — post-Ф10

**Status:** evolving. Planning document, not a promise. Priorities may
change; the current contract is [`checklist-tracker.md`](./checklist-tracker.md).

This is the **detailed** roadmap for everything **after** the checklist
2.1 is accepted (after gate Ф10). It covers three groups:

1. **Gamebook mechanics** (Ф12–Ф18) — support for more formats and
   mechanics from [`research/gamebook-mechanics.md`](./research/gamebook-mechanics.md).
   Which mechanics are supported today and which gap blocks each one is
   recorded in [`gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md`](./gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md).
2. **Nice-to-have** items from Appendix B of the checklist (S3 undo,
   PWA, Steam, plugins, analytics, …).
3. **Distribution / community** — how the app reaches people once the
   core is stable.

**Not to be confused with:**
- [`../ROADMAP.md`](../ROADMAP.md) — one-page "current focus / next /
  later", human-readable for newcomers. It points here for depth.
- [`checklist-tracker.md`](./checklist-tracker.md) — the contract for
  Ф0–Ф10. This file starts where that one ends.
- [`research/gamebook-mechanics.md`](./research/gamebook-mechanics.md) —
  the source classification of gamebook mechanics. This roadmap does
  **not** redefine mechanics; it schedules them.
- [`gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md`](./gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md) —
  which mechanics are supported **today**. This roadmap says when the
  unsupported ones arrive.

## Where we are

The checklist 2.1 closes at gate Ф10 with 40 Must and 19 explicit Nice
items. See [`checklist-tracker.md`](./checklist-tracker.md). Everything
in this roadmap is **after** that point and is **not** required for
acceptance.

## Part 1 — Gamebook mechanics (Ф12–Ф18)

Seven phases. Six architectural gaps (RNG, PROC, EXT, CROSS, MULTI, APP)
from [`gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md`](./gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md)
close all 21 unsupported mechanics. The foundation that makes these
phases tractable without re-architecting already exists:

- sealed `Condition`/`Effect` (Ф1.2) — new variants are additive;
- N6 subroutines (Ф4.7–Ф4.8) — scaffolding for `Procedure`;
- versioned IR + migrations (Ф5.3) — every phase bumps
  `Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION`;
- `CompiledAdventure` O(1) lookup (Ф1.5.5.1) — the runtime does not
  change shape, only what happens inside a step.

**Ordering rationale:** RNG is first because most other gaps depend on
it (combat, character init, hybrid, boost). Procedures are second
because combat is the largest single feature. External outcomes and
cross-adventure state are independent and can be reordered. Authoring UI
is last, after the engine mechanics exist, mirroring the pattern of Ф9
(author tools after the engine and reader are stable).

### Ф12 — RNG foundation

**Goal:** a `RandomSource` abstraction + first IR nodes that consume it.

**Unlocks:** `M-NAV-RANDOM`, `M-NAV-EVENT`, `M-RES-RNG*` (HIGH / LOW /
DVD), `M-RES-HYBRID` (partial — with PROC in Ф13),
`M-RES-BOOST`.

**Depends on:** Ф10 (stable engine); no dependency on Ф13–Ф17.

| ID | Task | Days | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ф12.1 | `RandomSource` interface + `Engine.step(randomSource, …)` overload. Production: `SecureRandom`; tests: deterministic `SeededRandomSource`. | 2 | `Engine.step` accepts `RandomSource`; existing tests unchanged (overload with default); one test proves two runs with the same seed produce the same outcomes |
| Ф12.2 | `Effect.Roll` / `Condition.Roll` — the three roll directions (HIGH, LOW, DVD). IR v3 + migration v2 → v3 (identity — old files simply have no rolls). | 3 | `ConditionParser` accepts `roll_high(2d6 + skill >= 10)`, `roll_low(2d6 <= luck)`, `roll_dvd(2d6 + spd vs 2d6 + spd)`; golden updated; analyzer rejects malformed roll specs |
| Ф12.3 | `M-RES-HYBRID` — a roll combined with a condition (`if has_sword && roll_high(...)`) | 1.5 | A scene with `has_sword` AND a roll works; analyzer warns when the roll depends on a stat that is never set |
| Ф12.4 | `M-RES-BOOST` — resource-spending reroll / modifier (`spend 1 luck to reroll`) | 2 | A choice with `boost(luck, 1, reroll)` either spends and rerolls, or is `Rejected(Blocked(...))` when the resource is missing |
| Ф12.5 | `M-NAV-RANDOM` — random link: `next_scene` determined by a roll | 1 | A scene's exit rolls a die, result indexes into a list of scene ids; both branches playable; `test_adventure.json` has a demo |
| Ф12.6 | `M-NAV-EVENT` — random content event: RNG picks an **effect list**, not a transition | 1.5 | A scene rolls, applies one of two effect lists; state differs measurably between seeds |
| Ф12.7 | Docs + `test_adventure.json` extended with one demo per roll type + `docs/engine-rng.md` | 1.5 | All M-RNG mechanics in `gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md` marked Supported; golden updated; `docs/engine-rng.md` stable |

**Gate Ф12:** all six sub-mechanics work end-to-end on `test_adventure.json`; `RandomSource` is injectable; the same seed produces byte-identical `PlayerState` after a full playthrough.

**Scope guard.** Do **not** add "fudge" / "reroll entire playthrough" / hidden luck counters. Only what the coverage map lists under RNG. Anything else is a new mechanic → new roadmap row.

### Ф13 — Procedures and advanced navigation

**Goal:** a first-class `Procedure` node in IR, plus open-world / hub navigation.

**Unlocks:** `M-COMBAT-ROUND`, `M-COMBAT-CMP`, `M-COMBAT-DRAIN`,
`M-META-CRAFT` (atomicity), `M-NAV-FREE`.

**Depends on:** Ф12 (combat needs RNG for to-hit rolls).

| ID | Task | Days | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ф13.1 | `Procedure` node in IR (call / return with local state, bounded loop count). Reuses the stack idea from N6 but adds local variables and a step counter. | 4 | A `Procedure` with a loop and local state compiles, runs, and is testable in isolation; analyzer rejects unbounded loops |
| Ф13.2 | `M-COMBAT-ROUND` — one round: attacker roll, defender roll, loser takes damage. Implemented as a `Procedure`. | 3 | A combat scene runs until one side reaches 0; each round visible in tests; `test_adventure.json` has a demo combat with a win and a loss path |
| Ф13.3 | `M-COMBAT-CMP` — combat-ratio table (Lone Wolf style): a `Procedure` that maps `(attacker_skill − defender_skill, roll)` to damage | 2.5 | Table-driven combat works; the table is IR data (not code); analyzer checks the table is complete for all ratios |
| Ф13.4 | `M-META-CRAFT` — atomic crafting: a `Procedure` that checks ingredients, consumes them, produces the result, or rolls back on failure | 2 | A failed craft leaves the state unchanged (test: 3 ingredients, fail, 3 remain); a successful craft is atomic |
| Ф13.5 | `M-NAV-FREE` — open-world / hub navigation: a scene with a list of "rooms" (scene ids) reachable from it; a persistent "current room" in progress | 3 | A hub scene with 4 rooms playable; returning to the hub remembers where the player was; `docs/engine-navigation.md` |
| Ф13.6 | Docs + `test_adventure.json` combat + hub demos + golden | 2 | All PROC + `M-NAV-FREE` mechanics marked Supported; `docs/engine-procedures.md` stable |

**Gate Ф13:** combat, crafting, and open-world navigation all work on `test_adventure.json`; the `Procedure` node is analysable (no infinite loops, no unbounded locals); analyzer reports combat-table gaps as errors, not warnings.

**Scope guard.** Combat is **single-player, turn-based**. No real-time, no grid, no spell-crafting loop. `M-COMBAT-MULTI` is Ф17. Crafting is **atomic one-step**, not a tree of recipes.

### Ф14 — Character initialization

**Goal:** build the starting `PlayerState` from rolls / choices, not from a hardcoded `initial_state`.

**Unlocks:** `M-STATE-BUILD`.

**Depends on:** Ф12 (rolls).

| ID | Task | Days | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ф14.1 | `Adventure.startBuild: BuildSpec?` in IR — rolls and/or choice menus (`roll 1d6+6 for skill`, `choose one of 4 disciplines`); replaces `InitialState` when present, augments when absent | 3 | A v4 adventure with `start_build` produces a `PlayerState` from rolls/choices; legacy `initial_state` still works unchanged |
| Ф14.2 | Editor UI: "Character creation" tab in `AdventureEditorFragment` | 2 | Author can add rolls / choice menus; preview shows a sample `PlayerState` generated by three different seeds |
| Ф14.3 | Docs + `test_adventure.json` demo + golden | 1.5 | `M-STATE-BUILD` marked Supported; migration v3 → v4 (identity: old files have no `start_build`) |

**Gate Ф14:** a new adventure can define `start_build` with a stat roll and a choice menu; three different seeds produce three different, valid starting states; a legacy adventure without `start_build` is unchanged.

### Ф15 — External outcomes and real-time pacing

**Goal:** hooks for mechanics that the engine cannot decide on its own —
physical dexterity, puzzles, wall-clock timing.

**Unlocks:** `M-RES-PHYS`, `M-RES-PUZZLE`, `M-META-REALTIME`.

**Depends on:** Ф10 only (independent of Ф12–Ф14).

| ID | Task | Days | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ф15.1 | `Condition.ExternalOutcome(name)` — a condition the engine treats as "decided by the caller"; `:app` provides the boolean (mini-game result, drawn line, found object) | 2 | A scene gated by `external_outcome("draw_line")` plays: `:app` shows the mini-game, returns the result, engine advances. Test uses a stubbed outcome |
| Ф15.2 | `M-META-REALTIME` — wall-clock pacing (delay before a choice, timer countdown) as an `:app`-level feature that gates the `StepResult` | 2 | A choice with `delay_seconds(120)` is disabled until the timer expires; `:app` shows countdown; engine knows nothing about wall clock |
| Ф15.3 | Docs + `test_adventure.json` demo + golden | 1.5 | `M-RES-PHYS`, `M-RES-PUZZLE`, `M-META-REALTIME` marked Supported; `docs/engine-external.md` |

**Gate Ф15:** an external outcome can gate a choice; the engine never sees the mini-game code; a wall-clock timer can gate a choice without keeping the app awake.

### Ф16 — Cross-adventure state

**Goal:** state that survives across adventures and playthroughs.

**Unlocks:** `M-META-XFER`, `M-META-PERSIST`, `M-META-LEGACY`.

**Depends on:** Ф10 (saves, S1–S6) + Ф13 (procedures, for skill carry-over if any).

| ID | Task | Days | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ф16.1 | `LibraryState` (separate from `ProgressData`) — per-library, not per-adventure. Fields: which books finished, which endings seen, per-book "persistent" flags | 3 | Two adventures in a library share `LibraryState`; progress of one does not overwrite the other |
| Ф16.2 | `M-META-XFER` — character transfer between adventures of a series: `Adventure.accepts_transfer_from: List<String>` | 2 | Playing "Book 2" can import the final `PlayerState` of "Book 1"; conflicts (skill missing) reported, not silently defaulted |
| Ф16.3 | `M-META-PERSIST` / `M-META-LEGACY` — flags set in one playthrough that persist to the next; legacy modifiers | 3 | A flag set in run 1 changes the start of run 2 (test with two linked runs) |
| Ф16.4 | Docs + `test_adventure.json` demo (two-adventure series) + `docs/engine-library-state.md` | 2 | `M-META-XFER` / `PERSIST` / `LEGACY` marked Supported; migration of any new IR fields |

**Gate Ф16:** two adventures in one library can transfer a character; a persistent flag set in one is visible in the next; `LibraryState` is not lost on app restart.

### Ф17 — Meta-mechanics

**Goal:** the remaining exotic mechanics.

**Unlocks:** `M-COMBAT-MULTI`, `M-META-MOD`, `M-META-TIME` (turn counter as first-class).

**Depends on:** Ф12 (RNG), Ф13 (combat), Ф16 (library).

| ID | Task | Days | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ф17.1 | `M-META-TIME` — a first-class turn / day counter with an author-visible action cost per step; exhaustion is `StepResult.Rejected(Blocked(...))` or `Success(isDead = true)` per author spec | 2 | A playthrough with a 30-day limit ends correctly; the analyzer shows estimated "days to finish" per branch |
| Ф17.2 | `M-META-MOD` — modular content: a side IR fragment (`Module`) that an adventure can opt into; collision on ids reported | 2.5 | A small module adds one scene and one item to a base adventure; test verifies the merge and a collision report |
| Ф17.3 | `M-COMBAT-MULTI` — two-player simultaneous combat | 5 | Two devices, one match, both see the same outcome. **Only if** Ф17.1 / Ф17.2 land and there is demand. Otherwise parked. |
| Ф17.4 | Docs + `test_adventure.json` demo + `docs/engine-meta.md` | 2 | All `M-META-*` marked Supported (except multi, which may stay Partial) |

**Gate Ф17:** `M-META-TIME`, `M-META-MOD` work end-to-end; `M-COMBAT-MULTI` either lands or is explicitly parked in `gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md` with a rationale.

**Scope guard.** Multiplayer is **offline two-device** (local network, no server). If it needs a backend, it moves out of the roadmap into a separate product decision.

### Ф18 — Authoring UI for new mechanics

**Goal:** bring the author tools up to date with Ф12–Ф17, mirroring what
Ф9 did for the base feature set.

**Depends on:** Ф12–Ф17.

| ID | Task | Days | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ф18.1 | Editor for `Procedure` (combat and crafting): a visual loop editor, not a text DSL | 4 | Author builds a 3-round combat with two effects in one scene; preview shows the effect on `PlayerState` |
| Ф18.2 | Editor for rolls: choose direction, dice, threshold; live preview with a "roll 10 times" button | 2 | Author sees the distribution of outcomes before playing |
| Ф18.3 | Editor for cross-adventure links: pick `accepts_transfer_from`; show `LibraryState` keys available | 2 | Author links book 2 to book 1; a "test transfer" button shows the resulting state |
| Ф18.4 | Editor for external outcomes: pick mini-game template; define the boolean mapping | 2 | Author picks "draw line" mini-game, defines "success = line does not intersect"; preview stubs the result |
| Ф18.5 | End-to-end audit: a full authoring scenario covering RNG + combat + transfer | 2 | The scenario runs without leaving the app; results in `docs/authoring-tools.md` |
| Ф18.6 | Docs | 1.5 | `docs/authoring-tools.md` and `docs/authoring-guide.md` cover every new mechanic |

**Gate Ф18:** the editor exposes every mechanic that Ф12–Ф17 added; the end-to-end authoring scenario succeeds; the analyzer is up to date (all new checks surface inline, per A5 from Ф9).

## Part 2 — Nice-to-have from Appendix B

17 explicit Nice items + 10 `.advanced` extensions. Grouped by domain;
each row says what makes it actionable (the "entry trigger"). None of
these block acceptance.

| ID | Item | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| S3 | Undo | After Ф5 (delta model exists) |
| S4 | Backlog (history viewer) | After S3 |
| S7 | Compact history | After S5 + P2 (i.e. after Ф5) |
| P3 | Compact snapshots | After S5 + P2 |
| U1 | Themes (dark / light, separately from system) | After U9.base (Ф6) |
| U8 | Reduced motion (extended) | After U9.base |
| U10 | Lint-choice | After A5 (Ф9) |
| L5 | Plurals | After L1–L4; StringId already designed for plural forms |
| L7 | Incremental localization | After L4, when the catalog exceeds ~500 strings |
| E2 | PWA | If E1.base returns to scope, or as a standalone export once Ф7 stable |
| E3 | Mobile distribution (Play Store / F-Droid) | After Ф10, once the app is stable |
| E4 | Steam | Only if E1.base returns to scope (needs JS runtime) |
| E6 | Embedding (integrate the reader into another app) | After E5 (schema + round-trip) |
| A2 | Graph visualisation | After A5 (realtime linter); it is a visualisation of the analyzer, not the other way around |
| A7 | Merge tool | After N5 (explicit merge) and A2 |
| X1 | Plugins | After X3.base (stable docs) and A5 |
| Q3 | Analytics | ⚠ Conflicts with Q2.base (no telemetry). Only opt-in, local, with explicit consent |

### S3a — Step back from any scene

**Status:** shipped in Ф1.7.1b-followup (2026-11-08). Recorded here
for traceability.

**Goal:** the player can step back one scene at any point, not
only after death — e.g. walked into a gated scene, decided not to
walk N steps, wants to undo.

**What it needed (small — ~30 lines):**
- **Single-level undo.** `previousStepSnapshot` already holds the
  previous scene's state (saved in `updateChoices` before the
  transition). No `ArrayDeque` is needed: a book-game allows only
  one step back, plus "to chapter start" and "restart adventure"
  — all three snapshots already exist.
- **`previousStepSnapshot = null` after a step back.** Prevents
  chaining. Done in `restoreSnapshot` (single source of truth for
  any caller).
- **UI:** menu item "↩ Шаг назад", visible only when
  `previousStepSnapshot != null`, not in preview mode, and not on
  the death screen (the death screen has its own button).
- **Gate interaction:** `restoreSnapshot` already called
  `resetGate()` — with this feature, that call became functional
  (no longer a no-op). Leaving a gated scene discards its gate
  progress; returning re-engages the gate (repeatable) or shows it
  already passed (non-repeatable).

**Depends on:** nothing new — the state was already there.

**Entry trigger:** shipped alongside Ф1.7.1b (persistence of
`passedGates`) — the two are complementary: without persistence,
a non-repeatable gate's "passed" state would not survive a step
back across app restarts; without step back, the gate progress
could only be reset by restarting the adventure.

**`.advanced` extensions** (do not have separate rows; they are extensions
of the parent Must and are picked up opportunistically):

| Extension | Parent | When it becomes actionable |
|---|---|---|
| N6.advanced (loops in subroutines) | N6 | With Ф13 (`Procedure` already needs bounded loops) |
| N7.advanced (beyond AND/OR/count) | N7.base | If authors ask; needs an ADR |
| U4.advanced (automatic contrast adjustment) | U4.base | If users ask |
| L8.advanced (dynamic language loading) | L8.base | If more than 3 languages are needed |
| E1.advanced (full PWA offline) | E1 | If E2 (PWA) enters scope |
| A6.advanced (random-walk test generator) | A6 | If authoring needs more test data than the sample file |
| P1.advanced (10k+ scenes) | P1.base | If a real adventure hits the 2k ceiling; needs a measurement first |
| P4.advanced (incremental / cancellable analysis) | P4.base | If the analyzer becomes a UI bottleneck on a 2k-scene project |
| X3.advanced (community docs) | X3.base | If contributors ask for an external wiki |
| Q2.advanced (IndexedDB / local cache) | Q2.base | Only with Q3 (analytics), which is opt-in and unlikely |

### Additional Nice items (identified 2026-11-07)

These two blocks were identified during the UI/UX foundation (U11–U14)
and localization (L1–L4) discussions in the checklist. They are Nice-class
work **after** Ф10 and do **not** block acceptance. They live here rather
than in Appendix B because Appendix B is the **frozen** checklist 2.1 list
— new items found later belong to the roadmap, not to the contract.

#### Author themes (U15)

**Goal:** let an author attach a visual style to their adventure —
fonts, colours, background, spacing — so that a horror adventure looks
different from a cozy one, without the user having to change system
settings per book.

**What U13/U14 (Must, Ф6.3/Ф6.4) already provide:** the **mechanism** —
`theme.json` schema, `ThemeManager`, levels (user / author / default),
priority rules (especially with reduced motion and high contrast),
whether the theme travels with the adventure or lives separately. U13/U14
are Must because they define **how** theming works. U15 is the **author
feature** built on top.

**Not to be confused with:** U1 (dark/light as a user preference) — that
is a per-user setting, part of the default theme, not an author feature.

| ID | Task | Days | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| U15.1 | Editor UI: author picks a theme (from a shipped set), overrides individual properties (font, colours, background), previews the reader with the theme applied | 3 | U14 (must), Ф9.3 (preview) |
| U15.2 | Theme distribution: package `theme.json` inside the adventure ZIP (E7), or as a sidecar file `Themes/<adventure-id>.json` — pick one, document in `docs/theming.md` (U13 already reserves the decision) | 1.5 | U13, U14 |
| U15.3 | Inheritance and precedence tests: user's reduced motion and high contrast **win** over the author's theme (accessibility cannot be silently overridden); document the exact rules; automated tests | 2 | U15.1 |
| U15.4 | Docs: extend `docs/theming.md` and `docs/authoring-guide.md` with the author-facing workflow | 1.5 | U15.3 |

**Gate U15:** author can attach a theme to an adventure; the reader uses
it; the user's accessibility settings still win where they should; a
"default" adventure and a "themed" adventure side by side demonstrate the
difference; documentation is stable.

**Entry trigger:** after Ф10 (checklist accepted) **and** after U14 has
shipped and seen at least one release cycle — otherwise we would be
designing the author UI against an unstable user-facing theme mechanism.

#### Translation workflow (T1–T4)

**Goal:** let an adventure be translated into multiple languages, shipped
with all of them, and updated when the source changes — without the
translator needing to work inside the Android app.

**What L1–L4 (Must, Ф7) already provide:** string extraction
(`extractStrings` → `StringCatalog`), stable `StringId` (structural
path, survives text edits), context export, PO/XLIFF round-trip. These
are **file-level** primitives. What they do **not** provide: how multiple
translations of the **same** adventure live together, how a translation
is updated when the source changes, how to validate a translation before
shipping.

| ID | Task | Days | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Multi-language packaging: one adventure × N languages, linked by `StringId`. Format: either `adventure.json` + `strings/<locale>.json` inside the ZIP (E7), or a parallel `adventure.<locale>.json` — pick one, document in `docs/localization.md` | 3 | L1–L4 (Ф7), E7 (ZIP) |
| T2 | Translation update flow: diff current source against the last translated source, list stale `StringId`s, mark them in the editor (U10 realtime-linter picks them up). "Update translation" button in the editor | 2.5 | T1, Ф9.2 (linter) |
| T3 | Placeholder validation: `%d`, `{name}`, `${var}` — check that translations contain the same placeholders as the source, in the same positions; reject translations that drop or duplicate a placeholder; automated test in the exporter/importer | 2 | L4 (PO/XLIFF), T1 |
| T4 | Translator UI (minimal): import `.po`, apply to the current IR, show completeness ("142/150 strings translated"), export back; not a full CAT tool, just a round-trip in-app | 2 | T3, Ф9 (editor infrastructure) |

**Gate T1–T4:** an adventure with two translations (ru/en) ships as one
ZIP; the reader picks the language from the user's UI locale; the editor
shows stale strings after a source edit; placeholder mismatches are
blocked at import; a translator can round-trip `.po` inside the app.

**Entry trigger:** after Ф10 (checklist accepted) **and** after L1–L4
have shipped; T1 depends on E7 (ZIP) being stable.

### i18n cleanup — RU source comments (C1)

**Goal:** translate every remaining Russian **source comment** (`// …`
and `/** … */` KDoc) in `:app/src/main/java/` to English, per
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md)'s "source-code comments are in
English" rule.

**Status (as of 2026-11-15).** User-facing migration is complete across
`:app` **and** `:engine`:

- every user-facing string lives in
  `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`;
- `:engine` **code** is clean of RU (data defaults that used to carry
  RU — `DeathScene.text = "💀 Вы погибли."`, `Dto.DeathSceneDto.text`,
  `:app/data/Adventure.author = "Неизвестен"` — are now empty strings,
  and the reader / library fall back to `R.string.*`; see 3b-6h in
  `progress-log-4.md`);
- KDoc **quotations** of UI strings remain in both `:app` and
  `:engine` (e.g. `:engine/.../parse/StepResult.kt:33` quotes
  `"недоступно"`, `:engine/.../format/JsonToIr.kt:597` quotes
  `«Проверить»`, `:engine/.../ir/types/TypeChecker.kt:59` quotes the
  Ф2.2 DoD), and are covered by this item — they are citations, not
  Russian prose.
- `HardcodedText = 0` in every layout except the debug-only ones
  (`dialog_debug_*`, `item_debug_*`), which are exempt per
  [`i18n-policy.md`](./i18n-policy.md);
- every `Toast` / `AlertDialog` / `setText` for the user in `:app` goes
  through `getString(R.string.…)`.

What remains is **developer-facing**: `// ---------- Section ----------`
dividers, a few `//` notes in adapters, and `Ф`-prefixed KDoc — see the
table below.

**Data defaults vs user-facing strings.** A `String` constant inside
`:engine` IR or `:app` data classes is user-facing **iff** the UI reads
it directly. The `test_adventure.json` reference sample writes
`author`, `death_scene.text`, `display_name`, etc. explicitly, so the
defaults only fire for legacy files — but where they do, they land on
screen. 3b-6h converted every such default to an empty `""` and moved
the user-visible fallback into `R.string.*` in `:app`. Remaining RU
constants in code (e.g. `AdventureEditorViewModel` translit map, JSON
`Chapter.title = "Глава $N"`) are **not** user-facing: the first is a
transliteration table, the second is never rendered (UI regenerates
chapter titles from editor state).

| File | ~blocks | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `ui/editor/AdventureEditorFragment.kt` | ~14 | `// --- Section ---` dividers + a few notes |
| `ui/editor/AdventureEditorViewModel.kt` | ~10 | `// --- Section ---` dividers + `Ф2.7` KDoc |
| `ui/editor/EditorSceneAdapter.kt` | ~15 | `// --- Section ---` dividers |
| `ui/editor/VariablesAdapter.kt` | ~4 | KDoc header (Ф2.7) + 3 notes |
| `ui/editor/EditorHelpers.kt` | 1 | KDoc `/** Renders one tag row … */` |
| `ui/editor/AdventureMapAdapter.kt` | 2 | KDoc + `// --- Model ---` |
| `ui/editor/AdventureMapFragment.kt` | 1 | KDoc `/** Same algorithm as … */` |
| `ui/editor/InitialStateAdapter.kt` | 1 | (already fixed to `// Tag rows` in 3b-6c — one left as example) |
| `utils/StoryStatsService.kt` | 3 | `/** … */` + 3 `//` notes |
| `data/ProgressData.kt`, `data/EditorModels.kt`, `data/Adventure.kt` | ~15 | KDoc referencing `Ф2.7` / `Ф1.7.5` |
| `utils/StoryValidator.kt` | ~10 | `Ф2.6`-prefixed KDoc |
| `:engine/.../parse/StepResult.kt`, `Condition.kt`, `ir/DeathScene.kt`, `ir/Outcome.kt`, `format/JsonToIr.kt`, `ir/types/TypeChecker.kt`, `ir/types/TypeInference.kt` | ~7 | KDoc quotations of UI strings / DoD text (per §1, translation deferred to the same Ф7.3 pass) |

**Why deferred.** Two reasons:

1. **Nuance.** Many comments carry a deliberate reference — `Ф2.7 DoD`,
   `Ф1.7.5` decision, direct quotes from `checklist-tracker.md`. A
   batch-by-batch translation risks dropping that reference. One
   translation pass, once, preserves it.
2. **Terminology alignment.** RU → EN for "метка", "сцена", "шаг",
   "стат", `Ф`-prefix retention, is a **single decision**. Doing it in
   the same change as `values-en/` guarantees source comments and
   resource strings use the same final terms.

**Entry trigger:** Ф7.3 (localization). Do it as the **first sub-step**
of Ф7.3 — before adding `values-en/` — so that source-comment terminology
and resource-string terminology land together.

**What stays in Russian forever** (by policy, not this item):

- `Logger.log(…)` — diagnostics, not user-facing.
- Debug-panel strings — `showDebugPanel` and friends.
- `docs/progress/progress-log-1.md`, `progress-log-2.md` — historical
  records; `documentation-rules.md §1` explicitly says "do not translate
  this file retroactively".
- `Ф`-prefix in KDoc and comments — project terminology, not Russian
  prose (`documentation-rules.md §1`, "The `Ф` prefix is project
  terminology, not Russian text").

### Data path cleanup (after Ф1.7.5)

The same adventure JSON has **two representations** in the codebase
— `:app/data/Adventure` (Gson POJO, lossy) and `:engine/ir/Adventure`
(kotlinx.serialization, full). IR-only fields (`is_ending`, `gate`,
`gate_repeatable`, `version`, `start_scene`, `variables`) silently
vanish whenever data passes through `:app/data/Adventure`. This is
the class of bug behind Ф1.7.1a-fix (`AdventureListFragment` →
reader) and the `is_ending`-in-preview limitation of Ф1.7.5 (fixed
by adding the field to the POJO, but `gate` / `gate_repeatable`
still drop on the same path — **gates in preview still do not
work**).

Three steps, in order. Each is independently shippable; b3 is
blocked on the exporter (Ф8).

#### b1 — `AdventureListFragment` reads IR

**Goal:** the library list stops going through
`:app/data/Adventure` for reading. `parseAdventureFromUri` →
`JsonToIr.parse` → `:engine/ir/Adventure`. `AdventureAdapter` takes
`List<:engine/ir/Adventure>` (fields `title` / `author` /
`description` are identical to the POJO).

**Why now, why safe:** the list already does not pass
`adventure_json` to the reader (Ф1.7.1a-fix — only
`adventure_file_uri`). So the POJO is used solely for the list
display, and its lossy nature has no observable effect on the
list. Migrating removes a latent path, not a live bug.

**Scope:** ~15 lines, `:app/ui/list/`. No new tests — the existing
`:engine` tests (`RealAdventureTest`, `GoldenIrTest`) already cover
`JsonToIr.parse` on `test_adventure.json`. Smoke: the list still
shows the same title / author / description.

**Depends on:** Ф1.7.5 (shipped 2026-11-09).

#### b2 — `:app/data` gets `gate`, `gate_repeatable`, `version`, `start_scene`

**Goal:** the editor write path emits enough fields for the reader
to see gates and `is_ending` in preview. **No IR migration** — the
`:app/data` POJO is extended to match the adventure JSON exactly
for the fields the reader needs.

**What it does:**
- `:app/data/Scene` += `gate: Int?` (`@SerializedName("gate")`),
  `gateRepeatable: Boolean?`
  (`@SerializedName("gate_repeatable")`).
- `:app/data/Adventure` += `version: Int?`
  (`@SerializedName("version")`), `startScene: String?`
  (`@SerializedName("start_scene")`).
- `EditorScene` += `gateRequiredSteps: Int = 0`,
  `gateRepeatable: Boolean = false` (the editor already has these
  conceptually — `requiredSteps` was for the legacy chapter-level
  gate; move to per-scene).
- `loadFromUri` reads them; `buildAdventure()` writes them.
- UI: a "🎯 Шаговый гейт на этой сцене" checkbox + a steps input,
  mirroring `cb_chapter_end` / `layout_steps` (which currently write
  to `chapter.required_steps` — legacy — and should be **replaced**
  by per-scene `gate`).

**Result:** preview shows the gate indicator for `health_test`
(`gate: 1`), and the editor saves files with `gate` /
`gate_repeatable` / `version` / `start_scene` intact.

**Why not full IR migration now:** `loadFromUri` iterates
`:app/data/Scene` and calls `extractTags(scene, tagDefs)`, which
reads `scene.setFlags` / `removeFlags` / `modifyStats`. IR's
`Scene` has `effects: List<Effect>` instead. Migrating
`loadFromUri` to IR is **~50 lines of logic rewriting**, not a
call-site swap. b2 achieves the observable goal (gates in preview)
without touching that logic. Full migration goes to b3.

**Scope:** ~40 lines, `:app/data/` + `:app/ui/editor/`.
**No unit tests** — `:app/data` is a transitional model that will
be deleted in b3 (after Ф8); unit tests for it would be investment
in throwaway code. Smoke covers it: preview of `health_test`
shows "Пройдено 0 из 1"; editor saves and loads files without
losing `gate` / `gate_repeatable`.

**Depends on:** b1 (independently shippable, but ships right after).

#### b3 — editor on IR; delete `:app/data/Adventure`

**Goal:** the last consumer of `:app/data/Adventure` — the editor
write path — moves to `:engine/ir/Adventure` + `IrToJson` (for
writes) / `JsonToIr.parse` (for reads). `:app/data/Adventure.kt` is
deleted.

**Blocked on:** **Ф8 (`IrToJson`)**. Without an exporter that
serialises IR back to the adventure JSON format (`"has_sword"`,
not `{"type": "has", "name": "sword"}`),
`buildAdventure()` cannot produce a file that `JsonToIr.parse`
will read back. `Adventure.serializer()` is **not** a substitute —
it emits the IR shape, not the adventure shape.

**What it does (after Ф8):**
- `buildAdventure()` returns `:engine/ir/Adventure`; writes via
  `IrToJson.encode(adventure)`.
- `loadFromUri` uses `JsonToIr.parse`; iterates
  `:engine/ir/Chapter` / `:engine/ir/Scene`; `extractTags` reads
  `scene.effects` (`Effect.SetFlag` / `RemoveFlag` / `ModifyStat`).
- `:app/data/Adventure.kt` deleted.

**Pre-written round-trip tests** (in `:engine`, before this
starts):
- `Adventure` (constructed by `test_adventure.json`) →
  `IrToJson.encode` → JSON → `JsonToIr.parse` → IR → structurally
  equal to input.
- These tests will fail to compile before `IrToJson` exists —
  which is exactly the point of "blocked on Ф8".

**Scope:** ~200 lines, 3–4 sections. Requires a **full editor
smoke pass** afterwards: create / load / edit / save / preview /
map / statistics. The editor was not smoke-tested during Ф1.7.1a —
this is the first time we actively test it.

**What NOT to do (for all three):**
- Do not delete `:app/data/Adventure.kt` before b3.
- Do not merge b1 / b2 / b3 into one PR — three independently
  testable steps.
- Do not merge with `format/json/` restructure — different modules,
  different scope.
- Do not write unit tests for `:app/data` in b2 — it is a
  transitional model, deleted in b3.

#### `format/json/` restructure

**Goal:** move JSON-format files under `format/json/` so the
directory layout self-documents the format boundary. No behaviour
change — pure `git mv` + package renames.

**What it touches:**
- `format/JsonToIr.kt` → `format/json/JsonToIr.kt`
- `format/dto/` → `format/json/dto/`
- `format/JsonToIrTest.kt`, `RealAdventureTest.kt`, `GoldenIrTest.kt`,
  `GoldenWriter.kt` → `format/json/`
- `format/SchemaFingerprintTest.kt` → `ir/` — it pins the IR
  schema, not JSON, so it belongs next to the classes it guards.
- `test/resources/golden_ir.json` → `test/resources/json/golden_ir.json`
- `test_adventure.json` is still copied from `:app` — into
  `test/resources/json/`
- `engine/build.gradle.kts`: `processTestResources { into("json") }`;
  `updateGolden` path and `GoldenWriter.GOLDEN_PATH` updated to match.
- Package declarations in the moved files updated
  (`…format` → `…format.json`, `…format.dto` → `…format.json.dto`,
  `SchemaFingerprintTest` → `…ir`).

**What it does NOT change:**
- `ConditionParser` stays in `parse/` — moving it to `ir/` would
  create an `ir → parse` dependency (data depending on parsing
  infrastructure), which inverts the layer direction.
- No `AdventureFormat` / `AdventureImporter` / `FormatDetector`.
  Those are multi-format abstractions (see next entry).
- No `IrToJson`. That arrives with the exporter (Ф8).

**Depends on:** Ф1.7.5 (`is_ending` in the editor) — the same PR
that changes `AdventureEditorViewModel.buildAdventure()` to write
`is_ending` also touches the `:app → :engine` boundary, so doing
`format/json/` in the same window avoids two separate `:app`
round-trips. But they are separate PRs.

**Entry trigger:** immediately after Ф1.7.5 ships. Small, ~1 hour,
no behaviour change (`./gradlew :engine:test` proves it).

#### Multi-format support (Twine / Ink / ChoiceScript)

**Goal:** let Adventure import adventures written in other
gamebook / interactive-fiction formats — Twine (Twee, HTML,
Twison), Ink, ChoiceScript, Yarn, Adventuron.

**Not yet.** This is a **post-Ф10** feature with a concrete trigger:
the first time a real author brings a non-JSON file and asks for
it. Until then, the entire abstraction (`AdventureFormat`,
`AdventureImporter`, `ImportResult`) is designed against **zero**
real formats beyond JSON — the classic YAGNI violation. When the
first non-JSON format arrives, we will have **two** real cases, and
the right abstraction will be obvious; designing now is guessing.

**When the trigger fires, do this** (design reviewed 2026-11-07):

- **Layout: one format = one folder.** `format/json/`, `format/twine/`,
  `format/ink/`. Shared code stays in `format/` (or `format/common/`).
  Do **not** create `parsers/` + `converters/` + `models/` — the
  anti-pattern is a horizontal split that loses the format boundary.
- **`AdventureFormat` interface:** `id: String`,
  `detect(content: String): Boolean` (content sniffing only —
  no hint/extension; those are `AdventureImporter`'s concern),
  `parse(content: String): ImportResult`.
- **`AdventureImporter`:** hint → extension → content sniffing;
  `≥2` detects → `AmbiguousFormat` (never pick silently);
  `0` → `NoFormatFound`.
- **`ImportResult`:** `format`, `adventure: Adventure?`,
  `warnings: List<ImportWarning>`, `errors: List<ImportError>`.
  `ImportError` is **not** `ParseError`: add
  `ImportError.Unsupported(feature, location, detail)` — "parsed
  but IR cannot express" (Twine `<<if>>`, ChoiceScript
  `*gosub_scene`). Wrapping `ParseError.FromParser(errors)` keeps
  parser errors intact.
- **Lossy policy.** Macros → error (not silent loss). Presentation
  (inline HTML/CSS, base64 images) → warning + strip
  (`ImportWarning.PresentationStripped`). Decided inside
  `<Format>ToIr`, never in sub-parsers.
- **Intermediate model** only when (a) the format has >1 sub-format
  (Twee / HTML / Twison) **or** (b) it needs normalisation before IR
  (Ink knot/stitch). Otherwise direct `<Format>ToIr`.
- **`FormatDetector`** is created **only when the second format
  lands** — with one format there is nothing to detect.
- **`docs/import-formats.md`** is written at the same time as the
  first non-JSON format — not before (see
  [`documentation-rules.md`](../documentation-rules.md) on
  not documenting what does not yet exist).

**What NOT to do before the trigger:**
- Do not create empty `twine/`, `ink/` folders "for the future" —
  dead code.
- Do not add `extensions` to IR "so Twine round-trips" — only if a
  concrete round-trip requirement arrives.
- Do not unify the editor write path (`:app/data/Adventure` →
  `:engine/ir/Adventure` + `Adventure.serializer()`) as part of
  multi-format work — that is Ф1.7.5's job, done already.
- Do not build `IrToJson` before Ф8 (export).

**Entry trigger:** a real author brings a non-JSON file. Not
before.

**Depends on:** Ф10 (checklist accepted) **and** the trigger above.

## Part 3 — Distribution / community

Not a phase; a set of decisions that open after acceptance (Ф10).

- **E3 Mobile distribution** — Play Store and F-Droid. Needs: signed
  release build, privacy policy, store screenshots. Triggers only after
  Ф10 + a stable `docs/` set (X3.base from Ф10 already covers this).
- **E4 Steam** — only if E1.base (single-file HTML) returns to scope.
  Without a JS runtime, there is no Steam build.
- **Community docs** — see X3.advanced in Part 2. Only when contributors
  ask for a wiki or forum; a pre-alpha project does not need a community
  platform.

No dates. No promises. Every item here is triggered by a concrete
question, not by a calendar.

## How to update this file

- **Add a mechanic to Ф12–Ф18** — first add the mechanic to
  [`research/gamebook-mechanics.md`](./research/gamebook-mechanics.md),
  then add the status row to
  [`gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md`](./gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md)
  with "Planned: Фxx" — this roadmap already has the phase.
  Only if the mechanic does not fit **any** phase, add a new phase here.
- **Change a phase's content** — update the phase table; also update
  the "Unlocks" list; also update the corresponding rows in
  [`gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md`](./gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md)
  so the roadmap and coverage map stay in sync.
- **Close a phase's gate** — add an entry to
  [`progress/progress-log.md`](./progress/progress-log.md); update the
  affected rows in coverage map from "Planned: Фxx" to "Supported".
- **Add a Nice-to-have** — add a row to Part 2 with its trigger;
  if the Nice-to-have implies new code in `:engine`, add a phase.
- **Promote a Nice-to-have into a phase** — move the row from Part 2
  to the appropriate phase; update coverage map if it unlocks a mechanic.
