package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition

/**
 * Parses a condition string into a [Condition] AST node.
 *
 * **Syntactic only.** This parser knows nothing about variable types or
 * declared variables — that is the type checker's job (Ф2.2). It accepts
 * `has_sword` and produces [Condition.Has] even if `sword` is declared as
 * `ItemCount`; Ф2.2 rejects that with a hint to use `sword > 0` instead.
 *
 * **Grammar (Ф3.2 / N7.base):**
 *
 * ```
 * expr    = or
 * or      = and ("||" and)*
 * and     = not ("&&" not)*
 * not     = "!" not | primary
 * primary = "(" expr ")"
 *         | "true"
 *         | "false"
 *         | "has_" IDENT
 *         | IDENT "in" INT ".." INT
 *         | IDENT COMPARE_OP INT
 * ```
 *
 * **Precedence:** `!` (highest) > `&&` > `||` (lowest). `&&` and `||`
 * are **left-associative**: `a && b && c` parses as `And(And(a, b), c)`,
 * same for `||`.
 *
 * **Associativity and round-trip with [ConditionWriter].**
 * [ConditionWriter] produces a canonical minimal-bracket form; this
 * parser accepts it back. `parse(write(c))` is structurally equal to `c`
 * for the variants listed below.
 *
 * **Round-trip status (as of Ф3.2):**
 *
 * | Variant | Round-trips |
 * |---|---|
 * | `Has`, `Not(Has)`, `Compare` (all 6 ops) | ✅ |
 * | `And`, `Or`, `Not(And)`, `Not(Or)`, `Not(Compare)`, `!!`, `InRange`, `Literal` | ✅ |
 * | `VarRef` | ❌ — not produced by the parser, see below |
 *
 * **`VarRef` is deliberately NOT parsed in Ф3.2.** Bare identifiers
 * (e.g. `"health"`, `"sword && key"` where `sword` / `key` are Bool
 * flags) are parsed as `ConditionError`. Reason: accepting a bare name
 * would be ambiguous with `has_X` (an author with a variable named
 * `has_seen` would have no way to reference it — parser would see
 * `Has("seen")`). `VarRef` is planned for a future phase (see roadmap /
 * progress log), along with `TypeError.VarRefOnNonBool` and the
 * `has_`-prefix reservation. Until then: `has_X` is the only way to
 * reference a Bool variable, and that is the canonical syntax authors
 * have been using since Ф1.3.
 *
 * **Reserved characters.** Flag names (`has_X`) and variable names in
 * `X in A..B` / `X op N` must not contain `&`, `|`, `!`, `<`, `>`, `=`,
 * `(`, `)`. These are part of the condition syntax. A name containing
 * one → `ConditionError` with a fix hint. This catches `has_sword &&
 * health` if the author meant `has_sword && has_health`.
 *
 * **Not supported yet (post-Ф3.2):** `VarRef` (bare Bool reference);
 * `Set`/`Add`/`Sub` as effects (those are not conditions — `ConditionParser`
 * is condition-only); `roll(...)` (Ф12, RNG).
 */
public object ConditionParser {

    /**
     * Parses [input] as a single condition.
     *
     * @return [ParseResult.Success] with the AST node, or
     *   [ParseResult.Failure] with exactly one [ParseError.ConditionError].
     */
    public fun parse(input: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val s = input.trim()
        if (s.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Empty condition string", input, 0)
        }
        return parseExpr(s, input)
    }

    // ---------- Grammar ----------

    private fun parseExpr(text: String, original: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val orParts = splitTopLevel(text, "||")
        if (orParts.size > 1) {
            val conditions = mutableListOf<Condition>()
            for (part in orParts) {
                val trimmed = part.trim()
                if (trimmed.isEmpty()) {
                    return fail("Empty operand of '||' in '$original'", original, 0)
                }
                when (val r = parseAnd(trimmed, original)) {
                    is ParseResult.Success -> conditions.add(r.value)
                    is ParseResult.Failure -> return r
                }
            }
            var result = conditions[0]
            for (i in 1 until conditions.size) {
                result = Condition.Or(result, conditions[i])
            }
            return ParseResult.Success(result)
        }
        return parseAnd(text, original)
    }

    private fun parseAnd(text: String, original: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val andParts = splitTopLevel(text, "&&")
        if (andParts.size > 1) {
            val conditions = mutableListOf<Condition>()
            for (part in andParts) {
                val trimmed = part.trim()
                if (trimmed.isEmpty()) {
                    return fail("Empty operand of '&&' in '$original'", original, 0)
                }
                when (val r = parseNot(trimmed, original)) {
                    is ParseResult.Success -> conditions.add(r.value)
                    is ParseResult.Failure -> return r
                }
            }
            var result = conditions[0]
            for (i in 1 until conditions.size) {
                result = Condition.And(result, conditions[i])
            }
            return ParseResult.Success(result)
        }
        return parseNot(text, original)
    }

    private fun parseNot(text: String, original: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val trimmed = text.trim()
        if (trimmed.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Empty condition in '$original'", original, 0)
        }
        if (trimmed.startsWith("!") && !trimmed.startsWith("!=")) {
            val inner = trimmed.substring(1).trim()
            if (inner.isEmpty()) {
                return fail("Missing operand after '!' in '$original'", original, 0)
            }
            return when (val r = parseNot(inner, original)) {
                is ParseResult.Success -> ParseResult.Success(Condition.Not(r.value))
                is ParseResult.Failure -> r
            }
        }
        return parsePrimary(trimmed, original)
    }

    private fun parsePrimary(text: String, original: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val trimmed = text.trim()
        if (trimmed.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Empty condition in '$original'", original, 0)
        }

        // Parentheses
        if (trimmed.startsWith("(")) {
            if (!trimmed.endsWith(")")) {
                return fail("Unclosed parenthesis in '$original'", original, 0)
            }
            if (!isMatchingParens(trimmed)) {
                return fail(
                    "Parentheses in '$trimmed' do not form a single group. " +
                            "If you meant to join multiple conditions, use '&&' or '||'.",
                    original,
                    0,
                )
            }
            return parseExpr(trimmed.substring(1, trimmed.length - 1), original)
        }

        // Literal
        if (trimmed == "true") return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Literal(true))
        if (trimmed == "false") return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Literal(false))

        // has_X
        if (trimmed.startsWith("has_")) {
            val name = trimmed.removePrefix("has_").trim()
            if (name.isEmpty()) {
                return fail("Missing variable name after 'has_' in '$original'", original, 0)
            }
            checkNoReservedChars(name, original, "Flag name")?.let { return it }
            return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Has(name))
        }

        // InRange: X in A..B
        val inRangeMatch = IN_RANGE_REGEX.find(trimmed)
        if (inRangeMatch != null) {
            val varName = inRangeMatch.groupValues[1].trim()
            if (varName.isEmpty()) {
                return fail("Missing variable name before 'in' in '$original'", original, 0)
            }
            checkNoReservedChars(varName, original, "Variable name")?.let { return it }
            val minStr = inRangeMatch.groupValues[2]
            val maxStr = inRangeMatch.groupValues[3]
            val min = minStr.toIntOrNull()
                ?: return fail("Expected integer after 'in', got '$minStr' in '$original'", original, 0)
            val max = maxStr.toIntOrNull()
                ?: return fail("Expected integer after '..', got '$maxStr' in '$original'", original, 0)
            return ParseResult.Success(Condition.InRange(varName, min, max))
        }

        // Compare: X <op> N. Two-char ops first so `>=` is not consumed as `>` + `=`.
        val compareOps = listOf(
            ">=" to CompareOp.GE,
            "<=" to CompareOp.LE,
            "==" to CompareOp.EQ,
            "!=" to CompareOp.NE,
            ">" to CompareOp.GT,
            "<" to CompareOp.LT,
        )
        for ((opStr, op) in compareOps) {
            val idx = trimmed.indexOf(opStr)
            if (idx <= 0) continue
            val varName = trimmed.substring(0, idx).trim()
            val valueStr = trimmed.substring(idx + opStr.length).trim()
            val value = valueStr.toIntOrNull() ?: continue
            if (varName.isEmpty()) continue
            checkNoReservedChars(varName, original, "Variable name")?.let { return it }
            return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Compare(varName, op, value))
        }

        return fail(
            "Unrecognized condition syntax: '$trimmed'. " +
                    "Expected one of: 'has_X', '!has_X', 'X <op> N', " +
                    "'X in A..B', 'true', 'false', a parenthesized expression, " +
                    "or '&&' / '||' joining any two of the above.",
            original,
            0,
        )
    }

    // ---------- Helpers ----------

    private val IN_RANGE_REGEX = Regex("""^(.+?)\s+in\s+(-?\d+)\s*\.\.\s*(-?\d+)$""")

    /**
     * Splits [input] by [op] at the top parenthesis level. `||` / `&&`
     * inside `(...)` do not split the outer expression:
     * `(a || b) && c` splits only by `&&`.
     */
    private fun splitTopLevel(input: String, op: String): List<String> {
        val parts = mutableListOf<String>()
        var depth = 0
        var start = 0
        var i = 0
        while (i < input.length) {
            when (input[i]) {
                '(' -> { depth++; i++ }
                ')' -> { depth--; i++ }
                else -> {
                    if (depth == 0 && input.startsWith(op, i)) {
                        parts.add(input.substring(start, i))
                        i += op.length
                        start = i
                    } else {
                        i++
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        parts.add(input.substring(start))
        return parts
    }

    /**
     * True iff [s] starts with `(`, ends with `)`, and the opening `(`
     * matches the final `)`. `"(a) && (b)"` returns false — the first
     * `(` matches the `)` at index 2, not the last `)`.
     */
    private fun isMatchingParens(s: String): Boolean {
        if (!s.startsWith("(") || !s.endsWith(")")) return false
        var depth = 0
        for (i in s.indices) {
            when (s[i]) {
                '(' -> depth++
                ')' -> {
                    depth--
                    if (depth == 0 && i < s.length - 1) return false
                }
            }
        }
        return depth == 0
    }

    private val RESERVED_CHARS: Set<Char> = setOf('&', '|', '!', '<', '>', '=', '(', ')')

    private fun checkNoReservedChars(
        value: String,
        input: String,
        forWhat: String,
    ): ParseResult.Failure? {
        val bad = value.firstOrNull { it in RESERVED_CHARS }
        if (bad != null) {
            return fail(
                "$forWhat '$value' contains reserved character '$bad'. " +
                        "Logical operators (&&, ||, !), comparisons, and parentheses " +
                        "are part of the condition syntax, not the variable name.",
                input,
                0,
            )
        }
        return null
    }

    private fun fail(message: String, input: String, position: Int): ParseResult.Failure =
        ParseResult.Failure(listOf(ParseError.ConditionError(message, input, position)))
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition

/**
 * Writes a [Condition] AST back into a string in the format accepted by
 * [ConditionParser].
 *
 * **Symmetry with [ConditionParser].** The two objects form a round-trip:
 * for a condition that the parser can produce today, `parse(write(c)) ==
 * c` (structurally). This is the contract that makes the editor (Ф9.2)
 * able to represent a condition in JSON: the editor holds a
 * `Condition` in memory, and when the author saves, [write] serializes
 * it back into the `"condition"` field. If the two sides did not
 * round-trip, saving a file would silently change the meaning of a
 * condition — the worst possible failure mode.
 *
 * **What round-trips today.** Only the variants the parser produces:
 * - [Condition.Has]
 * - [Condition.Not]`(`[Condition.Has]`)`
 * - [Condition.Compare] (all 6 [CompareOp] values)
 *
 * **What does NOT round-trip today** (writer produces a string, parser
 * rejects it):
 * - [Condition.And] → `"a && b"` (parser: `&` is a reserved char).
 * - [Condition.Or] → `"a || b"` (`|` is reserved).
 * - [Condition.Not] where the inner is not `Has` — e.g.
 *   `Not(Compare(...))` → `"!(health >= 50)"` (parser: `!` only
 *   recognized as `!has_`).
 * - `Not(Not(...))` → `"!!has_x"` (parser: `!!` not recognized).
 * - [Condition.Literal] → `"true"` / `"false"` (no literal syntax).
 * - [Condition.VarRef] → bare name, e.g. `"sword"` (parser: a bare
 *   name without an operator is `ConditionError`).
 * - [Condition.InRange] → `"x in 0..10"` (parser: `in` / `..` not
 *   supported yet).
 *
 * These are all resolved by **Ф3.2 (N7.base)**, which extends
 * [ConditionParser] with `&&`, `||`, `!`, parentheses, and `X in a..b`.
 * The writer's output for these variants is already **canonical** — it
 * is the syntax that Ф3.2 will accept. Tests in
 * [ConditionWriterTest] pin both the string output (which is already
 * correct) and the current round-trip failure (which will flip to
 * success when Ф3.2 lands).
 *
 * **Canonical form.** The writer produces the **minimal-bracket** form
 * that respects precedence: `!` (highest) > `&&` > `||` (lowest).
 * Leaves ([Condition.Has], [Condition.Compare], [Condition.InRange],
 * [Condition.Literal], [Condition.VarRef]) are always at the top, no
 * brackets around them.
 *
 * For example:
 * - `And(Has("a"), Or(Has("b"), Has("c")))` → `"has_a && (has_b || has_c)"`.
 * - `Or(And(Has("a"), Has("b")), Has("c"))` → `"has_a && has_b || has_c"`.
 * - `Not(And(Has("a"), Has("b")))` → `"!(has_a && has_b)"`.
 * - `And(And(Has("a"), Has("b")), Has("c"))` → `"has_a && has_b && has_c"`
 *   (associative, no extra brackets).
 *
 * **What is NOT the writer's job.**
 * - **No simplification.** `And(Literal(true), Has("x"))` is written as
 *   `"true && has_x"`, not `"has_x"`. Simplification is a separate
 *   concern (`ConditionSimplifier`, future — Ф3.2 or later).
 * - **No effect writing.** `Effect` AST → string (the `"set_flags"` /
 *   `"modify_stats"` fields) is `IrToJson` (Ф8), not this writer.
 * - **No whitespace preferences.** `"a && b"` (single spaces) is what
 *   the writer produces; the parser accepts any whitespace. The writer
 *   is canonical, the parser is lenient.
 *
 * **Known corner case** (documented, not fixed): a variable whose name
 * starts with `"has_"` cannot be referenced from [Condition.VarRef] or
 * [Condition.Compare] unambiguously — the parser will interpret
 * `"has_x"` as `Has("x")`, not as `VarRef("has_x")` or as the start of a
 * comparison. This is a naming collision in the author's file, not a bug
 * in the writer. Ф3.2 will define the disambiguation rule (probably:
 * reserved prefix, rejected by [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeChecker]).
 */
public object ConditionWriter {

    /**
     * Serializes [condition] into the condition-string format accepted
     * by [ConditionParser.parse].
     *
     * The output is **canonical**: single spaces around binary operators,
     * no trailing whitespace, minimal brackets (only where precedence
     * requires them).
     */
    public fun write(condition: Condition): String =
        writeWithPrecedence(condition, minPrecedence = PREC_OR)

    // ---------- Precedence ----------

    /** Leaves: no internal boolean operators. */
    private const val PREC_LEAF = 3

    /** Unary prefix `!`. */
    private const val PREC_NOT = 2

    /** `&&`. */
    private const val PREC_AND = 1

    /** `||`. */
    private const val PREC_OR = 0

    private fun precedence(c: Condition): Int = when (c) {
        is Condition.Literal,
        is Condition.VarRef,
        is Condition.Has,
        is Condition.Compare,
        is Condition.InRange,
            -> PREC_LEAF
        is Condition.Not -> PREC_NOT
        is Condition.And -> PREC_AND
        is Condition.Or -> PREC_OR
    }

    // ---------- Core writer ----------

    /**
     * Writes [c] and, if its precedence is **strictly lower** than
     * [minPrecedence], wraps the result in `(…)`.
     *
     * Precedence is a partial order: `!` > `&&` > `||`. A child whose
     * precedence equals the parent's does **not** get brackets — `&&`
     * and `||` are associative, so `a && b && c` is unambiguous
     * regardless of the tree shape.
     */
    private fun writeWithPrecedence(c: Condition, minPrecedence: Int): String {
        val body = when (c) {
            is Condition.Literal -> if (c.value) "true" else "false"
            is Condition.VarRef -> c.name
            is Condition.Has -> "has_${c.name}"
            is Condition.Compare -> "${c.varName} ${opSymbol(c.op)} ${c.value}"
            is Condition.InRange -> "${c.varName} in ${c.min}..${c.max}"
            is Condition.Not -> "!" + writeNotChild(c.inner)
            is Condition.And ->
                writeWithPrecedence(c.left, PREC_AND) + " && " +
                        writeWithPrecedence(c.right, PREC_AND)
            is Condition.Or ->
                writeWithPrecedence(c.left, PREC_OR) + " || " +
                        writeWithPrecedence(c.right, PREC_OR)
        }
        return if (precedence(c) < minPrecedence) "($body)" else body
    }

    /**
     * Writes the child of a `!` prefix.
     *
     * Precedence alone is **not** enough for this position. `!` is a
     * prefix operator, and `!x > 5` reads as `(!x) > 5` in most
     * languages, not `!(x > 5)`. Bracket decisions are therefore made
     * per-variant, not by precedence:
     *
     * - `Has`, `VarRef`, `Literal`, `Not` → **no brackets**
     *   (`!has_x`, `!x`, `!true`, `!!y` — all unambiguous).
     * - `Compare`, `InRange`, `And`, `Or` → **brackets**
     *   (`!(x >= 5)`, `!(x in 0..10)`, `!(a && b)`, `!(a || b)` — a
     *   bare `!` would bind to the first token of the child, not the
     *   whole expression).
     *
     * `Not` recurses here rather than via `writeWithPrecedence` so that
     * `Not(Not(Has("a")))` produces `"!!has_a"` (no parenthesised
     * `"!(!has_a)"`), which is the canonical form the parser will
     * accept once Ф3.2 supports `!!`.
     */
    private fun writeNotChild(c: Condition): String = when (c) {
        is Condition.Has -> "has_${c.name}"
        is Condition.VarRef -> c.name
        is Condition.Literal -> if (c.value) "true" else "false"
        is Condition.Not -> "!" + writeNotChild(c.inner)
        is Condition.Compare, is Condition.InRange, is Condition.And, is Condition.Or ->
            "(" + writeWithPrecedence(c, PREC_OR) + ")"
    }

    // ---------- Operator symbols ----------

    private fun opSymbol(op: CompareOp): String = when (op) {
        CompareOp.LT -> "<"
        CompareOp.LE -> "<="
        CompareOp.GT -> ">"
        CompareOp.GE -> ">="
        CompareOp.EQ -> "=="
        CompareOp.NE -> "!="
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

/**
 * A single error produced by the JSON parser ([JsonToIr]) or by the
 * condition parser ([ConditionParser]).
 *
 * The parser never throws. It accumulates errors and returns them all at
 * once in [ParseResult.Failure], so that the editor and the analyzer can
 * show the author every problem in one pass instead of one at a time.
 *
 * **Not** `@Serializable`: parse errors are an API for the caller, not part
 * of the on-disk format. If they ever need to be persisted (e.g. in a
 * validation report), serialize them separately.
 */
public sealed class ParseError {

    /** Human-readable, English, one sentence. */
    public abstract val message: String

    /**
     * JSON-level syntax error: malformed input, unknown field with
     * strict mode, wrong type for a well-known field.
     *
     * @property path JSON path to the offending value
     *   (e.g. `"chapters[0].scenes[2].choices[0].condition"`), when known.
     */
    public data class Syntax(
        override val message: String,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()

    /**
     * Structural problem that is not a JSON syntax error: empty chapter
     * list, blank scene id, empty `next_scene`, etc.
     *
     * @property path same convention as [Syntax.path].
     */
    public data class Structure(
        override val message: String,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()

    /**
     * Condition string could not be parsed into
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition].
     *
     * @property input the raw condition string from JSON.
     * @property position 0-based offset in [input] where the parser gave up,
     *   when determinable.
     * @property path JSON path to the offending condition
     *   (e.g. `"chapters[1:c2].scenes[0:start].choices[2].condition"`),
     *   filled in by [JsonToIr] when accumulating errors. `null` when the
     *   error came from a standalone [ConditionParser] call.
     */
    public data class ConditionError(
        override val message: String,
        public val input: String,
        public val position: Int? = null,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeError

/**
 * Result of a parse operation: either a value of type [T] or an error
 * describing why parsing failed.
 *
 * Chosen over Kotlin's stdlib [Result] because:
 * - [Result.Failure] carries a single [Throwable], not a list of errors.
 * - Wrapping [ParseError] in an exception would lose the structured type
 *   (the caller wants to pattern-match on [ParseError.ConditionError] etc.).
 *
 * **Two-stage pipeline (Ф2.3).** Starting with Ф2.3,
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr.parse] performs **two**
 * checks in sequence:
 * 1. **Parse** (JSON syntax, structural problems, condition syntax) —
 *    produces [ParseError]s.
 * 2. **Type check** ([com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeChecker.check],
 *    Ф2.2) — unknown variables, wrong types — produces
 *    [TypeError]s.
 *
 * The two stages are sequential and mutually exclusive in [Failure]:
 * - if parsing fails, type checking is **not attempted** — a partial IR
 *   has missing conditions and effects (a choice whose condition string
 *   failed to parse has `condition = null`), so type checking it would
 *   produce false negatives at best, and false positives at worst. Result:
 *   `Failure(errors = [...], typeErrors = emptyList())`.
 * - if parsing succeeds, type checking runs on the full IR. Result:
 *   `Success(ir)` when there are no type errors, or
 *   `Failure(errors = emptyList(), typeErrors = [...])` otherwise.
 *
 * **Invariant (enforced in `init`):** [Failure] contains **exactly one**
 * non-empty list — either [Failure.errors] or [Failure.typeErrors].
 * Both empty would be a `Success`; both non-empty would mean the two
 * stages overlapped, which contradicts the sequential design.
 *
 * **Why not a single `List<ParseError>` that includes type errors as a
 * variant.** The two error kinds come from different layers of the
 * pipeline (parser vs type checker) and carry different structured data
 * ([ParseError] has JSON paths and condition fragments; [TypeError] has
 * variable names and types). Merging them into one list would blur the
 * I3 boundary between "the file cannot be parsed" and "the file parses,
 * but its variable references are wrong". Two fields keep the boundary
 * visible in the type system.
 */
public sealed class ParseResult<out T> {

    /** Successful parse + type check. */
    public data class Success<T>(public val value: T) : ParseResult<T>()

    /**
     * Failed parse or failed type check.
     *
     * @property errors JSON syntax / structural / condition-syntax errors,
     *   produced by the parser. Non-empty iff parsing failed.
     * @property typeErrors type errors from
     *   [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeChecker.check], produced
     *   after a fully successful parse. Non-empty iff parsing succeeded
     *   but the IR has semantic problems. See class KDoc for the pipeline.
     *
     * **Exactly one** of [errors] / [typeErrors] is non-empty; enforced by
     * the `init` block below.
     */
    public data class Failure(
        public val errors: List<ParseError>,
        public val typeErrors: List<TypeError> = emptyList(),
    ) : ParseResult<Nothing>() {
        init {
            require(errors.isNotEmpty() || typeErrors.isNotEmpty()) {
                "ParseResult.Failure must contain at least one error in " +
                        "`errors` (parse) or `typeErrors` (type check)"
            }
            require(!(errors.isNotEmpty() && typeErrors.isNotEmpty())) {
                "ParseResult.Failure must not contain both parse errors and type errors: " +
                        "type checking runs only on a fully parsed IR (Ф2.3 / B1 decision). " +
                        "Got ${errors.size} parse errors and ${typeErrors.size} type errors."
            }
        }
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.AdventureDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.ChapterDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.ChoiceDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.SceneDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.DeathScene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagDefinition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Gate
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.ChoiceTemplateDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.InvariantDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.VarDeclDto

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceTemplate
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseError

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeChecker
import kotlinx.serialization.SerializationException
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId

/**
 * Parses the adventure JSON file into the typed IR ([Adventure]).
 *
 * **Single entry point for JSON → IR.** This is the only public function
 * in `:engine` that turns raw JSON text into an [Adventure]. It is used by:
 * - the reader (`:app`, Ф1.7) to load an adventure for playing;
 * - the editor (`:app`, Ф9.2) to validate an author's in-progress JSON;
 * - the analyzer (Ф1.6) after parsing, to check reachability and duplicates;
 * - tests (`:engine`, Ф1.3.4, Ф1.4), including the real `test_adventure.json`
 *   shipped to users.
 *
 * Do **not** write a second parser alongside this one. If a new format is
 * needed (YAML, binary, a future JS runtime), either add a `parse` overload
 * here or create a new top-level `object <Format>ToIr` with the same
 * `ParseResult<Adventure>` contract. Two parsers with divergent behaviour
 * is exactly the bug N2/Ф3 exists to prevent.
 *
 * **Parser vs Analyzer boundary** (do not blur this):
 * - **Parser** (this object): "can the file be turned into an
 *   [Adventure]?" — syntax of JSON, syntax of conditions, blank required
 *   fields, empty chapters. Nothing about the **meaning** of the file.
 * - **Analyzer** (Ф1.6): "is the resulting IR coherent?" — reachability,
 *   duplicate `scene.id`, `next_scene` pointing to a missing scene,
 *   `has_X` on a numeric variable (type checker, Ф2.2).
 *
 * Consequence: a JSON file that parses **successfully** may still be
 * rejected by the analyzer. That is by design — the two layers answer
 * different questions, and mixing them would make both harder to test.
 *
 * **Error strategy** (decision B from Ф1.3.3):
 * - **JSON syntax errors** (malformed JSON, wrong type for a field) — the
 *   underlying decoder throws `SerializationException`; we catch it once
 *   and return a single [ParseError.Syntax]. These are rare in practice:
 *   the editor always emits valid JSON, authors do not hand-write it.
 * - **Semantic errors** (blank ids, empty chapters, unparseable
 *   conditions) — accumulated into a [ParseResult.Failure] with **all**
 *   errors at once. Authors see every problem in one pass, not one at a
 *   time. This is the common case, so it is worth the extra code.
 *
 * **`path` convention:** `chapters[i:<id>].scenes[j:<id>].choices[k]`,
 * with `:<id>` omitted when the id is blank. Example:
 * `chapters[1:forest].scenes[0:start].choices[2]`. The author sees the
 * chapter and scene by name in the editor error panel (Ф9.2), not just
 * an index.
 *
 * **Not in scope here** (deferred):
 * - Type checking of variables (`has_X` on numeric variable) — Ф2.2.
 * - Duplicate `scene.id` detection — Ф2 / `Analyzer`.
 * - `next_scene` reachability — Ф2 / `Analyzer`.
 * - Migration of `version < CURRENT_VERSION` — Ф5.3 (for now, files with
 *   no `version` get [Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION]; files with any `version`
 *   keep it as-is).
 */
public object JsonToIr {

    private val json: Json = Json {
        ignoreUnknownKeys = true
        coerceInputValues = true
    }

    /**
     * Parses [text] (raw JSON contents of an adventure file) into an
     * [Adventure], or returns [ParseResult.Failure] with one or more
     * [ParseError]s.
     */
    public fun parse(text: String): ParseResult<Adventure> {
        val dto: AdventureDto = try {
            json.decodeFromString<AdventureDto>(text)
        } catch (e: SerializationException) {
            return ParseResult.Failure(
                listOf(
                    ParseError.Syntax(
                        message = "Malformed JSON: ${e.message ?: "unknown syntax error"}",
                        path = null,
                    ),
                ),
            )
        }

        val errors = mutableListOf<ParseError>()
        val adventure = buildAdventure(dto, errors)
        if (errors.isNotEmpty()) {
            // B1 decision (Ф2.3): if parsing failed, type checking is not
            // attempted. The partial IR produced above has missing
            // conditions / effects (a choice whose condition string failed
            // to parse has `condition = null`), so type checking it would
            // produce false negatives (unchecked paths) at best, and false
            // positives at worst. The author must fix the parse errors
            // first, then rerun.
            return ParseResult.Failure(errors)
        }
        // Ф2.3: type check the fully-parsed IR. TypeChecker is the "second
        // stage" of the pipeline (I3 invariant in architecture.md), and
        // it is the **only** place where unknown variables / wrong types
        // are caught. After this call, the caller (reader, editor,
        // analyzer) receives either Success (fully valid) or Failure with
        // `typeErrors` (fully parsed, but semantically wrong).
        val typeErrors = TypeChecker.check(adventure)
        return if (typeErrors.isEmpty()) {
            ParseResult.Success(adventure)
        } else {
            ParseResult.Failure(emptyList(), typeErrors)
        }
    }

    // ---------- DTO → IR ----------

    private fun buildAdventure(
        dto: AdventureDto,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): Adventure {
        if (dto.chapters.isEmpty()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Adventure has no chapters",
                path = null,
            )
        }
        // Version migration (v1 → v2, Ф1.5.4): gates moved from chapters
        // to scenes. A v1 file has `chapter.required_steps`; the migration
        // moves `chapter[i].required_steps = N > 0` onto the **last scene
        // of chapter i-1** as `Gate(N)`. The first chapter's
        // `required_steps` is dropped (it was always 0 in practice; even if
        // set, there is no "previous chapter" to gate).
        //
        // Files without `version` (pre-IR) are treated as v1 — same
        // migration. Files with `version >= 2` have `required_steps` on
        // chapters only as a leftover; we ignore it (it should be absent in
        // a well-formed v2 file).
        val effectiveVersion = dto.version ?: 1
        val lastChapterIndex = dto.chapters.lastIndex
        val chapters = dto.chapters.mapIndexed { index, chapterDto ->
            buildChapter(
                dto = chapterDto,
                index = index,
                errors = errors,
                // v1 → v2: `chapter[i].required_steps = N > 0` means
                // "walk N steps to enter chapter i". In v2 the gate lives
                // on the **last scene of chapter i-1** (the scene the player
                // must leave to enter chapter i). So for chapter `index`
                // we pass `required_steps` of chapter `index + 1`.
                previousChapterLastSceneGate = if (index < lastChapterIndex && effectiveVersion < 2) {
                    dto.chapters[index + 1].requiredSteps
                        .takeIf { it > 0 }
                        ?.let { Gate(it) }
                } else {
                    null
                },
            )
        }
        val deathScene = dto.deathScene?.let { d ->
            DeathScene(
                id = SceneId(d.id),
                text = d.text,
                allowStepBack = d.allowStepBack,
                allowChapterRestart = d.allowChapterRestart,
                allowAdventureRestart = d.allowAdventureRestart,
            )
        }
        // start_scene: explicit since v3; migrated from chapters in v1/v2.
        // - explicit value wins (v3+);
        // - v1/v2 without explicit value: infer from chapters;
        // - v3+ without explicit value: structural error (the field is
        //   required from v3 onward); fall back to SceneId("") so that
        //   Adventure can still be constructed, but `errors` is non-empty,
        //   so `JsonToIr.parse` returns Failure and the IR is not used.
        val startScene = dto.startScene?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { SceneId(it) }
            ?: if (effectiveVersion < 3) {
                chapters.firstOrNull()?.scenes?.firstOrNull()?.id ?: SceneId("")
            } else {
                errors += ParseError.Structure(
                    message = "Adventure has no start_scene (required since v3)",
                    path = null,
                )
                SceneId("")
            }
        val choiceTemplates = dto.choiceTemplates.mapIndexed { i, t ->
            buildChoiceTemplate(t, "choice_templates[$i]", errors)
        }
        val duplicateTemplateIds = choiceTemplates
            .groupBy { it.id }
            .filter { it.value.size > 1 }
            .keys
        duplicateTemplateIds.forEach { id ->
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Duplicate choice template id '$id'",
                path = "choice_templates",
            )
        }
        return Adventure(
            version = dto.version ?: Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION,
            title = dto.title,
            author = dto.author,
            description = dto.description,
            variables = dto.variables.mapValues { (name, vDto) ->
                VarDecl(name, vDto.toVarType())
            },
            choiceTemplates = choiceTemplates,
            invariants = dto.invariants.mapIndexedNotNull { index, invDto ->
                buildInvariant(invDto, index, errors)
            },
            tags = dto.tags.map { t ->
                TagDefinition(
                    name = t.name,
                    displayName = t.displayName,
                    category = t.category,
                    visible = t.visible,
                )
            },
            initialState = InitialState(
                flags = dto.initialState.flags,
                stats = dto.initialState.stats,
            ),
            deathScene = deathScene,
            startScene = startScene,
            chapters = chapters,
        )
    }

    private fun buildChapter(
        dto: ChapterDto,
        index: Int,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
        /**
         * v1 → v2 migration: a non-null gate to attach to the **last scene**
         * of this chapter. This comes from `chapter[index+1].required_steps`
         * in a v1 file, or from `null` for v2 files (and for the last
         * chapter).
         */
        previousChapterLastSceneGate: Gate? = null,
    ): Chapter {
        val path = chapterPath(index, dto.id)
        if (dto.scenes.isEmpty()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Chapter has no scenes",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        val lastIndex = dto.scenes.lastIndex
        val scenes = dto.scenes.mapIndexed { sceneIndex, sceneDto ->
            val built = buildScene(sceneDto, path, sceneIndex, errors)
            // Apply v1 → v2 migration gate on the last scene of this chapter
            // (if any). A scene that already has its own gate wins — the
            // author's intent (v2) overrides the legacy (v1) interpretation.
            if (sceneIndex == lastIndex && previousChapterLastSceneGate != null && built.gate == null) {
                built.copy(gate = previousChapterLastSceneGate)
            } else {
                built
            }
        }
        return Chapter(
            id = dto.id,
            title = dto.title,
            scenes = scenes,
        )
    }

    private fun buildScene(
        dto: SceneDto,
        parentPath: String,
        index: Int,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): Scene {
        val path = scenePath(parentPath, index, dto.id)
        if (dto.id.isBlank()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Scene id is blank",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        val effects = buildEffects(dto.setFlags, dto.removeFlags, dto.modifyStats)
        val choices = dto.choices.mapIndexed { choiceIndex, choiceDto ->
            buildChoice(choiceDto, dto.id, path, choiceIndex, errors)
        }
        val gate = dto.gate?.let { raw ->
            if (raw <= 0) {
                errors += ParseError.Structure(
                    message = "Scene gate must be a positive number of steps, got $raw",
                    path = "$path.gate",
                )
                null
            } else {
                // Ф1.7.0.4: identity migration v4 → v5. Old files have no
                // gate_repeatable; default is "once passed, stays passed
                // for this playthrough" — the least surprising mode for the
                // common "unlock the next chapter" case. Per-visit behaviour
                // is opt-in via "gate_repeatable": true.
                Gate(requiredSteps = raw, repeatable = dto.gateRepeatable ?: false)
            }
        }
        return Scene(
            id = SceneId(dto.id),
            text = dto.text,
            effects = effects,
            choices = choices,
            gate = gate,
            // Ф1.7.0: identity migration v3 → v4. Files that predate v4
            // have no is_ending field; treat as false. Files that carry
            // it use the value as written.
            isEnding = dto.isEnding ?: false,
            // Ф4.5: identity migration — absent merge / merge_sources
            // default to false / emptyList. Cross-scene validation of
            // `mergeSources` lives in `Engine.compile` (a reference to a
            // missing scene is a `CompileError`, not a `ParseError` —
            // same layer as `MissingNextScene`).
            isMerge = dto.merge ?: false,
            mergeSources = dto.mergeSources.map { SceneId(it) },
        )
    }

    private fun buildChoice(
        dto: ChoiceDto,
        sceneId: String,
        parentPath: String,
        index: Int,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): Choice {
        val path = "$parentPath.choices[$index]"
        if (dto.text.isBlank()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Choice text is blank",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        if (dto.nextScene.isBlank()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Choice next_scene is blank",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        val condition = dto.condition?.let { raw ->
            parseCondition(raw, "$path.condition", errors)
        }
        val effects = buildEffects(dto.setFlags, dto.removeFlags, dto.modifyStats)
        val choiceId = dto.id?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
            ?.let { ChoiceId(it) }
            ?: ChoiceId("${sceneId}_choice_$index")
        return Choice(
            id = choiceId,
            text = dto.text,
            nextScene = SceneId(dto.nextScene),
            condition = condition,
            effects = effects,
        )
    }

    /**
     * Flattens the three parallel JSON fields into a single ordered
     * [Effect] list. Order matches the current reader:
     * `set_flags` first, then `remove_flags`, then `modify_stats`.
     * `modify_stats` order follows the JSON object's key order
     * (`LinkedHashMap` in `kotlinx.serialization`).
     */
    private fun buildEffects(
        setFlags: List<String>,
        removeFlags: List<String>,
        modifyStats: Map<String, Int>,
    ): List<Effect> {
        val result = mutableListOf<Effect>()
        setFlags.forEach { result += Effect.SetFlag(it) }
        removeFlags.forEach { result += Effect.RemoveFlag(it) }
        modifyStats.forEach { (name, delta) -> result += Effect.ModifyStat(name, delta) }
        return result
    }

    // ---------- Path helpers ----------

    private fun chapterPath(index: Int, id: String): String =
        if (id.isBlank()) "chapters[$index]" else "chapters[$index:$id]"

    private fun scenePath(parentPath: String, index: Int, id: String): String =
        if (id.isBlank()) "$parentPath.scenes[$index]"
        else "$parentPath.scenes[$index:$id]"


    /**
     * Ф2.8: converts a wire-format [VariableDto] into an IR [VarType].
     *
     * **Permissive defaults.** Unknown `type`, or `int_min` / `int_range`
     * without `min` / `max`, fall back to [VarType.Integer] (the widest
     * numeric type). Rationale:
     *
     * - **Unknown type** → forward compatibility: a file written by a
     *   future version may carry a type this version does not know.
     *   Failing would reject the whole file; defaulting to `Integer`
     *   keeps the adventure playable, and `TypeChecker` still catches
     *   typos in **variable names** (the most common authoring error).
     * - **Incomplete `IntMin` / `IntRange`** → the author typed a type
     *   but not the bounds. The `:app` editor (Ф2.7) does the same
     *   downgrade in `EditorVarDecl.toVarType()` — matching behaviour
     *   means the editor's "Проверить" report and the reader's runtime
     *   view agree.
     *
     * **Not downgraded to `Bool`.** `Bool` is not a superset of numeric
     * types; an `IntRange` that loses its bounds is still intended as a
     * number, just an unbounded one. Defaulting to `Bool` would turn a
     * `modify_stat` on it into `ModifyStatOnNonNumeric` — a spurious
     * error.
     */


    /**
     * Ф3.5: converts an [InvariantDto] to an IR [Invariant].
     *
     * Two stages, both may fail independently:
     * - `condition` — parsed by `ConditionParser`. On
     *   `ParseResult.Failure`, the errors are collected with a
     *   `invariants[i].condition` path.
     * - `outcome` — flat string mapped to [Outcome]. Only `"death"`
     *   is recognised today; unknown values produce a
     *   `ParseError.Structure`. Forward-compat: a future variant
     *   (`"ending"`, `"custom"`) would add a branch here and a new
     *   `Outcome` subclass in the IR. **Not** silently defaulted —
     *   an author who writes `"outcome": "deth"` should see the error,
     *   not a silently-fallen-back-to-death rule.
     *
     * Returns `null` if either stage failed; the caller
     * (`buildAdventure`) skips the invariant in the IR, and the
     * `errors` list (already non-empty) causes `JsonToIr.parse` to
     * return `ParseResult.Failure` — so the partial IR is not used.
     */
    private fun buildInvariant(
        dto: InvariantDto,
        index: Int,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): Invariant? {
        val path = "invariants[$index]"
        val condition = parseCondition(dto.condition, "$path.condition", errors)
        val outcome = when (dto.outcome) {
            "death" -> Outcome.Death
            else -> {
                errors += ParseError.Structure(
                    message = "Unknown invariant outcome '${dto.outcome}'. " +
                            "Supported: 'death'.",
                    path = "$path.outcome",
                )
                null
            }
        }
        return if (condition != null && outcome != null) {
            Invariant(condition = condition, outcome = outcome)
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    /**
     * Ф3.5 / Ф3.6 / Ф4.1: shared "parse a raw condition string into
     * an IR `Condition?`, collecting errors at [path]".
     *
     * Extracted from `buildChoice` and `buildInvariant`, both of which
     * had the same 15-line block. Ф4.1 adds two more callers
     * (`ChoiceTemplate.visibilityCondition` /
     * `availabilityCondition`); four duplicates would be worse than
     * one helper.
     */
    private fun parseCondition(
        raw: String,
        path: String,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): Condition? = when (val result = ConditionParser.parse(raw)) {
        is ParseResult.Success -> result.value
        is ParseResult.Failure -> {
            result.errors.forEach { err ->
                errors += if (err is ParseError.ConditionError) {
                    err.copy(path = path)
                } else {
                    err
                }
            }
            null
        }
    }

    /**
     * Ф4.1: converts a [ChoiceTemplateDto] to an IR [ChoiceTemplate].
     *
     * **Two-stage validation** (same shape as `buildInvariant` /
     * `buildChoice`):
     * - blank `id` → `ParseError.Structure` at [path].
     * - blank parameter name → `ParseError.Structure` at
     *   `$path.parameters[i]`.
     * - `visibility_condition` / `availability_condition` parsed by
     *   `ConditionParser` → on failure, `ParseError.ConditionError` is
     *   re-anchored to the field path.
     * - blank `next_scene` → `ParseError.Structure`.
     *
     * If any of these fail, the template is still constructed and
     * passed to `Adventure.choiceTemplates` (parser already records
     * errors, so `JsonToIr.parse` returns `Failure` overall — the
     * partial IR is not used by callers).
     *
     * **Not checked here:**
     * - Duplicate `id`s across templates → caught by `buildAdventure`
     *   in one pass over the whole list.
     * - Duplicate parameter names within one template → **not**
     *   checked in Ф4.1 (would surface as ambiguous scope in Ф4.2's
     *   `checkChoiceTemplate`). Can be added as an extra
     *   `ParseError.Structure` if it becomes a real source of bugs.
     * - Condition validity against `parameters` — `TypeChecker`
     *   extension in Ф4.2.
     */
    private fun buildChoiceTemplate(
        dto: ChoiceTemplateDto,
        path: String,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): ChoiceTemplate {
        if (dto.id.isBlank()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Choice template id is blank",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        val parameters = dto.parameters.mapIndexed { i, p ->
            if (p.name.isBlank()) {
                errors += ParseError.Structure(
                    message = "Parameter name is blank",
                    path = "$path.parameters[$i]",
                )
            }
            VarDecl(name = p.name, type = p.toVarType())
        }
        val visibilityCondition = dto.visibilityCondition?.let {
            parseCondition(it, "$path.visibility_condition", errors)
        }
        val availabilityCondition = dto.availabilityCondition?.let {
            parseCondition(it, "$path.availability_condition", errors)
        }
        val effects = buildEffects(dto.setFlags, dto.removeFlags, dto.modifyStats)
        if (dto.nextScene.isBlank()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Choice template next_scene is blank",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        return ChoiceTemplate(
            id = dto.id,
            parameters = parameters,
            text = dto.text,
            visibilityCondition = visibilityCondition,
            availabilityCondition = availabilityCondition,
            effects = effects,
            nextScene = SceneId(dto.nextScene),
        )
    }

    private fun VariableDto.toVarType(): VarType =
        typeStringToVarType(type, min, max)

    private fun VarDeclDto.toVarType(): VarType =
        typeStringToVarType(type, min, max)

    /**
     * Ф2.8 / Ф4.1: shared downgrade logic for wire-format type strings
     * (`VariableDto`, `VarDeclDto`). Extracted in Ф4.1 because
     * `ChoiceTemplate.parameters` uses `VarDeclDto` and needs the same
     * permissive-default rules.
     *
     * **Permissive defaults.** Unknown `type`, or `int_min` / `int_range`
     * without `min` / `max`, fall back to [VarType.Integer] (the widest
     * numeric type). Rationale (from Ф2.8):
     *
     * - **Unknown type** → forward compatibility: a file written by a
     *   future version may carry a type this version does not know.
     *   Failing would reject the whole file; defaulting to `Integer`
     *   keeps the adventure playable, and `TypeChecker` still catches
     *   typos in **variable names** (the most common authoring error).
     * - **Incomplete `IntMin` / `IntRange`** → the author typed a type
     *   but not the bounds. The `:app` editor (`EditorVarDecl.toVarType`)
     *   does the same downgrade in Ф2.7 — matching behaviour means the
     *   editor's «Проверить» report and the reader's runtime view agree.
     *
     * **Not downgraded to `Bool`.** `Bool` is not a superset of numeric
     * types; an `IntRange` that loses its bounds is still intended as a
     * number, just an unbounded one. Defaulting to `Bool` would turn a
     * `modify_stat` on it into `ModifyStatOnNonNumeric` — a spurious
     * error.
     */
    private fun typeStringToVarType(type: String, min: Int?, max: Int?): VarType =
        when (type) {
            "bool" -> VarType.Bool
            "int" -> VarType.Integer
            "int_min" -> min?.let { VarType.IntMin(it) } ?: VarType.Integer
            "int_range" -> {
                val minLocal = min
                val maxLocal = max
                if (minLocal != null && maxLocal != null) {
                    VarType.IntRange(minLocal, maxLocal)
                } else {
                    VarType.Integer
                }
            }
            "item_count" -> VarType.ItemCount
            "item_list" -> VarType.ItemList
            else -> VarType.Integer  // forward-compat
        }
}

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/format/dto/Dto.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory
import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Wire-format DTOs for the adventure JSON.
 *
 * These classes mirror the on-disk JSON exactly. They are **internal** —
 * a detail of the [com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr] pipeline,
 * not part of `:engine`'s public API. The public API works with
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure] and friends.
 *
 * All optional fields use non-null defaults (`emptyList()`, `emptyMap()`,
 * `null` for nullable types) so that the mapper does not have to write
 * `?: emptyList()` at every call site. `Json { coerceInputValues = true }`
 * (configured in `JsonToIr`) makes an explicit `null` in JSON behave the
 * same as a missing field.
 *
 * **Exception:** [AdventureDto.version] is nullable on purpose. `null`
 * means "the file has no version field" → the parser substitutes
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION]. We must be
 * able to distinguish "no version" from any explicit integer.
 *
 * **Why one file:** DTOs form a single JSON contract and change together;
 * splitting them across several files would add navigation noise without
 * any benefit. This is an intentional exception to the "one class per
 * file" convention, not an accident.
 */
@Serializable
internal data class AdventureDto(
    val version: Int? = null,
    val title: String,
    val author: String = "",
    val description: String = "",
    @SerialName("initial_state")
    val initialState: InitialStateDto = InitialStateDto(),
    /**
     * Ф2.8: declared variable types. `null`/absent → empty map → the
     * reader's `TypeChecker` runs in **fallback** mode (infers types
     * from `tags` + `initialState`). Non-empty → strict mode (every
     * reference must be declared here).
     *
     * `Map<String, VariableDto>`, not `Map<String, VarType>`. See
     * [VariableDto] KDoc: `VarType` cannot express the "incomplete
     * declaration" state (`IntMin(min = null)` is not constructible),
     * which the parser must accept and downgrade.
     */
    val variables: Map<String, VariableDto> = emptyMap(),
    /**
     * Ф4.1: reusable choice templates. Flat list of
     * `ChoiceTemplateDto` — see [ChoiceTemplateDto] KDoc. Empty /
     * absent → `Adventure.choiceTemplates = emptyList()`.
     * **No consumer in Ф4.1**: parsed infrastructure only. Ф4.2
     * adds `Choice.templateRef` + `applyTemplate`.
     */
    @SerialName("choice_templates")
    val choiceTemplates: List<ChoiceTemplateDto> = emptyList(),
    val invariants: List<InvariantDto> = emptyList(),
    val tags: List<TagDefinitionDto> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("death_scene")
    val deathScene: DeathSceneDto? = null,
    /** v3+; absent in v1/v2 files (migrated in `JsonToIr`). */
    @SerialName("start_scene")
    val startScene: String? = null,
    val chapters: List<ChapterDto> = emptyList(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class ChapterDto(
    val id: String,
    val title: String = "",
    /**
     * **Legacy (v1).** In adventure files of version 1 this field carried
     * a step gate on the chapter. Since v2 the gate lives on the scene
     * ([SceneDto.gate]). Kept here so v1 files still parse; `JsonToIr`
     * migrates a non-zero value onto the last scene of the previous
     * chapter as `Gate(requiredSteps)`.
     */
    @SerialName("required_steps")
    val requiredSteps: Int = 0,
    val scenes: List<SceneDto> = emptyList(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class SceneDto(
    val id: String,
    val text: String,
    @SerialName("set_flags")
    val setFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("remove_flags")
    val removeFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("modify_stats")
    val modifyStats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    val choices: List<ChoiceDto> = emptyList(),
    val gate: Int? = null,
    /**
     * v5+; absent in v1–v4 files. `null` means "field was not in the
     * source file". `JsonToIr` maps `null` to `false` (identity
     * migration v4 → v5). Adventure file format keeps the gate flat:
     * `"gate": N` + optional `"gate_repeatable": true`, so a simple
     * gate stays one key.
     */
    @SerialName("gate_repeatable")
    val gateRepeatable: Boolean? = null,
    /**
     * v4+; absent in v1–v3 files. `null` means "field was not in the
     * source file". `JsonToIr` maps `null` to `false` (identity
     * migration v3 → v4). Nullable rather than `Boolean = false` for
     * consistency with [AdventureDto.version] and [SceneDto.gate], and
     * so that a future migration can distinguish "author explicitly
     * wrote `is_ending: false`" from "author did not write the field".
     * Today both collapse to `Scene.isEnding = false`, so the
     * distinction is not observed.
     */
    @SerialName("is_ending")
    val isEnding: Boolean? = null,
    /**
     * Ф4.5: `"merge": true` marks this scene as a merge point.
     * `null` (field absent) → false (identity migration). See
     * `:engine/ir/Scene.isMerge`.
     */
    val merge: Boolean? = null,
    /**
     * Ф4.5: `"merge_sources": ["s1", "s2"]` — declared incoming
     * branches. Empty list (field absent) → no sources declared; the
     * analyzer (Ф4.6) will collect them from the `nextScene` graph.
     */
    @SerialName("merge_sources")
    val mergeSources: List<String> = emptyList(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class ChoiceDto(
    val id: String? = null,
    val text: String,
    @SerialName("next_scene")
    val nextScene: String,
    val condition: String? = null,
    @SerialName("set_flags")
    val setFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("remove_flags")
    val removeFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("modify_stats")
    val modifyStats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class TagDefinitionDto(
    val name: String,
    @SerialName("display_name")
    val displayName: String = "",
    val category: TagCategory = TagCategory.JOURNAL,
    val visible: Boolean = false,
)

@Serializable
internal data class InitialStateDto(
    val flags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class DeathSceneDto(
    val id: String = "death_scene",
    /**
     * Ф4-infra (3b-6h): empty default — see `:engine/ir/DeathScene.text`
     * KDoc. Reader falls back to `R.string.reader_default_death_text`
     * in `AdventureReaderFragment.showDeathScreen` when this is empty.
     */
    val text: String = "",
    @SerialName("allow_step_back")
    val allowStepBack: Boolean = true,
    @SerialName("allow_chapter_restart")
    val allowChapterRestart: Boolean = true,
    @SerialName("allow_adventure_restart")
    val allowAdventureRestart: Boolean = true,
)

/**
 * Ф2.8: wire-format for a single variable declaration.
 *
 * [type] is a **string discriminator** (`"bool"`, `"int"`, `"int_min"`,
 * `"int_range"`, `"item_count"`, `"item_list"`), matching the
 * `@SerialName` values on
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType]. `min` / `max` are only
 * meaningful for `int_min` / `int_range`, `null` for the others.
 *
 * **Why not reuse `VarType` directly.** `VarType` is a `sealed class`
 * with polymorphic serialization, which produces
 * `{"type": "int_min", "min": 0}` — the same JSON shape as
 * `VariableDto`. But `VarType` cannot express the "incomplete
 * declaration" state: `IntMin(min = null)` is not constructible
 * (`min` is required). The parser must accept
 * `{"type": "int_min"}` (no `min`) from a partially-filled file and
 * downgrade to `Integer`. `VariableDto` can hold that state
 * (`min = null`); `VarType` cannot. See `JsonToIr.VariableDto.toVarType`
 * for the downgrade logic.
 */
@Serializable
internal data class VariableDto(
    val type: String,
    val min: Int? = null,
    val max: Int? = null,
)


/**
 * Ф4.1: wire-format for a single reusable choice template.
 *
 * The adventure file uses `choice_templates` (plural, snake_case) at
 * the top level and `next_scene` / `visibility_condition` /
 * `availability_condition` (snake_case) inside each entry, matching
 * `ChoiceDto.nextScene` and the general snake_case convention of
 * multi-word fields.
 *
 * **Flat-vs-typed distinction** (same as everywhere else): `text` is
 * a plain string; `visibilityCondition` / `availabilityCondition` are
 * condition **strings** parsed by `ConditionParser`; effects are the
 * three parallel fields `set_flags` / `remove_flags` /
 * `modify_stats`. The typed IR counterpart is `ChoiceTemplate`.
 *
 * **Why `parameters: List<VarDeclDto>`, not `Map<String, VarType>`.**
 * Parameters are an ordered list of typed declarations; `VarDeclDto`
 * has `name` inside the object (`{"name": "itemId", "type":
 * "item_count"}`), not as the map key. This mirrors how
 * `Adventure.variables` looks in JSON (`{"health": {"type": ...}}` —
 * name is the key), except that template parameters use list form
 * because order is meaningful for documentation and duplicates must
 * be an error (checked by `JsonToIr`).
 */
@Serializable
internal data class ChoiceTemplateDto(
    val id: String,
    val parameters: List<VarDeclDto> = emptyList(),
    val text: String,
    @SerialName("visibility_condition")
    val visibilityCondition: String? = null,
    @SerialName("availability_condition")
    val availabilityCondition: String? = null,
    @SerialName("set_flags")
    val setFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("remove_flags")
    val removeFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("modify_stats")
    val modifyStats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    @SerialName("next_scene")
    val nextScene: String,
)

/**
 * Ф4.1: wire-format for a single typed parameter declaration.
 *
 * `name` + `type` + optional `min` / `max` (for `int_min` /
 * `int_range`). Field set is identical to `VariableDto` plus `name`;
 * the two types share the `type` / `min` / `max` downgrade logic
 * (see `JsonToIr.typeStringToVarType`).
 */
@Serializable
internal data class VarDeclDto(
    val name: String,
    val type: String,
    val min: Int? = null,
    val max: Int? = null,
)

/**
 * Ф3.5: wire-format for a single invariant.
 *
 * **Flat shape** (unlike the IR `Invariant`, which has typed
 * `condition: Condition` and sealed `outcome: Outcome`):
 * - `condition` is a condition string — same syntax as
 *   `ChoiceDto.condition`, parsed by `ConditionParser`.
 * - `outcome` is a flat string (`"death"` today). Future variants
 *   (`"ending"`, `"custom"`) extend the allowed set — `JsonToIr`
 *   maps them into `Outcome`.
 *
 * The flat-vs-typed distinction is intentional, same as with
 * `ChoiceDto.condition` (string) vs. `Choice.condition` (AST): the
 * author's file is a string, the runtime works on the AST.
 */
@Serializable
internal data class InvariantDto(
    val condition: String,
    val outcome: String,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.PlayerState
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals

class EffectsApplierTest {

    @Test
    fun `empty effects return same state`() {
        val s = PlayerState(flags = setOf("a"), stats = mapOf("health" to 10))
        assertEquals(s, EffectsApplier.apply(s, emptyList()))
    }

    @Test
    fun `set flag adds`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(),
            listOf(Effect.SetFlag("a"), Effect.SetFlag("b")),
        )
        assertEquals(setOf("a", "b"), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `set flag is idempotent`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(flags = setOf("a")),
            listOf(Effect.SetFlag("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(setOf("a"), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `remove flag removes`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(flags = setOf("a", "b")),
            listOf(Effect.RemoveFlag("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(setOf("b"), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `modify stat adds delta`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
            listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -30)),
        )
        assertEquals(70, s.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `modify stat creates missing with delta`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(),
            listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("mana", 5)),
        )
        assertEquals(5, s.stats["mana"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `modify stat clamps to zero`() {
        // Ф1.5 policy: all ModifyStat clamp to >= 0. In Ф2.8 this becomes
        // type-dependent (HEALTH/ITEM clamp, Integer/IntRange per-type).
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 3)),
            listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10)),
        )
        assertEquals(0, s.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `order matters - remove then set leaves set`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(flags = setOf("a")),
            listOf(Effect.RemoveFlag("a"), Effect.SetFlag("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(setOf("a"), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `order matters - set then remove leaves unset`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(),
            listOf(Effect.SetFlag("a"), Effect.RemoveFlag("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(emptySet(), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `state is not mutated`() {
        val original = PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 10))
        EffectsApplier.apply(original, listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -5)))
        assertEquals(10, original.stats["health"])
    }

    // ---------- Ф3.1: Effect.Set ----------

    @Test
    fun `set stat sets absolute value`() {
        // Pre-existing value 50 → 100 (not 100 + 50).
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 50)),
            listOf(Effect.Set("health", 100)),
        )
        assertEquals(100, s.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `set stat creates missing stat with value`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(),
            listOf(Effect.Set("mana", 5)),
        )
        assertEquals(5, s.stats["mana"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `set stat clamps to zero`() {
        // Same clamp policy as ModifyStat (Ф5 will make it type-aware).
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 50)),
            listOf(Effect.Set("health", -10)),
        )
        assertEquals(0, s.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `state is not mutated by set`() {
        val original = PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 50))
        EffectsApplier.apply(original, listOf(Effect.Set("health", 100)))
        assertEquals(50, original.stats["health"], "original state must not be mutated")
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertTrue


class EngineCompileTest {

    private fun adventure(vararg chapters: Chapter): Adventure = Adventure(
        title = "T",
        startScene = chapters.firstOrNull()?.scenes?.firstOrNull()?.id ?: SceneId(""),
        chapters = chapters.toList(),
    )

    private fun chapter(id: String, vararg scenes: Scene): Chapter = Chapter(
        id = id,
        title = id,
        scenes = scenes.toList(),
    )

    private fun scene(id: String): Scene = Scene(id = SceneId(id), text = "x")

    @Test
    fun `single scene compiles`() {
        val adv = adventure(chapter("c1", scene("s1")))
        val result = Engine.compile(adv)
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(result).compiled
        assertEquals(1, compiled.scenesById.size)
        assertEquals("s1", compiled.scenesById[SceneId("s1")]?.id?.value)
        assertEquals(0, compiled.chapterIndexBySceneId[SceneId("s1")])
    }

    @Test
    fun `multiple chapters compile`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            chapter("c1", scene("s1"), scene("s2")),
            chapter("c2", scene("s3")),
        )
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adv)).compiled
        assertEquals(3, compiled.scenesById.size)
        assertEquals(0, compiled.chapterIndexBySceneId[SceneId("s1")])
        assertEquals(0, compiled.chapterIndexBySceneId[SceneId("s2")])
        assertEquals(1, compiled.chapterIndexBySceneId[SceneId("s3")])
    }

    @Test
    fun `duplicate scene id fails with chapter indices`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            chapter("c1", scene("s1")),
            chapter("c2", scene("s1")),
        )
        val result = Engine.compile(adv)
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(result).errors
        val duplicate = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.DuplicateSceneId>().single()
        assertEquals(SceneId("s1"), duplicate.sceneId)
        assertEquals(listOf(0, 1), duplicate.chapterIndices)
        assertTrue(duplicate.message.contains("chapters 1, 2"), duplicate.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing start scene fails compile`() {
        // startScene points to "ghost"; the only scene is "s1".
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("ghost"),
            chapters = listOf(chapter("c1", scene("s1"))),
        )
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(Engine.compile(adv)).errors
        val missing = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.MissingStartScene>().single()
        assertEquals(SceneId("ghost"), missing.startSceneId)
        assertTrue(missing.message.contains("ghost"), missing.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing next_scene fails compile with choice details`() {
        val a = Scene(
            id = SceneId("a"),
            text = "text of a",
            choices = listOf(
                Choice(
                    id = ChoiceId("c1"),
                    text = "Go",
                    nextScene = SceneId("ghost"),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("a"),
            chapters = listOf(chapter("ch", a)),
        )
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(Engine.compile(adv)).errors
        val missing = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.MissingNextScene>().single()
        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), missing.sceneId)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("c1"), missing.choiceId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("ghost"), missing.targetSceneId)
        assertTrue(missing.message.contains("c1"), missing.message)
        assertTrue(missing.message.contains("ghost"), missing.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `multiple missing next_scene errors are reported in stable order`() {
        val a = Scene(
            id = SceneId("a"),
            text = "text of a",
            choices = listOf(
                Choice(id = ChoiceId("c1"), text = "Go", nextScene = SceneId("ghost1")),
                Choice(id = ChoiceId("c2"), text = "Go", nextScene = SceneId("ghost2")),
            ),
        )
        val b = Scene(
            id = SceneId("b"),
            text = "text of b",
            choices = listOf(
                Choice(id = ChoiceId("c1"), text = "Go", nextScene = SceneId("ghost3")),
            ),
        )
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("a"),
            chapters = listOf(chapter("ch", a, b)),
        )
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(Engine.compile(adv)).errors
        val missing = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.MissingNextScene>()
        assertEquals(3, missing.size)
        // Sorted by (sceneId, choiceId): a/c1, a/c2, b/c1.
        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), missing[0].sceneId)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("c1"), missing[0].choiceId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), missing[1].sceneId)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("c2"), missing[1].choiceId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("b"), missing[2].sceneId)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("c1"), missing[2].choiceId)
    }

    // ---------- Ф4.5: merge sources ----------

    @Test
    fun `merge source pointing to missing scene fails compile`() {
        val m = Scene(
            id = SceneId("m"),
            text = "M",
            isMerge = true,
            mergeSources = listOf(SceneId("ghost")),
        )
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("m"),
            chapters = listOf(chapter("ch", m)),
        )
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(Engine.compile(adv)).errors
        val missing = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.MissingMergeSource>().single()
        assertEquals(SceneId("m"), missing.sceneId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("ghost"), missing.mergeSourceId)
        assertTrue(missing.message.contains("ghost"), missing.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `valid merge sources compile`() {
        val a = Scene(
            id = SceneId("a"),
            text = "A",
            choices = listOf(Choice(ChoiceId("ca"), "Go", SceneId("m"))),
        )
        val b = Scene(
            id = SceneId("b"),
            text = "B",
            choices = listOf(Choice(ChoiceId("cb"), "Go", SceneId("m"))),
        )
        val m = Scene(
            id = SceneId("m"),
            text = "M",
            isMerge = true,
            mergeSources = listOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b")),
        )
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("a"),
            chapters = listOf(chapter("ch", a, b, m)),
        )
        assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adv))
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Gate
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.PlayerState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.toPlayerState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Invariant
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Outcome
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompiledAdventure
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertFalse
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertNotNull
import kotlin.test.assertTrue

class EngineStepTest {

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    private fun scene(
        id: String,
        choices: List<Choice> = emptyList(),
        gate: Gate? = null,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
    ): Scene = Scene(
        id = SceneId(id),
        text = "text of $id",
        effects = effects,
        choices = choices,
        gate = gate,
    )

    private fun choice(
        id: String,
        next: String,
        condition: Condition? = null,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
    ): Choice = Choice(
        id = ChoiceId(id),
        text = "choice $id",
        nextScene = SceneId(next),
        condition = condition,
        effects = effects,
    )

    private fun chapter(id: String, vararg scenes: Scene): Chapter =
        Chapter(id = id, title = id, scenes = scenes.toList())

    private fun adventure(vararg chapters: Chapter): Adventure = Adventure(
        title = "T",
        startScene = chapters.firstOrNull()?.scenes?.firstOrNull()?.id ?: SceneId(""),
        chapters = chapters.toList(),
    )

    private fun compile(adventure: Adventure): CompiledAdventure =
        assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adventure)).compiled

    private fun state(
        flags: Set<String> = emptySet(),
        stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    ): PlayerState = PlayerState(flags = flags, stats = stats)

    private fun rejected(result: StepResult): RejectReason =
        assertIs<StepResult.Rejected>(result, "expected Rejected, got $result").reason

    // ---------- happy path ----------

    @Test
    fun `simple transition succeeds and returns target scene`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))
        val initial = state()

        val result = Engine.step(compiled, initial, SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"))
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(SceneId("b"), success.currentScene.id)
        assertEquals(false, success.isDead)
        assertEquals(initial, success.state)
    }

    @Test
    fun `choice effects applied to state`() {
        val a = scene(

    @Test

        // Set then remove: flag absent. If order were reversed, flag present.
        val a = scene(

    @Test

        assertIs<RejectReason.SceneNotFound>(reason)
        assertEquals(SceneId("missing"), reason.sceneId)
    }

    @Test

        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "a")))
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a)))

        val reason = rejected(
