package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseError
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertNull
import kotlin.test.assertTrue

class JsonToIrTest {

    private fun success(json: String): Adventure {
        val result = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val s = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(
            result,
            "expected Success, got $result",
        )
        return s.value
    }

    private fun failure(json: String): List<ParseError> {
        val result = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val f = assertIs<ParseResult.Failure>(
            result,
            "expected Failure, got $result",
        )
        assertTrue(f.errors.isNotEmpty(), "Failure must contain at least one error")
        return f.errors
    }

    @Test
    fun `minimal valid adventure`() {
        val json = """
            {
              "title": "Test",
              "chapters": [{
                "id": "c1",
                "scenes": [{"id": "s1", "text": "Hello"}]
              }]
            }
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals("Test", adv.title)
        assertEquals(5, adv.version) // CURRENT_VERSION after Ф1.7.0.4
        assertEquals(1, adv.chapters.size)
        assertEquals("c1", adv.chapters[0].id)
        assertEquals("s1", adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].id.value)
        assertNull(adv.deathScene)
    }

    @Test
    fun `version absent becomes CURRENT_VERSION`() {
        val json = """{"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{"id":"s1","text":"Hi"}]}]}"""
        assertEquals(Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION, success(json).version)
    }

    @Test
    fun `version present is preserved`() {
        val json = """{"version":2,"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{"id":"s1","text":"Hi"}]}]}"""
        assertEquals(2, success(json).version)
    }

    @Test
    fun `empty chapters is an error`() {
        val json = """{"title":"T","chapters":[]}"""
        val errors = failure(json)
        assertTrue(
            errors.any { it is ParseError.Structure && it.message.contains("no chapters") },
            "expected 'no chapters' Structure error, got $errors",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `empty chapter scenes is an error`() {
        val json = """{"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[]}]}"""
        val errors = failure(json)
        assertTrue(
            errors.any { it is ParseError.Structure && it.message.contains("no scenes") },
            "expected 'no scenes' Structure error, got $errors",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `blank scene id is an error`() {
        val json = """{"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{"id":"  ","text":"Hi"}]}]}"""
        val errors = failure(json)
        assertTrue(
            errors.any { it is ParseError.Structure && it.message.contains("Scene id") },
            "expected 'Scene id' Structure error, got $errors",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `blank choice text is an error`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","choices":[{"text":"","next_scene":"s1"}]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val errors = failure(json)
        assertTrue(
            errors.any { it is ParseError.Structure && it.message.contains("Choice text") },
            "expected 'Choice text' Structure error, got $errors",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `blank choice next_scene is an error`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","choices":[{"text":"Go","next_scene":""}]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val errors = failure(json)
        assertTrue(
            errors.any { it is ParseError.Structure && it.message.contains("next_scene") },
            "expected 'next_scene' Structure error, got $errors",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `invalid condition is a ConditionError with path`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","choices":[{"text":"Go","next_scene":"s1","condition":"has_sword && health"}]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val errors = failure(json)
        val condErr = errors.filterIsInstance<ParseError.ConditionError>().single()
        val path = condErr.path
        assertTrue(
            path != null && path.contains("choices[0].condition"),
            "expected path to contain 'choices[0].condition', got $path",
        )
        assertTrue(
            path.contains("c1") && path.contains("s1"),
            "expected path to contain chapter id 'c1' and scene id 's1', got $path",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `multiple errors accumulated`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"","text":"Hi","choices":[{"text":"","next_scene":"s1"}]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val errors = failure(json)
        // blank scene.id + blank choice.text = at least 2
        assertTrue(
            errors.size >= 2,
            "expected at least 2 accumulated errors, got ${errors.size}: $errors",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `effects order set remove modify`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi",
              "set_flags":["a","b"],
              "remove_flags":["c"],
              "modify_stats":{"health":-5,"mana":3}
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        val effects = adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].effects
        assertEquals(5, effects.size)
        assertIs<Effect.SetFlag>(effects[0])
        assertIs<Effect.SetFlag>(effects[1])
        assertIs<Effect.RemoveFlag>(effects[2])
        assertIs<Effect.ModifyStat>(effects[3])
        assertIs<Effect.ModifyStat>(effects[4])
        assertEquals("health", (effects[3] as Effect.ModifyStat).name)
        assertEquals(-5, (effects[3] as Effect.ModifyStat).delta)
        assertEquals("mana", (effects[4] as Effect.ModifyStat).name)
        assertEquals(3, (effects[4] as Effect.ModifyStat).delta)
    }

    @Test
    fun `malformed JSON is a Syntax error`() {
        val json = """{"title":"""
        val errors = failure(json)
        val syntax = errors.single()
        assertIs<ParseError.Syntax>(syntax)
    }

    @Test
    fun `typo in flag name produces TypeError now that F2_3 wires the checker`() {
        // Ф1.3.4.1 documented this boundary as "parser accepts, type
        // checker rejects". Ф2.3 now actually runs the type checker inside
        // `JsonToIr.parse`, so the same JSON that used to return
        // `Success(ir)` now returns `Failure(typeErrors = [UnknownVariable])`.
        //
        // **Fixture note.** The JSON includes `initial_state.flags` so
        // that TypeChecker's fallback mode (C4) builds a non-empty type
        // table. With an entirely empty `tags` + `initialState`,
        // TypeChecker returns `emptyList()` (nothing to check against —
        // see its KDoc, "Fallback" mode), and `swrod` would slip through
        // as `Success`. The flag `marker` itself is irrelevant; it just
        // makes the table non-empty, so `swrod` (which is not in it) is
        // correctly reported as UnknownVariable.
        //
        // The parser/type-checker boundary is still preserved: this error
        // is a **type error**, not a **parse error** — it lives in
        // `typeErrors`, not in `errors`. Callers that only inspect
        // `result.errors` see "the JSON is structurally valid"; callers
        // that also inspect `result.typeErrors` see "but `swrod` is not a
        // declared variable".
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","initial_state":{"flags":["marker"]},"chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","choices":[{"text":"Go","next_scene":"s1","condition":"has_swrod"}]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val result = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val failure = assertIs<ParseResult.Failure>(result)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), failure.errors)
        assertEquals(1, failure.typeErrors.size)
        val typeErr = assertIs<com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeError.UnknownVariable>(
            failure.typeErrors.single(),
        )
        assertEquals("swrod", typeErr.name)
    }

    @Test
    fun `type errors are not checked when parse errors are present`() {
        // B1 decision (Ф2.3): if parsing fails, type checking is not
        // attempted. A partial IR would produce false negatives at best
        // (unchecked conditions) and false positives at worst (unknown
        // variables that would have been declared in the unparsed part).
        //
        // The input below combines two independent errors:
        // - a **parse error**: blank choice.text (structural problem);
        // - a **type error**: `has_swrod` (unknown variable).
        // Expected: `Failure` with `errors` non-empty (the parse error)
        // and `typeErrors` empty (typecheck was skipped).
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","choices":[
                {"text":"","next_scene":"s1","condition":"has_swrod"}
              ]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val result = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val failure = assertIs<ParseResult.Failure>(result)
        assertTrue(
            failure.errors.isNotEmpty(),
            "expected parse errors (blank choice.text), got ${failure.errors}",
        )
        assertEquals(
            emptyList(),
            failure.typeErrors,
            "type checking must not run when parsing failed (B1 decision)",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `type errors produced when parse is clean - HasOnNonBool path`() {
        // Companion to the test above, but exercises a **different**
        // TypeError variant through the same pipeline: not "unknown
        // variable", but "variable exists, but `has_` on it is wrong
        // because its type is not Bool".
        //
        // Fixture: `sword` is declared as an ITEM tag (fallback mode
        // infers `VarType.ItemCount`) and given `1` in the initial state.
        // The choice uses `has_sword` on it — the common authoring
        // mistake that Ф1.7.1a-fix3 fixed in `test_adventure.json` by
        // rewriting it as `sword > 0`. TypeChecker now catches this
        // automatically. The expected error is `HasOnNonBool`, with a
        // fix-hint in its message ("use 'sword > 0' instead").
        val json = """
            {
              "title": "T",
              "tags": [{"name": "sword", "category": "ITEM"}],
              "initial_state": {"stats": {"sword": 1}},
              "chapters": [{"id": "c1", "scenes": [{
                "id": "s1",
                "text": "Hi",
                "choices": [{"text": "Go", "next_scene": "s1", "condition": "has_sword"}]
              }]}]
            }
        """.trimIndent()
        val result = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val failure = assertIs<ParseResult.Failure>(result)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), failure.errors)
        assertEquals(1, failure.typeErrors.size)
        val typeErr = assertIs<com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeError.HasOnNonBool>(
            failure.typeErrors.single(),
        )
        assertEquals("sword", typeErr.name)
    }

    @Test
    fun `choice id generated when absent in JSON`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"start","text":"Hi","choices":[
                {"text":"First","next_scene":"start"},
                {"text":"Second","next_scene":"start"}
              ]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        val choices = adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].choices
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("start_choice_0"), choices[0].id)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("start_choice_1"), choices[1].id)
    }

    @Test
    fun `choice id from JSON preserved when present`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"start","text":"Hi","choices":[
                {"id":"my_custom_id","text":"Go","next_scene":"start"}
              ]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("my_custom_id"), adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].choices[0].id)
    }

    @Test
    fun `scene gate absent is null`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi"
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals(null, adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].gate)
    }

    @Test
    fun `scene gate positive is parsed`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","gate":100
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals(100, adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].gate?.requiredSteps)
    }

    @Test
    fun `scene gate zero is an error`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","gate":0
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val errors = failure(json)
        assertTrue(
            errors.any { it is ParseError.Structure && it.message.contains("gate must be") },
            "expected 'gate must be' Structure error, got $errors",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `scene gate negative is an error`() {
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","gate":-5
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val errors = failure(json)
        assertTrue(
            errors.any { it is ParseError.Structure && it.message.contains("gate must be") },
            "expected 'gate must be' Structure error, got $errors",
        )

    @Test
    fun `v1 file migrates chapter required_steps to gate on previous chapter last scene`() {
        // v1 file: no explicit "version", gates on chapters.
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[
              {"id":"c1","required_steps":0,"scenes":[
                {"id":"s1","text":"A"},{"id":"s2","text":"B"}
              ]},
              {"id":"c2","required_steps":100,"scenes":[
                {"id":"s3","text":"C"}
              ]}
            ]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        // s2 is the last scene of c1; the gate from c2.required_steps migrates to it.
        assertEquals(100, adv.chapters[0].scenes[1].gate?.requiredSteps)
        // No gate on s1 or s3.
        assertEquals(null, adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].gate)
        assertEquals(null, adv.chapters[1].scenes[0].gate)
    }

    @Test
    fun `v1 file explicit version 1 migrates the same way`() {
        val json = """
            {"version":1,"title":"T","chapters":[
              {"id":"c1","required_steps":0,"scenes":[{"id":"s1","text":"A"}]},
              {"id":"c2","required_steps":42,"scenes":[{"id":"s2","text":"B"}]}
            ]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals(42, adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].gate?.requiredSteps)
    }


    @Test
    fun `v2 file without start_scene migrates from chapters`() {
        val json = """
            {"version":2,"title":"T","chapters":[
              {"id":"c1","scenes":[{"id":"first","text":"A"},{"id":"second","text":"B"}]},
              {"id":"c2","scenes":[{"id":"third","text":"C"}]}
            ]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals(SceneId("first"), adv.startScene)
    }

    @Test
    fun `v2 file with explicit start_scene preserves it`() {
        val json = """
            {"version":2,"title":"T","start_scene":"second","chapters":[
              {"id":"c1","scenes":[{"id":"first","text":"A"},{"id":"second","text":"B"}]}
            ]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals(SceneId("second"), adv.startScene)
    }

    @Test
    fun `gate_repeatable absent defaults to false`() {
        // Identity migration v4 → v5: files that predate gate_repeatable
        // get repeatable = false ("once passed, stays passed in this
        // playthrough"). This is the common "unlock the next chapter"
        // case — the least surprising default.
        val json = """
            {"version":5,"title":"T","start_scene":"s1","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[
              {"id":"s1","text":"Hi","gate":100}
            ]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        val gate = adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].gate
        assertEquals(100, gate?.requiredSteps)
        assertEquals(false, gate?.repeatable)
    }

    @Test
    fun `gate_repeatable true is parsed`() {
        // Per-visit mode: the gate re-engages every time the player
        // enters this scene. Used by authors for "travelled a path" /
        // "wait N steps before each visit" scenarios.
        val json = """
            {"version":5,"title":"T","start_scene":"s1","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[
              {"id":"s1","text":"Hi","gate":4000,"gate_repeatable":true}
            ]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        val gate = adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].gate
        assertEquals(4000, gate?.requiredSteps)
        assertEquals(true, gate?.repeatable)
    }

    @Test
    fun `unknown next_scene parses as SceneId - reachability is F2`() {
        // `next_scene: "nonexistent"` parses successfully: the parser
        // does not know the full scene set while parsing one choice
        // (the scene may be defined in another chapter). Reachability is
        // the analyzer's job (Ф1.6 / Ф2); the resulting IR contains
        // SceneId("nonexistent"), which the analyzer will flag.
        //
        // This test documents the boundary. If it starts failing, someone
        // moved reachability into the parser.
        val json = """
            {"title":"T","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[{
              "id":"s1","text":"Hi","choices":[{"text":"Go","next_scene":"nonexistent"}]
            }]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        val choice = adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].choices[0]
        assertEquals(SceneId("nonexistent"), choice.nextScene)
    }

    @Test
    fun `v4 file without is_ending defaults to false`() {
        // Identity migration v3 → v4: files that predate the field have
        // no is_ending. The parser must map absent → false, not crash
        // and not leave it null.
        // start_scene is required since v3; the parser rejects v3+ files
        // without it before is_ending is even looked at — so we include it.
        val json = """
            {"version":4,"title":"T","start_scene":"s1","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[
              {"id":"s1","text":"Hi"}
            ]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals(false, adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].isEnding)
    }

    @Test
    fun `v4 file with is_ending true marks the scene as ending`() {
        // Multiple endings are allowed by design (see Scene.isEnding KDoc).
        // Here: `mid` has a choice, `end1` and `end2` are both endings.
        // start_scene is required since v3; without it the parser returns
        // ParseError.Structure before any is_ending logic runs.
        val json = """
            {"version":4,"title":"T","start_scene":"mid","chapters":[{"id":"c1","scenes":[
              {"id":"mid","text":"Choose","choices":[
                {"text":"Win","next_scene":"end1"},
                {"text":"Retire","next_scene":"end2"}
              ]},
              {"id":"end1","text":"You win","is_ending":true},
              {"id":"end2","text":"You retire","is_ending":true}
            ]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        val scenes = adv.chapters[0].scenes
        assertEquals(3, scenes.size)
        assertEquals(false, scenes[0].isEnding) // mid
        assertEquals(true, scenes[1].isEnding)  // end1
        assertEquals(true, scenes[2].isEnding)  // end2
    }

    @Test
    fun `v3 file without is_ending migrates to false`() {
        // A v3 file has no is_ending field. After the v3 → v4 identity
        // migration, Scene.isEnding must be false, not null. This is the
        // last layer of the "old files keep working" guarantee at the
        // parser level — the analyzer layer (DeadEnd ERROR on
        // unreachable/no-choices scenes) is what surfaces the change.
        val json = """
            {"version":3,"title":"T","start_scene":"s1","chapters":[
              {"id":"c1","scenes":[{"id":"s1","text":"Hi"}]}
            ]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        assertEquals(false, adv.chapters[0].scenes[0].isEnding)
    }

    // ---------- Ф2.8: variables parsing ----------

        val json = """
            {

                "sword": {"type": "item_count"},

    }

    @Test

              {"id":"m","text":"M","merge":true,"merge_sources":["s1","s2"]}
            ]}]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val adv = success(json)
        val m = adv.chapters[0].scenes.first { it.id == SceneId("m") }

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertNotNull
import kotlin.test.assertTrue
import kotlin.test.assertNull
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp

/**
 * Integration test: parses the **real** `test_adventure.json` (copied
 * from `:app` into `:engine` test resources by the Gradle copy task in
 * `engine/build.gradle.kts`, see Ф1.3.3.1) and asserts the resulting IR
 * matches the file's documented contents.
 *
 * **Why this test exists:** `test_adventure.json` is shipped to every new
 * user (SetupFragment copies it into their `Adventures/` folder on first
 * launch). If the engine cannot parse it, the very first adventure the
 * user opens is broken. This test fails in CI **before** a broken file
 * reaches a user.
 *
 * **What this test does NOT check** (deliberately deferred):
 * - Type validity of `has_sword` on `sword: ItemCount` — type checker
 *   Ф2.2. Today `sword` is `ItemCount`, but `test_adventure.json` still
 *   uses `has_sword`. This will be rewritten in Ф2.8 to `sword > 0`.
 * - `next_scene` reachability, duplicate scene ids — `Analyzer` (Ф1.6).
 *
 * If this test fails after you changed `test_adventure.json`, it is
 * working as designed: update the test (both are in the same repo) or,
 * if the change is a bug in the engine, fix the engine.
 */
class RealAdventureTest {

    private fun loadAdventureJson(): String {
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream("/test_adventure.json")
        assertNotNull(stream, "test_adventure.json not found in test resources — check the copy task in engine/build.gradle.kts")
        return stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
    }

    private fun parseRealFile(): Adventure {
        val json = loadAdventureJson()
        val result = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val success = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(
            result,
            "real test_adventure.json failed to parse: $result",
        )
        return success.value
    }

    @Test
    fun `parses without errors`() {
        // If the real file fails to parse, CI fails here before a new user
        // sees a broken sample on first launch.
        parseRealFile()
    }

    @Test
    fun `start scene is start`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        assertEquals(SceneId("start"), adv.startScene)
    }

    @Test
    fun `metadata`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        assertEquals("Тестовое приключение", adv.title)
        assertEquals("Безумный монах", adv.author)
        // test_adventure.json explicitly carries "version": CURRENT_VERSION.
        // It is the reference sample — a reader opening it should see the
        // current schema, not a legacy one. When CURRENT_VERSION bumps, the
        // sample bumps in the same PR; this test catches a forgotten bump.
        assertEquals(Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION, adv.version)
        assertTrue(adv.description.isNotEmpty())
    }

    @Test
    fun `three chapters with gates on specific scenes`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        assertEquals(3, adv.chapters.size)
        assertEquals("chapter_1", adv.chapters[0].id)
        assertEquals("chapter_2", adv.chapters[1].id)
        assertEquals("chapter_3", adv.chapters[2].id)
        // Главы больше не несут гейт — это чисто нарративная группировка.
        // Гейты живут на конкретных сценах (Ф1.5.4).
    }

    @Test
    fun `gates on specific scenes`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        fun gateOf(chapterIndex: Int, sceneId: String): Int? =
            adv.chapters[chapterIndex].scenes
                .first { it.id == SceneId(sceneId) }
                .gate
                ?.requiredSteps

        // Все три гейта в эталонном приключении — 1 шаг: достаточно,
        // чтобы проверить механику вручную (см. проектный принцип
        // «тестовое приключение должно проходиться быстро»), и не
        // заставляет тестировщика ходить. Реальные приключения,
        // разумеется, ставят тысячи шагов.
        //
        // Ф3.4-fix2: гейт вынесен из `health_test` в отдельную сцену
        // `gate_test`, чтобы тестировать здоровье/предметы/журнал без
        // шагов. `health_test` теперь без гейта. `gate_test` — per-visit
        // режим. `chapter_end_*` — one-shot, нарративные, тоже 1 шаг.
        assertEquals(1, gateOf(0, "gate_test"))     // per-visit gate (middle of chapter 1)
        assertEquals(1, gateOf(0, "chapter_end_1")) // one-shot gate (end of chapter 1)
        assertEquals(1, gateOf(1, "chapter_end_2")) // one-shot gate (end of chapter 2)
        // У остальных сцен гейта нет.
        assertEquals(null, gateOf(0, "start"))
        assertEquals(null, gateOf(0, "health_test"))
        assertEquals(null, gateOf(0, "items_test"))
        assertEquals(null, gateOf(1, "conditions_test"))
        assertEquals(null, gateOf(2, "final"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `cross-chapter next_scene is allowed`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        // Демонстрация: сцена из главы 2 может вести в сцену главы 3
        // напрямую. Это разрешено: главы — нарративная группировка, а не
        // барьеры. Гейт 4000 шагов на chapter_end_2 обходится — автор
        // делает это намеренно (демо для тестового приключения).
        val conditions = adv.chapters[1].scenes.first { it.id == SceneId("conditions_test") }
        val jumpChoice = conditions.choices.first {
            it.nextScene == SceneId("final")
        }
        assertEquals("В финал (демо межглавного перехода)", jumpChoice.text)
    }

    @Test
    fun `death scene present and fully enabled`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        val death = assertNotNull(adv.deathScene)
        assertEquals(SceneId("death_scene"), death.id)
        assertTrue(death.allowStepBack)
        assertTrue(death.allowChapterRestart)
        assertTrue(death.allowAdventureRestart)
    }

    @Test
    fun `tags registry`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        assertEquals(11, adv.tags.size)
        val health = adv.tags.first { it.name == "health" }
        assertEquals(TagCategory.HEALTH, health.category)
        assertTrue(health.visible)
        val sword = adv.tags.first { it.name == "sword" }
        assertEquals(TagCategory.ITEM, sword.category)
        assertEquals("Ржавый меч", sword.displayName)
    }

    @Test
    fun `initial state`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        assertEquals(listOf("initial_flag"), adv.initialState.flags)
        assertEquals(100, adv.initialState.stats["health"])
        assertEquals(3, adv.initialState.stats["potion"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `start scene has seven choices`() {
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        val start = adv.chapters[0].scenes.first { it.id == SceneId("start") }
        assertEquals(7, start.choices.size)
    }

    @Test
    fun `sword_gt_zero condition parsed as Compare AST`() {
        // Ф1.7.1a-fix3: the sample used `has_sword` (legacy semantics,
        // where `has_X` was true if X was a flag OR a positive stat).
        // Since Ф1.5, `has_X` means "boolean flag X is set" and does
        // NOT look at stats. `sword` is an ItemCount, so `has_sword`
        // evaluated to false — the button was always disabled. The
        // sample now uses `sword > 0`, which matches the new
        // semantics. Type checker (Ф2.2) will reject the legacy form
        // with a hint to use `Compare` instead.
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        val start = adv.chapters[0].scenes.first { it.id == SceneId("start") }
        val hasSwordChoice = start.choices.first { it.text.startsWith("Проверить условие") }
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Compare("sword", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            hasSwordChoice.condition,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `final scene is marked as ending`() {
        // Ф1.7.0: the reference sample's `final` scene must be marked
        // "is_ending": true. The old behavior ("no choices = implicit
        // end") was dropped; the analyzer now flags an unmarked terminal
        // as DeadEnd ERROR. If this assertion fails, either the file was
        // edited (check docs/test-adventure-policy.md Rule 7) or the
        // parser stopped reading is_ending (bug in JsonToIr).
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        val final = adv.chapters[2].scenes.first { it.id == SceneId("final") }
        assertTrue(final.isEnding, "final scene must have is_ending = true")
        assertTrue(final.choices.isEmpty(), "final scene must have no choices")
    }

    @Test
    fun `gate_test is repeatable, chapter ends are not`() {
        // Ф1.7.0.4: the only "path" example (you walk there, walk back
        // if you return) is gate_test — per-visit. The chapter-end
        // gates use the default "once passed, stays passed in this
        // playthrough" (repeatable = false). This test pins both so that
        // the reference sample keeps demonstrating both modes.
        //
        // Ф3.4-fix2: gate moved from `health_test` to `gate_test` so
        // that testing health/items/journal does not require walking.
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        fun gateOf(chapterIndex: Int, sceneId: String) =
            adv.chapters[chapterIndex].scenes
                .first { it.id == SceneId(sceneId) }
                .gate

        assertEquals(true, gateOf(0, "gate_test")?.repeatable)
        assertEquals(false, gateOf(0, "chapter_end_1")?.repeatable)
        assertEquals(false, gateOf(1, "chapter_end_2")?.repeatable)
    }

    @Test
    fun `invariants has health rule`() {
        // Ф3.5: reference sample declares health <= 0 => death,
        // matching the pre-Ф3.5 fallback but explicit. This test pins
        // the format and one semantic check.
        val adv = parseRealFile()
        assertEquals(1, adv.invariants.size)
        val inv = adv.invariants.single()
        assertEquals(
            com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Outcome.Death,
            inv.outcome,
        )
        val condition = inv.condition
        assertIs<com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition.Compare>(condition)
        assertEquals(
            com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp.LE,
            condition.op,
        )
    }
}

FILE: engine/src/test/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/format/SchemaFingerprintTest.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.DeathScene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagDefinition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Gate
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TemplateRef
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarDecl
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.VariableDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Invariant
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Outcome
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.VarDeclDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceTemplate
import kotlinx.serialization.descriptors.SerialDescriptor
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals

/**
 * Schema fingerprint: pins the **names** of every serialized field in the
 * IR, independent of values.
 *
 * **Why this test exists.** `GoldenIrTest` compares **values** against
 * `golden_ir.json` with `encodeDefaults = false`. That catches value
 * changes and renames, but it does **not** catch **added** or **removed**
 * fields that carry defaults: such a field is simply absent from the
 * serialized output, and the golden stays byte-for-byte identical. If
 * someone adds `Adventure.age: Int = 0`, or accidentally loses
 * `Adventure.version` (e.g. by removing `@Serializable` from a field
 * without changing the type), `GoldenIrTest` would stay green and the
 * schema change would ship unnoticed.
 *
 * This test closes that gap by pinning **field names and sealed variants**
 * per class. Adding, removing, or renaming any serialized field breaks the
 * test with a message naming the class. The author then either reverts
 * (unintended change) or updates the corresponding map in this test in the
 * same PR (intended change).
 *
 * **Why a hardcoded map instead of a recursive walk of
 * `serializer().descriptor`.** The hardcoded map is read by a human in the
 * PR diff: "added `age` to `Adventure` and to `expectedFlatFields`". A
 * recursive walk would also catch the change, but the diff would be
 * "test failed, fields changed" without a clear pointer to what is
 * expected. The hardcoded map **is** the documentation of the schema.
 *
 * **What this test does NOT check.** It does not pin field types,
 * nullability, default values, or field-level `@SerialName` **values**
 * (although the descriptor returns the serialized name, so a change to
 * `@SerialName("display_name")` → `@SerialName("displayName")` would show
 * up here as a rename). It also does not cover the value classes
 * (`SceneId`, `ChoiceId`, `Gate`) — those serialize transparently as
 * bare strings/ints, so they have no "fields" in the JSON to pin. If a
 * value class ever gains a custom serializer, add it here as a new entry.
 *
 * **Maintenance.** When you intentionally add/remove/rename a field or a
 * sealed variant, update the corresponding map below. The diff in your PR
 * will show both the class change and the fingerprint update side by side.
 * When you add a **new flat IR class** (a new `data class` with
 * `@Serializable`), add it to `expectedFlatFields` **and** to the
 * `flat class fields match expected fingerprint` test below.
 */
class SchemaFingerprintTest {

    private val expectedFlatFields: Map<String, Set<String>> = mapOf(
        "Adventure" to setOf(
            "version", "title", "author", "description",
            "variables", "choice_templates", "invariants", "tags",
            "initial_state", "death_scene", "start_scene", "chapters",
        ),
        "Chapter" to setOf("id", "title", "scenes"),
        "Scene" to setOf("id", "text", "effects", "choices", "gate", "is_ending", "merge", "merge_sources"),
        "Choice" to setOf(
            "id", "text", "next_scene", "condition", "visibility_condition",
            "effects", "template_ref",
        ),
        "TemplateRef" to setOf("template_id", "args"),
        "TagDefinition" to setOf("name", "display_name", "category", "visible"),
        "InitialState" to setOf("flags", "stats"),
        "DeathScene" to setOf(
            "id", "text", "allow_step_back", "allow_chapter_restart", "allow_adventure_restart",
        ),
        "VarDecl" to setOf("name", "type"),
        "Gate" to setOf("required_steps", "repeatable"),
        "VariableDto" to setOf("type", "min", "max"),
        "ChoiceTemplate" to setOf(
            "id", "parameters", "text",
            "visibility_condition", "availability_condition",
            "effects", "next_scene",
        ),
        "VarDeclDto" to setOf("name", "type", "min", "max"),
        "Invariant" to setOf("condition", "outcome"),
    )

    /** Serialized variant name (from `@SerialName`) → its serialized fields. */
    private val expectedConditionVariants: Map<String, Set<String>> = mapOf(
        "literal" to setOf("value"),
        "var_ref" to setOf("name"),
        "has" to setOf("name"),
        "not" to setOf("inner"),
        "and" to setOf("left", "right"),
        "or" to setOf("left", "right"),
        "compare" to setOf("var_name", "op", "value"),
        "in_range" to setOf("var_name", "min", "max"),
    )

    private val expectedEffectVariants: Map<String, Set<String>> = mapOf(
        "set_flag" to setOf("name"),
        "remove_flag" to setOf("name"),
        "modify_stat" to setOf("name", "delta"),
        "set" to setOf("name", "value"),
    )

    private val expectedVarTypeVariants: Map<String, Set<String>> = mapOf(
        "bool" to emptySet(),
        "int" to emptySet(),
        "int_min" to setOf("min"),
        "int_range" to setOf("min", "max"),
        "item_count" to emptySet(),
        "item_list" to emptySet(),
    )

    private fun fieldNames(descriptor: SerialDescriptor): Set<String> =
        (0 until descriptor.elementsCount)
            .map { descriptor.getElementName(it) }
            .toSet()

    /**
     * Drill into a **polymorphic** descriptor (which is how `kotlinx.serialization`
     * exposes sealed-class serializers when the sealed type is used as a
     * field or as a top-level value). The descriptor has two elements:
     * `type` (the discriminator) and `value` (the actual payload). The
     * variants live inside `value`; each variant's fields live one level
     * further.
     */
    private fun polymorphicVariants(descriptor: SerialDescriptor): Map<String, Set<String>> {
        require(descriptor.elementsCount == 2) {
            "Expected polymorphic descriptor (2 elements: type, value), got " +
                    "${descriptor.elementsCount}: " +
                    (0 until descriptor.elementsCount).map { descriptor.getElementName(it) }
        }
        require(
            descriptor.getElementName(0) == "type" &&
                    descriptor.getElementName(1) == "value",
        ) {
            "Unexpected polymorphic descriptor shape: " +
                    (0 until descriptor.elementsCount).map { descriptor.getElementName(it) }
        }
        val valueDescriptor = descriptor.getElementDescriptor(1)
        return (0 until valueDescriptor.elementsCount).associate { i ->
            val variantName = valueDescriptor.getElementName(i)
            val variantDescriptor = valueDescriptor.getElementDescriptor(i)
            variantName to fieldNames(variantDescriptor)
        }
    }

    private fun assertFlat(name: String, descriptor: SerialDescriptor) {
        val expected = expectedFlatFields[name]
            ?: error(
                "No entry for '$name' in expectedFlatFields. " +
                        "Add it here AND in the test that calls assertFlat('$name', ...).",
            )
        val actual = fieldNames(descriptor)
        assertEquals(
            expected,
            actual,
            "Serialized fields of $name changed. " +
                    "If the change is intentional, update expectedFlatFields in this test and commit it " +
                    "in the same PR as the IR change. If not, revert the IR change.",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `flat class fields match expected fingerprint`() {
        assertFlat("Adventure", Adventure.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("Chapter", Chapter.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("Scene", Scene.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("Choice", Choice.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("TemplateRef", TemplateRef.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("TagDefinition", TagDefinition.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("InitialState", InitialState.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("DeathScene", DeathScene.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("VarDecl", VarDecl.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("Gate", Gate.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("VariableDto", VariableDto.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("ChoiceTemplate", ChoiceTemplate.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("VarDeclDto", VarDeclDto.serializer().descriptor)
        assertFlat("Invariant", Invariant.serializer().descriptor)
    }

    @Test
    fun `Condition sealed variants match expected fingerprint`() {
        assertEquals(
            expectedConditionVariants,
            polymorphicVariants(Condition.serializer().descriptor),
            "Condition sealed variants changed. Update expectedConditionVariants if intentional.",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `Effect sealed variants match expected fingerprint`() {
        assertEquals(
            expectedEffectVariants,
            polymorphicVariants(Effect.serializer().descriptor),
            "Effect sealed variants changed. Update expectedEffectVariants if intentional.",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `VarType sealed variants match expected fingerprint`() {
        assertEquals(
            expectedVarTypeVariants,
            polymorphicVariants(VarType.serializer().descriptor),
            "VarType sealed variants changed. Update expectedVarTypeVariants if intentional.",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `VarType IntMin round-trips through serializer`() {
        // Pins two things that the fingerprint test above cannot see:
        //  1. the polymorphic discriminator serializes as "int_min"
        //     (not "intmin" or "IntMin");
        //  2. the `min` field actually survives encode → decode.
        // Serializes through the same `Json { }` that :app will use
        // (encodeDefaults = true for readability in the test output).
        val json = kotlinx.serialization.json.Json { encodeDefaults = true }
        val original = VarType.IntMin(min = 5)
        val text = json.encodeToString(VarType.serializer(), original)
        kotlin.test.assertTrue(
            text.contains("\"int_min\""),
            "expected polymorphic type name 'int_min' in serialized JSON, got: $text",
        )
        val decoded = json.decodeFromString(VarType.serializer(), text)
        kotlin.test.assertEquals(original, decoded)
    }

    @Test
    fun `Outcome sealed variants match expected fingerprint`() {
        // Ф3.5: the only invariant outcome today is `Death`. When a
        // future variant (`Ending`, `Custom`) is added, this test fails
        // and the author updates it in the same PR as the Outcome change.
        assertEquals(
            mapOf("death" to emptySet<String>()),
            polymorphicVariants(Outcome.serializer().descriptor),
            "Outcome sealed variants changed. Update this test if intentional.",
        )
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto

import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertNull

class AdventureDtoTest {

    private val json = Json {
        ignoreUnknownKeys = true
        coerceInputValues = true
    }

    @Test
    fun `minimal adventure`() {
        val input = """
            {
              "title": "Test",
              "chapters": [
                {
                  "id": "c1",
                  "scenes": [
                    {"id": "s1", "text": "Hello"}
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
        """.trimIndent()
        val dto = json.decodeFromString<AdventureDto>(input)
        assertEquals("Test", dto.title)
        assertEquals(1, dto.chapters.size)
        assertEquals("c1", dto.chapters[0].id)
        assertEquals(0, dto.chapters[0].requiredSteps)
        assertEquals(1, dto.chapters[0].scenes.size)
        assertEquals("s1", dto.chapters[0].scenes[0].id)
        assertEquals(0, dto.chapters[0].scenes[0].choices.size)
    }

    @Test
    fun `version absent means null in DTO`() {
        val input = """{"title":"Test","chapters":[]}"""
        val dto = json.decodeFromString<AdventureDto>(input)
        assertNull(dto.version)
    }

    @Test
    fun `version present is read`() {
        val input = """{"version":2,"title":"Test","chapters":[]}"""
        val dto = json.decodeFromString<AdventureDto>(input)
        assertEquals(2, dto.version)
    }

    @Test
    fun `explicit null field becomes default`() {
        val input = """
            {"title":"Test","author":null,"chapters":[
              {"id":"c1","scenes":[{"id":"s1","text":"Hello","set_flags":null}]}
            ]}
        """.trimIndent()
        val dto = json.decodeFromString<AdventureDto>(input)
        assertEquals("", dto.author)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), dto.chapters[0].scenes[0].setFlags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `choice with condition and effects`() {
        val input = """
            {
              "title": "T",
              "chapters": [{
                "id": "c1",
                "scenes": [{
                  "id": "s1",
                  "text": "Hello",
                  "choices": [{
                    "text": "Go",
                    "next_scene": "s2",
                    "condition": "has_sword",
                    "modify_stats": {"health": -5}
                  }]
                }]
              }]
            }
        """.trimIndent()
        val dto = json.decodeFromString<AdventureDto>(input)
        val choice = dto.chapters[0].scenes[0].choices[0]
        assertEquals("Go", choice.text)
        assertEquals("s2", choice.nextScene)
        assertEquals("has_sword", choice.condition)
        assertEquals(mapOf("health" to -5), choice.modifyStats)
    }

    @Test
    fun `unknown keys are ignored`() {
        val input = """{"title":"T","chapters":[],"future_field":"x"}"""
        json.decodeFromString<AdventureDto>(input)
    }
}

FILE: engine/src/test/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/TemplateApplierTest.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarDecl
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertFailsWith
import kotlin.test.assertNotNull
import kotlin.test.assertNull
import kotlin.test.assertTrue

class TemplateApplierTest {

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    private fun template(
        id: String = "use_item",
        parameters: List<VarDecl> = listOf(VarDecl("itemId", VarType.ItemCount)),
        text: String = "Use {itemId}",
        visibilityCondition: Condition? = null,
        availabilityCondition: Condition? = null,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
        nextScene: String = "back",
    ): ChoiceTemplate = ChoiceTemplate(
        id = id,
        parameters = parameters,
        text = text,
        visibilityCondition = visibilityCondition,
        availabilityCondition = availabilityCondition,
        effects = effects,
        nextScene = SceneId(nextScene),
    )

    // ---------- happy path ----------

    @Test
    fun `text placeholder substituted`() {
        val c = applyTemplate(
            template = template(),
            args = mapOf("itemId" to "potion"),
            choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
        )
        assertEquals("Use potion", c.text)
    }

    @Test
    fun `different args produce different text`() {
        val t = template()
        val potion = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "potion"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        val sword = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "sword"), ChoiceId("c2"))
        assertEquals("Use potion", potion.text)
        assertEquals("Use sword", sword.text)
        assertTrue(potion.text != sword.text)
    }

    @Test
    fun `availability condition substituted - different args produce different conditions`() {
        val t = template(
            availabilityCondition = Condition.Compare("itemId", CompareOp.GT, 0),
        )
        val potion = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "potion"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        val sword = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "sword"), ChoiceId("c2"))
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Compare("potion", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            potion.condition,
        )
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Compare("sword", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            sword.condition,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `visibility condition substituted`() {
        val t = template(
            visibilityCondition = Condition.Has("itemId"),
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "potion"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertEquals(Condition.Has("potion"), c.visibilityCondition)
    }

    @Test
    fun `effects substituted - different args produce different effects`() {
        // B1 semantics: only exact name-slot matches are substituted.
        // Both sides of a two-effect list would need to reference the
        // same parameter exactly. One effect is enough to demonstrate
        // "different args → different effects" (the DoD requirement).
        val t = template(
            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("itemId", -1)),
        )
        val potion = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "potion"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        val sword = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "sword"), ChoiceId("c2"))
        assertEquals(
            listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("potion", -1)),
            potion.effects,
        )
        assertEquals(
            listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("sword", -1)),
            sword.effects,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `nested condition substituted - And`() {
        // B1 semantics: exact match. `other_flag` is not a parameter and
        // stays as-is; `itemId` is a parameter and gets substituted inside
        // the And tree. This demonstrates that substitution recurses into
        // nested conditions.
        val t = template(
            availabilityCondition = Condition.And(
                Condition.Has("other_flag"),
                Condition.Compare("itemId", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            ),
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "potion"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(
                Condition.Has("other_flag"),
                Condition.Compare("potion", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            ),
            c.condition,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `InRange substituted`() {
        val t = template(
            parameters = listOf(VarDecl("stat", VarType.IntRange(0, 100))),
            text = "{stat}",
            availabilityCondition = Condition.InRange("stat", 0, 100),
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("stat" to "health"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertEquals(Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100), c.condition)
    }

    @Test
    fun `Effect Set name substituted, value not`() {
        val t = template(
            parameters = listOf(VarDecl("stat", VarType.IntMin(0))),
            text = "{stat}",
            effects = listOf(Effect.Set("stat", 42)),
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("stat" to "health"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.Set("health", 42)), c.effects)
    }

    @Test
    fun `non-parameter names left as-is`() {
        // Template references a global variable `health` (not a parameter).
        val t = template(
            availabilityCondition = Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 0),
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "potion"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            c.condition,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `prefix composition is not substituted - exact match only (B1)`() {
        // B1 decision (Ф4.2.1): exact match only in AST name slots.
        // `has_itemId` is a **composed** name, not `has_` + parameter —
        // it does not equal any parameter name, so it stays as-is.
        // This is by design: predictable semantics, no ambiguity about
        // which substring is a parameter. Authors who need `has_potion`
        // derived from `itemId` pass a **dedicated Bool parameter**:
        //   parameters: [itemId: ItemCount, hasItem: Bool]
        //   args: {itemId: "potion", hasItem: "has_potion"}
        //   template uses: Has("hasItem") → Has("has_potion")
        // The alternative (prefix substitution) was rejected: it would
        // require a disambiguation rule (`has_` is reserved? what about
        // a literal flag named `has_itemId`?) and would complicate
        // future JSON parsing. See `docs/engine-architecture.md`
        // §"Choice templates" for the record.
        //
        // This test pins the current behaviour so a future "improvement"
        // to prefix substitution is a deliberate decision, not an
        // accidental one.
        val t = template(
            availabilityCondition = Condition.Has("has_itemId"),
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("itemId" to "potion"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Has("has_itemId"),
            c.condition,
            "Prefix composition must NOT be substituted (B1). " +
                    "If you want to change this, update the B1 decision record " +
                    "in docs/engine-architecture.md and this test in the same PR.",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `templateRef set on expanded choice`() {
        val c = applyTemplate(
            template = template(),
            args = mapOf("itemId" to "potion"),
            choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
        )
        val ref = assertNotNull(c.templateRef)
        assertEquals("use_item", ref.templateId)
        assertEquals(mapOf("itemId" to "potion"), ref.args)
    }

    @Test
    fun `nextScene not substituted`() {
        val t = template(
            parameters = listOf(VarDecl("sceneId", VarType.Bool)),
            nextScene = "back",
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(t, mapOf("sceneId" to "somewhere"), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertEquals(SceneId("back"), c.nextScene)
    }

    // ---------- validation ----------

    @Test
    fun `missing parameter argument throws`() {
        assertFailsWith<IllegalArgumentException> {
            applyTemplate(
                template = template(),
                args = emptyMap(),
                choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
            )
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `extra argument throws`() {
        assertFailsWith<IllegalArgumentException> {
            applyTemplate(
                template = template(),
                args = mapOf("itemId" to "potion", "typo" to "x"),
                choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
            )
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `no parameters - empty args works`() {
        val t = template(
            parameters = emptyList(),
            text = "Leave",
            availabilityCondition = null,
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(t, emptyMap(), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertEquals("Leave", c.text)
    }

    // ---------- Adventure extension ----------

    @Test
    fun `Adventure applyTemplate finds template by id`() {
        val t = template()
        val adventure = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("s1"),
            choiceTemplates = listOf(t),
            chapters = listOf(
                Chapter(
                    id = "ch",
                    title = "ch",
                    scenes = listOf(Scene(SceneId("s1"), "text", isEnding = true)),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val c = adventure.applyTemplate(
            templateId = "use_item",
            args = mapOf("itemId" to "potion"),
            choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
        )
        assertNotNull(c)
        assertEquals("Use potion", c.text)
    }

    @Test
    fun `Adventure applyTemplate returns null for missing template`() {
        val adventure = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("s1"),
            chapters = listOf(
                Chapter(
                    id = "ch",
                    title = "ch",
                    scenes = listOf(Scene(SceneId("s1"), "text", isEnding = true)),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val c = adventure.applyTemplate("no_such_template", emptyMap(), ChoiceId("c1"))
        assertNull(c)
    }


    // ---------- Ф4.3.2a: @self ----------

    @Test
    fun `@self resolved to currentSceneId when provided`() {
        val t = template(
            nextScene = "@self",
        )
        val c = applyTemplate(
            template = t,
            args = mapOf("itemId" to "potion"),
            choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
            currentSceneId = SceneId("forest_path"),
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("forest_path"), c.nextScene)
    }

    @Test
    fun `@self without currentSceneId throws`() {
        val t = template(
            nextScene = "@self",
        )
        assertFailsWith<IllegalArgumentException> {
            applyTemplate(
                template = t,
                args = mapOf("itemId" to "potion"),
                choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
            )
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `Adventure applyTemplate forwards currentSceneId`() {
        val t = template(nextScene = "@self")
        val adventure = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("s1"),
            choiceTemplates = listOf(t),
            chapters = listOf(
                Chapter(
                    id = "ch",
                    title = "ch",
                    scenes = listOf(Scene(SceneId("s1"), "text", isEnding = true)),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val c = adventure.applyTemplate(
            templateId = "use_item",
            args = mapOf("itemId" to "potion"),
            choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
            currentSceneId = SceneId("s1"),
        )
        assertNotNull(c)
        assertEquals(SceneId("s1"), c.nextScene)
    }

    @Test
    fun `non-@self nextScene ignores currentSceneId`() {
        // Sanity: currentSceneId is not a general "overwrite nextScene"
        // knob — only `@self` uses it.
        val t = template(nextScene = "back")
        val c = applyTemplate(
            template = t,
            args = mapOf("itemId" to "potion"),
            choiceId = ChoiceId("c1"),
            currentSceneId = SceneId("forest_path"),
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("back"), c.nextScene)
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagDefinition
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs

/**
 * Unit tests for [TypeChecker].
 *
 * Covers the three DoD cases (`UnknownVariable`, `HasOnNonBool`, wrong
 * type for `initial_state`) and the extra effect checks adopted in
 * Ф2.2 (B2 decision, 2026-11-12): `SetFlagOnNonBool`,
 * `RemoveFlagOnNonBool`, `ModifyStatOnNonNumeric`, `CompareOnNonNumeric`,
 * `InRangeOnNonNumeric`.
 *
 * Also covers fallback mode (C4 decision, 2026-11-12): with an empty
 * `Adventure.variables`, types are inferred from `tags` + `initialState`,
 * and a typo like `has_swrod` still produces [TypeError.UnknownVariable].
 *
 * **What is NOT here.** `health >= "abc"` — that is a **parse** error,
 * caught by `ConditionParser` in Ф1.3.1 before the IR exists (see
 * `ConditionParserTest > non-integer value fails`). Ф2.2 does not
 * re-check parse-level errors.
 */
class TypeCheckerTest {

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    private fun variables(vararg pairs: Pair<String, VarType>): Map<String, VarDecl> =
        pairs.associate { (name, type) -> name to VarDecl(name, type) }

    private fun adventure(
        variables: Map<String, VarDecl> = emptyMap(),
        tags: List<TagDefinition> = emptyList(),
        initialState: InitialState = InitialState(),
        vararg scenes: Scene,
    ): Adventure {
        val start = scenes.firstOrNull()?.id ?: SceneId("start")
        return Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = start,
            variables = variables,
            tags = tags,
            initialState = initialState,
            chapters = listOf(Chapter("ch", "ch", scenes.toList())),
        )
    }

    private fun scene(
        id: String,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
        choices: List<Choice> = emptyList(),
    ): Scene = Scene(
        id = SceneId(id),
        text = "text of $id",
        effects = effects,
        choices = choices,
    )

    private fun choice(
        id: String = "c1",
        next: String = "start",
        condition: Condition? = null,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
    ): Choice = Choice(
        id = ChoiceId(id),
        text = "go",
        nextScene = SceneId(next),
        condition = condition,
        effects = effects,
    )

    // ---------- empty input ----------

    @Test
    fun `empty adventure returns no errors`() {
        // No variables, no tags, no initial state -> type table empty ->
        // nothing to check against. The "you have not declared variables"
        // signal is a UI concern, not a TypeError (see TypeChecker KDoc).
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("start"),
            chapters = listOf(Chapter("ch", "ch", listOf(Scene(SceneId("start"), "text")))),
        )
        assertEquals(emptyList(), TypeChecker.check(adv))
    }

    // ---------- strict mode: unknown variable ----------

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - unknown variable in condition`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("sword" to VarType.ItemCount),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", choices = listOf(choice(condition = Condition.Has("never_declared")))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertEquals(1, errors.size)
        assertIs<TypeError.UnknownVariable>(errors.single())
        assertEquals("never_declared", (errors.single() as TypeError.UnknownVariable).name)
        assertEquals(SceneId("start"), errors.single().sceneId)
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - unknown variable in effect`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("gold" to VarType.IntMin(0)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("never_declared", 1))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertEquals(1, errors.size)
        assertIs<TypeError.UnknownVariable>(errors.single())
    }

    // ---------- strict mode: HasOnNonBool ----------

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - has on ItemCount is HasOnNonBool`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("sword" to VarType.ItemCount),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", choices = listOf(choice(condition = Condition.Has("sword")))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertEquals(1, errors.size)
        assertIs<TypeError.HasOnNonBool>(errors.single())
        assertEquals("sword", (errors.single() as TypeError.HasOnNonBool).name)
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - has on IntRange is HasOnNonBool`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("health" to VarType.IntRange(0, 100)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", choices = listOf(choice(condition = Condition.Has("health")))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.HasOnNonBool>(errors.single())
    }

    // ---------- strict mode: effect type checks (B2) ----------

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - set_flag on numeric is SetFlagOnNonBool`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("gold" to VarType.IntMin(0)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.SetFlag("gold"))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.SetFlagOnNonBool>(errors.single())
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - remove_flag on Bool-free numeric is RemoveFlagOnNonBool`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("score" to VarType.Integer),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.RemoveFlag("score"))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.RemoveFlagOnNonBool>(errors.single())
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - modify_stat on Bool is ModifyStatOnNonNumeric`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("has_key" to VarType.Bool),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("has_key", 1))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.ModifyStatOnNonNumeric>(errors.single())
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - compare on Bool is CompareOnNonNumeric`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("has_key" to VarType.Bool),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene(
                    "start",
                    choices = listOf(
                        choice(condition = Condition.Compare("has_key", CompareOp.GT, 0)),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.CompareOnNonNumeric>(errors.single())
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - in_range on Bool is InRangeOnNonNumeric`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("has_key" to VarType.Bool),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene(
                    "start",
                    choices = listOf(
                        choice(condition = Condition.InRange("has_key", 0, 1)),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.InRangeOnNonNumeric>(errors.single())
    }

    // ---------- strict mode: initial state checks (B2) ----------

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - initial flag on numeric is InitialFlagOnNonBool`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("health" to VarType.IntRange(0, 100)),
            initialState = InitialState(flags = listOf("health")),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        val e = errors.single()
        assertIs<TypeError.InitialFlagOnNonBool>(e)
        assertEquals(null, e.sceneId)
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - initial stat on Bool is InitialStatOnNonNumeric`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("has_key" to VarType.Bool),
            initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("has_key" to 1)),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        val e = errors.single()
        assertIs<TypeError.InitialStatOnNonNumeric>(e)
        assertEquals(null, e.sceneId)
    }

    // ---------- strict mode: clean cases ----------

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - clean adventure returns empty list`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables(
                "sword" to VarType.ItemCount,
                "health" to VarType.IntRange(0, 100),
                "has_key" to VarType.Bool,
            ),
            initialState = InitialState(
                flags = listOf("has_key"),
                stats = mapOf("sword" to 1, "health" to 100),
            ),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene(
                    "start",
                    choices = listOf(
                        choice(
                            condition = Condition.Has("has_key"),
                            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10)),
                        ),
                        choice(
                            id = "c2",
                            condition = Condition.Compare("sword", CompareOp.GT, 0),
                            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("sword", -1)),
                        ),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(emptyList(), TypeChecker.check(adv))
    }

    // ---------- strict mode: variables wins over tags ----------

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - variable in tags but not in variables is UnknownVariable`() {
        // `variables` is non-empty -> strict mode. `tags` is ignored for
        // type inference; the only source of truth is `variables`. So a
        // name that is in `tags` but not in `variables` is unknown, not
        // "found via tag".
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("gold" to VarType.IntMin(0)),
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("sword", category = TagCategory.ITEM)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("sword", 1))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.UnknownVariable>(errors.single())
        assertEquals("sword", (errors.single() as TypeError.UnknownVariable).name)
    }

    // ---------- fallback mode (empty variables) ----------

    @Test
    fun `fallback - typo in has flag produces UnknownVariable`() {
        // No variables; `sword` is a tag (ITEM). Condition uses `swrod` —
        // a typo. In fallback mode `sword` is inferred as ItemCount, but
        // `swrod` is not in the inferred table at all, so it is
        // UnknownVariable.
        //
        // This is the DoD requirement ("опечатка `has_swrod` → ошибка").
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("sword", category = TagCategory.ITEM)),
            initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("sword" to 1)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", choices = listOf(choice(condition = Condition.Has("swrod")))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertEquals(1, errors.size)
        assertIs<TypeError.UnknownVariable>(errors.single())
        assertEquals("swrod", (errors.single() as TypeError.UnknownVariable).name)
    }

    @Test
    fun `fallback - has on item tag produces HasOnNonBool`() {
        // ITEM -> ItemCount. `has_sword` on ItemCount is the same mistake
        // as in strict mode.
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("sword", category = TagCategory.ITEM)),
            initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("sword" to 1)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", choices = listOf(choice(condition = Condition.Has("sword")))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertEquals(1, errors.size)
        assertIs<TypeError.HasOnNonBool>(errors.single())
    }

    @Test
    fun `fallback - journal in initial flags treated as Bool`() {
        // No tags, but `started` is in `initialState.flags` -> Bool.
        val adv = adventure(
            initialState = InitialState(flags = listOf("started")),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", choices = listOf(choice(condition = Condition.Has("started")))),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(emptyList(), TypeChecker.check(adv))
    }

    @Test
    fun `fallback - health tag treated as IntMin, modify_stat allowed`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("health", category = TagCategory.HEALTH)),
            initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10))),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(emptyList(), TypeChecker.check(adv))
    }

    @Test
    fun `fallback - item tag treated as ItemCount, modify_stat allowed`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("potion", category = TagCategory.ITEM)),
            initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("potion" to 3)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("potion", -1))),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(emptyList(), TypeChecker.check(adv))
    }

    // ---------- sorting ----------

    @Test
    fun `initial state errors come before scene errors`() {
        // Both errors are present; InitialState errors (sceneId = null)
        // must come first in the sorted output.
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("health" to VarType.Bool),
            initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("never", 1))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertEquals(2, errors.size)
        assertIs<TypeError.InitialStatOnNonNumeric>(errors[0])
        assertIs<TypeError.UnknownVariable>(errors[1])
    }

    @Test
    fun `errors are sorted by scene id then by message`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("gold" to VarType.IntMin(0)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("z_scene", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("unknown_z", 1))),
                scene("a_scene", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("unknown_a", 1))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertEquals(2, errors.size)
        assertEquals("a_scene", errors[0].sceneId?.value)
        assertEquals("z_scene", errors[1].sceneId?.value)
    }

    @Test
    fun `multiple errors in one scene are all reported`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("has_key" to VarType.Bool),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene(
                    "start",
                    choices = listOf(
                        choice(
                            id = "c1",
                            effects = listOf(
                                Effect.ModifyStat("has_key", 1),          // Bool used as numeric
                                Effect.SetFlag("unknown_flag"),           // unknown
                            ),
                        ),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertEquals(2, errors.size)
        assertIs<TypeError.ModifyStatOnNonNumeric>(errors[0])
        assertIs<TypeError.UnknownVariable>(errors[1])
    }

    // ---------- integration: test_adventure.json is type-clean ----------

    @Test
    fun `real test_adventure_json is type-clean`() {
        // Sanity check before Ф2.3 wires TypeChecker into JsonToIr.parse:
        // the reference sample must pass the type checker. If it does not,
        // either the sample is broken (fix test_adventure.json) or the
        // fallback mode (C4) is too strict (fix TypeChecker). Do not wire
        // the checker into parse until this is green.
        //
        // After Ф2.3, this test will be replaced by a stronger one:
        // "JsonToIr.parse returns Success for test_adventure.json" — the
        // same guarantee, expressed at the pipeline level instead of
        // manually invoking TypeChecker.check. The current form is what
        // makes the wiring safe to do in the first place.
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream("/test_adventure.json")
            ?: error("test_adventure.json not on classpath")
        val raw = stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
        val parseResult = com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr.parse(raw)
        val adventure = when (parseResult) {
            is com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult.Success -> parseResult.value
            is com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult.Failure ->
                error("test_adventure.json failed to parse: ${parseResult.errors}")
        }
        val typeErrors = TypeChecker.check(adventure)
        assertEquals(
            emptyList(),
            typeErrors,
            "test_adventure.json must be type-clean under current rules. " +
                    "Either the sample is broken (fix test_adventure.json) " +
                    "or TypeChecker fallback mode is too strict (fix TypeChecker).",
        )
    }

    // ---------- Ф3.1: Effect.Set ----------

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - set on Bool is ModifyStatOnNonNumeric`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("has_key" to VarType.Bool),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.Set("has_key", 1))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.ModifyStatOnNonNumeric>(errors.single())
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - set on numeric is allowed`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("health" to VarType.IntRange(0, 100)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.Set("health", 100))),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(emptyList(), TypeChecker.check(adv))
    }

    @Test
    fun `strict mode - set unknown variable is UnknownVariable`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            variables = variables("health" to VarType.IntRange(0, 100)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.Set("never_declared", 1))),
            ),
        )
        val errors = TypeChecker.check(adv)
        assertIs<TypeError.UnknownVariable>(errors.single())
    }
