package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagDefinition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs

/**
 * Unit tests for [inferTypes].
 *
 * Covers the priority order documented on [inferTypes]:
 * `HEALTH tag > ITEM tag > numeric usage > Bool usage`.
 *
 * Also verifies the DoD-requirement that on `test_adventure.json` (which
 * since Ф2.8.1 carries an explicit `variables` block) `inferTypes` produces
 * **exactly** the same map the author wrote by hand. If inference drifts
 * from manual declaration, either the file's `variables` is wrong (fix the
 * file) or the inference logic is wrong (fix the code). The test is the
 * tripwire.
 */
class TypeInferenceTest {

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    private fun adventure(
        tags: List<TagDefinition> = emptyList(),
        initialState: InitialState = InitialState(),
        vararg scenes: Scene,
    ): Adventure = Adventure(
        title = "T",
        startScene = scenes.firstOrNull()?.id ?: SceneId("start"),
        tags = tags,
        initialState = initialState,
        chapters = listOf(Chapter("ch", "ch", scenes.toList())),
    )

    private fun scene(
        id: String,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
        choices: List<Choice> = emptyList(),
    ): Scene = Scene(
        id = SceneId(id),
        text = "text of $id",
        effects = effects,
        choices = choices,
    )

    private fun choice(
        condition: Condition? = null,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
    ): Choice = Choice(
        id = ChoiceId("c"),
        text = "go",
        nextScene = SceneId("start"),
        condition = condition,
        effects = effects,
    )

    // ---------- initial state signals ----------

    @Test
    fun `initial flag infers Bool`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            initialState = InitialState(flags = listOf("started")),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.Bool, inferTypes(adv)["started"]?.type)
    }

    @Test
    fun `initial stat infers IntMin zero`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("gold" to 10)),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.IntMin(0), inferTypes(adv)["gold"]?.type)
    }

    // ---------- tag signals ----------

    @Test
    fun `HEALTH tag infers IntMin zero`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("health", category = TagCategory.HEALTH)),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.IntMin(0), inferTypes(adv)["health"]?.type)
    }

    @Test
    fun `ITEM tag infers ItemCount`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("sword", category = TagCategory.ITEM)),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.ItemCount, inferTypes(adv)["sword"]?.type)
    }

    @Test
    fun `JOURNAL tag infers Bool when not in stats`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("seen_dragon", category = TagCategory.JOURNAL)),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.Bool, inferTypes(adv)["seen_dragon"]?.type)
    }

    @Test
    fun `JOURNAL tag infers IntMin when in stats`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("quest_steps", category = TagCategory.JOURNAL)),
            initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("quest_steps" to 0)),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.IntMin(0), inferTypes(adv)["quest_steps"]?.type)
    }

    // ---------- usage signals ----------

    @Test
    fun `SetFlag effect infers Bool`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.SetFlag("found_key"))),

        assertEquals(VarType.Bool, inferTypes(adv)["found_key"]?.type)
    }

    @Test
    fun `RemoveFlag effect infers Bool`() {

                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.RemoveFlag("found_key"))),

        assertEquals(VarType.Bool, inferTypes(adv)["found_key"]?.type)

    @Test

        val adv = adventure(

                scene("start", choices = listOf(choice(condition = Condition.Has("sword")))),

        )
        assertEquals(VarType.Bool, inferTypes(adv)["sword"]?.type)

    @Test

                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10))),

    fun `And condition recurses into both sides`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene(
                    "start",
                    choices = listOf(
                        choice(
                            condition = Condition.And(
                                Condition.Has("has_key"),
                                Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 0),
                            ),
                        ),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val types = inferTypes(adv)
        assertEquals(VarType.Bool, types["has_key"]?.type)
        assertEquals(VarType.IntMin(0), types["health"]?.type)
    }

    // ---------- priority resolution ----------

    @Test
    fun `HEALTH tag wins over Bool usage`() {
        // Contradictory: author declared HEALTH but uses set_flag. Inference
        // prioritises the explicit category — the type checker will report
        // SetFlagOnNonBool on the usage, which is the correct signal for the
        // author to fix one or the other.
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("health", category = TagCategory.HEALTH)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.SetFlag("health"))),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.IntMin(0), inferTypes(adv)["health"]?.type)
    }

    @Test
    fun `ITEM tag wins over numeric usage`() {
        // ITEM is ItemCount; ModifyStat is numeric. Both consistent, but
        // ITEM is more specific and expresses the author's intent more
        // clearly. ItemCount still supports ModifyStat.
        val adv = adventure(
            tags = listOf(TagDefinition("potion", category = TagCategory.ITEM)),
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene("start", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("potion", -1))),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.ItemCount, inferTypes(adv)["potion"]?.type)
    }

    @Test
    fun `numeric usage wins over Bool usage`() {
        // Contradictory: same name set as a flag and modified as a stat.
        // Numeric wins (see inferTypes KDoc — a numeric can appear in
        // set_flag only by mistake, while set_flag is the only way to
        // toggle a Bool). The type checker then reports the set_flag as
        // wrong — a clear signal for the author.
        val adv = adventure(
            scenes = arrayOf(
                scene(
                    "start",
                    effects = listOf(
                        Effect.SetFlag("count"),
                        Effect.ModifyStat("count", 1),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.IntMin(0), inferTypes(adv)["count"]?.type)
    }

    // ---------- edge cases ----------

    @Test
    fun `empty adventure returns empty map`() {
        val adv = adventure(scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")))
        assertEquals(emptyMap(), inferTypes(adv))
    }

    @Test
    fun `name in both flags and stats - numeric wins`() {
        // Pathological: same name in both initial-state collections. The
        // type checker will report InitialFlagOnNonBool or
        // InitialStatOnNonNumeric (depending on what the inferred type
        // ends up being); inference just needs to pick one deterministically.
        // Numeric wins by priority order — that matches the type checker's
        // expectation that ModifyStat / Compare on the name should work.
        val adv = adventure(
            initialState = InitialState(
                flags = listOf("ambiguous"),
                stats = mapOf("ambiguous" to 1),
            ),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        assertEquals(VarType.IntMin(0), inferTypes(adv)["ambiguous"]?.type)
    }

    @Test
    fun `VarDecl name matches map key`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            initialState = InitialState(flags = listOf("started")),
            scenes = arrayOf(scene("start")),
        )
        val decl = inferTypes(adv)["started"]
        assertEquals("started", decl?.name)
    }

    // ---------- integration: test_adventure.json ----------

    @Test
    fun `real test_adventure_json - inference matches declared variables`() {
        // DoD-close: the reference sample now declares its types by hand
        // (added in Ф2.8.1). `inferTypes` must produce exactly the same
        // map — otherwise either the inference logic or the sample is
        // wrong. This test is the tripwire.
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream("/test_adventure.json")
            ?: error("test_adventure.json not on classpath")
        val raw = stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
        val adventure = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(
            JsonToIr.parse(raw),
            "test_adventure.json must parse successfully",
        ).value

        // Precondition: the sample carries an explicit variables block.
        // If someone removes it (breaks 2.8.1), we want a clear message
        // here, not a confusing diff later.
        assertEquals(
            11,
            adventure.variables.size,
            "test_adventure.json should declare exactly 11 variables (see 2.8.1)",
        )

        val inferred = inferTypes(adventure)
        assertEquals(
            adventure.variables,
            inferred,
            "inferTypes must reproduce the sample's manual declarations. " +
                    "If they differ, either the inference logic drifted " +
                    "(fix TypeInference.kt) or the sample was edited " +
                    "inconsistently (fix test_adventure.json).",
        )
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertTrue

class ConditionParserTest {

    private fun success(input: String): Condition {
        val result = ConditionParser.parse(input)
        val s = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Condition>>(result, "expected success for '$input', got $result")
        return s.value
    }

    private fun failure(input: String): List<ParseError> {
        val result = ConditionParser.parse(input)
        val f = assertIs<ParseResult.Failure>(result, "expected failure for '$input', got $result")
        assertTrue(f.errors.isNotEmpty(), "failure must contain at least one error")
        return f.errors
    }

    // ---------- Leaves ----------

    @Test
    fun `has flag`() {
        assertEquals(Condition.Has("sword"), success("has_sword"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `has flag with spaces`() {
        assertEquals(Condition.Has("sword"), success("  has_sword  "))
        assertEquals(Condition.Has("my flag"), success("has_my flag"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `negated has flag`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Has("sword")),
            success("!has_sword"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `all comparison operators`() {
        assertEquals(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50), success("health >= 50"))
        assertEquals(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 50), success("health > 50"))
        assertEquals(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.LE, 50), success("health <= 50"))
        assertEquals(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.LT, 50), success("health < 50"))
        assertEquals(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.EQ, 50), success("health == 50"))
        assertEquals(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.NE, 50), success("health != 50"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `negative integer`() {
        assertEquals(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, -10), success("health >= -10"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `comparison with variable name containing spaces`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Compare("my stat", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            success("my stat > 0"),
        )
    }

    // ---------- Ф3.2: Literal ----------

    @Test
    fun `literal true`() {
        assertEquals(Condition.Literal(true), success("true"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `literal false`() {
        assertEquals(Condition.Literal(false), success("false"))
    }

    // ---------- Ф3.2: InRange ----------

    @Test
    fun `in range simple`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100),
            success("health in 0..100"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `in range with negative bounds`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.InRange("x", -10, 10),
            success("x in -10..10"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `in range with spaces around dots`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100),
            success("health in 0 .. 100"),
        )
    }

    // ---------- Ф3.2: And / Or / Not ----------

    @Test
    fun `simple and`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            success("has_a && has_b"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `simple or`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            success("has_a || has_b"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `and binds tighter than or`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Or(
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                Condition.Has("c"),
            ),
            success("has_a && has_b || has_c"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `or binds looser than and - alternative grouping`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Or(
                Condition.Has("a"),
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("b"), Condition.Has("c")),
            ),
            success("has_a || has_b && has_c"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `parentheses override precedence`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(
                Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                Condition.Has("c"),
            ),
            success("(has_a || has_b) && has_c"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `double not`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("a"))),
            success("!!has_a"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not applies to parenthesized expression`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Not(
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            ),
            success("!(has_a && has_b)"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not applies to comparison`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50)),
            success("!(health >= 50)"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `whitespace is tolerated`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            success("  has_a   &&   has_b  "),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `associative and on three operands`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                Condition.Has("c"),
            ),
            success("has_a && has_b && has_c"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `associative or on three operands`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Or(
                Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                Condition.Has("c"),
            ),
            success("has_a || has_b || has_c"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `and with compare inside`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(
                Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 50),
                Condition.Compare("stamina", CompareOp.GT, 20),
            ),
            success("health > 50 && stamina > 20"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `and with in range`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(
                Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100),
                Condition.Has("shield"),
            ),
            success("health in 0..100 && has_shield"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not before has in and`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(
                Condition.Not(Condition.Has("sword")),
                Condition.Not(Condition.Has("shield")),
            ),
            success("!has_sword && !has_shield"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `literal true and has`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(Condition.Literal(true), Condition.Has("a")),
            success("true && has_a"),
        )
    }

    // ---------- Ф3.2: errors ----------

    @Test
    fun `empty string fails`() {
        failure("")
        failure("   ")
    }

    @Test
    fun `non-integer value fails`() {
        val errors = failure("health >= abc")
        assertIs<ParseError.ConditionError>(errors.single())
    }

    @Test
    fun `bare name without operator fails`() {
        // `health` — not `has_`, not literal, not paren, not in, not
        // compare. `VarRef` is not produced by the parser (Ф3.2:
        // deliberately deferred, see progress log).
        failure("health")
    }

    @Test
    fun `unclosed parenthesis fails`() {
        failure("(has_a")
    }

    @Test
    fun `empty parentheses fail`() {
        failure("()")
    }

    @Test
    fun `unbalanced parentheses fail`() {
        failure("(has_a) && (has_b")
    }

    @Test
    fun `trailing junk after literal fails`() {
        // `true` / `false` require exact match — no trailing tokens.
        failure("true extra")
        failure("false extra")
    }

    @Test
    fun `has_ allows spaces in flag name - documented behavior`() {
        // The parser intentionally allows `has_my flag` → `Has("my flag")`
        // (see `ConditionParser` KDoc — matches `:app` pre-Ф2 reader
        // behaviour where the author had flag names with spaces).
        // So `has_a extra` is `Has("a extra")`, not a parse error. This
        // test pins the design so a future refactor does not accidentally
        // break author files that rely on multi-word flag names.
        assertEquals(Condition.Has("a extra"), success("has_a extra"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `empty operand of or fails`() {
        failure("has_a || ")
        failure(" || has_a")
    }

    @Test
    fun `empty operand of and fails`() {
        failure("has_a && ")
        failure(" && has_a")
    }

    @Test
    fun `single ampersand is rejected`() {
        // "has_a & has_b" — `&` is not a valid operator (must be `&&`).
        failure("has_a & has_b")
    }

    @Test
    fun `single pipe is rejected`() {
        failure("has_a | has_b")
    }

    @Test
    fun `reserved char in flag name is rejected`() {
        // `has_sword&x` — `&` is reserved in a flag name.
        val errors = failure("has_sword&x")
        assertIs<ParseError.ConditionError>(errors.single())
        assertTrue(errors.single().message.contains("reserved character"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `has_sword and health is rejected - DoD Ф2_4 - now at primary level`() {
        // "has_sword && health" — `&&` splits, left parses as `Has("sword")`,
        // right side "health" is a bare name (VarRef — not supported in
        // Ф3.2) → ConditionError. DoD Ф2.4 "has_sword && health produces
        // an error" is preserved, but the error class has moved from
        // "reserved char in flag name" (old parser) to "unrecognized
        // syntax: health" (bare name, no VarRef support).
        val errors = failure("has_sword && health")
        assertIs<ParseError.ConditionError>(errors.single())
    }

    @Test
    fun `has_sword and has_health parses - DoD Ф2_4 via TypeChecker`() {
        // The corrected form: both sides are `has_`, both parse. Then
        // TypeChecker catches `HasOnNonBool` on `sword` (ItemCount) in
        // strict mode. The "has_sword && health is rejected" DoD case is
        // covered by the test above; this test pins the "well-formed
        // grammar" side.
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(
                Condition.Has("sword"),
                Condition.Has("health"),
            ),
            success("has_sword && has_health"),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not then compare parses as Not-Compare`() {
        // "!health > 5" — `!` is unary, applies to "health > 5" (Compare).
        // Result: Not(Compare(health, GT, 5)). With `VarRef` not supported,
        // the author cannot express "(bool) > 5" — that would be a type
        // error anyway. The intuitive reading `!(health > 5)` matches
        // this AST.
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 5)),
            success("!health > 5"),
        )
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertNotEquals

/**
 * Unit tests for [ConditionWriter].
 *
 * Three groups:
 * 1. **True round-trip** — for the condition variants the parser
 *    produces today (`Has`, `Not(Has)`, `Compare`), `parse(write(c))`
 *    is structurally equal to `c`. These are the tests that must stay
 *    green at all times — they are the writer/parser contract.
 * 2. **Canonical string output** — for variants that the parser cannot
 *    produce yet (`And`, `Or`, `Literal`, `VarRef`, `InRange`,
 *    `Not(non-Has)`), the writer produces the string that **Ф3.2** will
 *    accept. Only the string is asserted here; round-trip will be
 *    tested when Ф3.2 lands.
 * 3. **Documented non-round-trip** — explicit negative assertions that
 *    the current parser cannot read back the string the writer produces
 *    for the future variants. When Ф3.2 extends the parser, these tests
 *    fail loudly and the author flips them to `parse(write(c)) == c`.
 */
class ConditionWriterTest {

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    private fun roundTrip(condition: Condition): Condition {
        val written = ConditionWriter.write(condition)
        val parsed = ConditionParser.parse(written)
        val success = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Condition>>(
            parsed,
            "expected '$written' to parse, got $parsed",
        )
        return success.value
    }

    private fun written(condition: Condition): String =
        ConditionWriter.write(condition)

    private fun parseFails(condition: Condition) {
        val written = ConditionWriter.write(condition)
        val parsed = ConditionParser.parse(written)
        assertIs<ParseResult.Failure>(
            parsed,
            "expected '$written' to fail to parse (documented limitation), " +
                    "but it produced ${parsed}",
        )
    }

    // ---------- 1. True round-trip (parser supports today) ----------

    @Test
    fun `has round-trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Has("sword"),
            roundTrip(Condition.Has("sword")),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `has with spaces round-trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Has("my flag"),
            roundTrip(Condition.Has("my flag")),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not has round-trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Has("sword")),
            roundTrip(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("sword"))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare round-trips for all six operators`() {
        val ops = listOf(
            CompareOp.LT, CompareOp.LE, CompareOp.GT,
            CompareOp.GE, CompareOp.EQ, CompareOp.NE,
        )
        for (op in ops) {
            val condition = Condition.Compare("health", op, 50)
            assertEquals(
                condition,
                roundTrip(condition),
                "round-trip failed for CompareOp.$op",
            )
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare with negative value round-trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, -10),
            roundTrip(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, -10)),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare with spaces in variable name round-trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Compare("my stat", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            roundTrip(Condition.Compare("my stat", CompareOp.GT, 0)),
        )
    }

    // ---------- 2. Canonical string output (Ф3.2 will make these parse) ----------

    @Test
    fun `literal writes as true or false`() {
        assertEquals("true", written(Condition.Literal(true)))
        assertEquals("false", written(Condition.Literal(false)))
    }

    @Test
    fun `varRef writes as bare name`() {
        assertEquals("sword", written(Condition.VarRef("sword")))
    }

    @Test
    fun `in range writes with range syntax`() {
        assertEquals(
            "health in 0..100",
            written(Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100)),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `simple and writes without brackets`() {
        assertEquals(
            "has_a && has_b",
            written(Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b"))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `simple or writes without brackets`() {
        assertEquals(
            "has_a || has_b",
            written(Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b"))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `and inside or does not need brackets - and binds tighter`() {
        // Or(And(a, b), c) → "a && b || c" (no brackets: && has higher precedence)
        assertEquals(
            "has_a && has_b || has_c",
            written(
                Condition.Or(
                    Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                    Condition.Has("c"),
                ),
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `or inside and needs brackets`() {
        // And(a, Or(b, c)) → "a && (b || c)" (brackets required)
        assertEquals(
            "has_a && (has_b || has_c)",
            written(
                Condition.And(
                    Condition.Has("a"),
                    Condition.Or(Condition.Has("b"), Condition.Has("c")),
                ),
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `nested and is associative - no extra brackets`() {
        // And(And(a, b), c) → "a && b && c"
        assertEquals(
            "has_a && has_b && has_c",
            written(
                Condition.And(
                    Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                    Condition.Has("c"),
                ),
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `nested or is associative - no extra brackets`() {
        // Or(Or(a, b), c) → "a || b || c"
        assertEquals(
            "has_a || has_b || has_c",
            written(
                Condition.Or(
                    Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                    Condition.Has("c"),
                ),
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not has writes without brackets`() {
        assertEquals(
            "!has_sword",
            written(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("sword"))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not compare needs brackets`() {
        assertEquals(
            "!(health >= 50)",
            written(Condition.Not(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not and needs brackets`() {
        assertEquals(
            "!(has_a && has_b)",
            written(Condition.Not(Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not or needs brackets`() {
        assertEquals(
            "!(has_a || has_b)",
            written(Condition.Not(Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `complex precedence - mixed and or`() {
        // Or(And(a, b), And(c, d)) → "a && b || c && d"
        assertEquals(
            "has_a && has_b || has_c && has_d",
            written(
                Condition.Or(
                    Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                    Condition.And(Condition.Has("c"), Condition.Has("d")),
                ),
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `complex precedence - not on and inside or`() {
        // Or(Not(And(a, b)), c) → "!(a && b) || c"
        assertEquals(
            "!(has_a && has_b) || has_c",
            written(
                Condition.Or(
                    Condition.Not(
                        Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                    ),
                    Condition.Has("c"),
                ),
            ),
        )
    }

    // ---------- 3. Documented non-round-trip (Ф3.2 will flip these) ----------

    @Test
    fun `and round trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            roundTrip(Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b"))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `or round trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            roundTrip(Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b"))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `literal round trips`() {
        assertEquals(Condition.Literal(true), roundTrip(Condition.Literal(true)))
        assertEquals(Condition.Literal(false), roundTrip(Condition.Literal(false)))
    }

    @Test
    fun `varRef does not round trip - parser rejects - until F3_2`() {
        parseFails(Condition.VarRef("sword"))
    }

    @Test
    fun `in range round trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100),
            roundTrip(Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100)),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not compare round trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50)),
            roundTrip(Condition.Not(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50))),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `double not round trips`() {
        assertEquals(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("a"))),
            roundTrip(Condition.Not(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("a")))),
        )
    }

    // ---------- 4. Known corner case: names starting with `has_` ----------

    @Test
    fun `varRef name starting with has_ is ambiguous - parses as Has`() {
        // Documented in ConditionWriter KDoc: a name starting with
        // "has_" cannot be referenced from VarRef unambiguously. The
        // parser interprets "has_x" as Has("x"), not VarRef("has_x").
        // Not a bug in the writer — a naming collision in the author's
        // file. Ф3.2 will define the disambiguation rule (probably:
        // reserved prefix, rejected by TypeChecker).
        val condition = Condition.VarRef("has_x")
        val text = ConditionWriter.write(condition)
        assertEquals("has_x", text)
        val parsed = ConditionParser.parse(text)
        val success = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Condition>>(parsed)
        // Different AST:
        assertEquals(Condition.Has("x"), success.value)
        assertNotEquals(condition, success.value)
    }
}
